# Pete Apps — Development Changelog

This is the consolidated historical development changelog for every application in the Pete Apps suite (P Apps launcher and the apps it hosts) and for the shared JavaScript components (`pal-shared.js`, `pal-gcal.js`). It replaces the individual per-app `.md` changelogs as the single historical development record for the whole ecosystem.

**Conventions used in this file**

- Newest first within every section. Version numbers, dates and feature/issue IDs are exactly as recorded in the source changelogs; a date appears only where the source gave one.
- ⚠ marks a discrepancy, reused ID, gap, superseded item or ambiguity carried over from the source. These are preserved, not corrected.
- Changes to shared JavaScript that affected several apps are recorded once under **Shared Components**. App sections keep a one-line pointer at the relevant version, plus any app-specific detail.
- Backlog, planned, deferred and open items are kept in clearly labelled sections and are **not** completed work.
- "Tested / Not tested" notes are kept in short form because the source changelogs consistently separate verified behaviour from assumptions.

## Applications on hold

Four applications were taken out of the launcher at **P Apps Launcher v11.01 (PET-105, 2026-10-04)**. **Gigs & Trips was reinstated at v11.24 (PET-128)**, so three remain on hold. They are **on hold, not retired**: Pete is exploring other ways of working with them. Their files are unchanged and still in the repository, and no data was touched. Nothing here is a statement that they are finished or abandoned.

| Application | File | Last version | Last launcher version that carried it |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| PeteGCal | `PeteGCal.html` | v1.0 | v11.00 |
| Test & Issues | `test-issues.html` | v1.77 | v11.00 |
| Food System | `food-system-tracker.html` | Not established | v11.00 |

- While on hold: no launcher nav icon, home card, iframe, backup row or layout-panel entry for any of them. `pal-gcal.js` is kept as-is (unchanged at v3); Gigs & Trips, one of its two consumers, is active again from v11.24, PeteGCal is still on hold.
- **Reinstated: Gigs & Trips (launcher v11.24, PET-128)** — first nav icon, first home card, iframe, backup row and Download All, for Pete and Lex alike. See the v11.24 entry under P Apps Launcher.
- Backlogs for these apps stay where they are; nothing was moved or closed.
- To reinstate an app, restore from launcher v11.00 (the full removal list is in the v11.01 entry under P Apps Launcher) and record it as a new launcher version.
- ⚠ **Side effects to be aware of** (details in the v11.01 entry): HTML Vault is embedded inside Test & Issues, so its only launcher route is now its Standalone setting in Customize layout; Lex no longer has PeteGCal in her launcher (she has Gigs & Trips again from v11.24).

# Suite Programme

Programme-level history for the suite-wide consolidation programme (architecture, design and platform work that is not owned by a single application). Per-application and shared-library changes made *under* the programme are recorded in their normal sections and reference the programme work package (e.g. WP0.2c). Planned and deferred work is **not** recorded here; it lives in `SuiteImplementationPlan.md`.

Programme documents: `SuiteArchitecture.md` (agreed architecture, ownership, contracts, current-state inventory) · `SuiteImplementationPlan.md` (phases, dependencies, status, deferred register) · `SuiteReview.md` (findings, disposition, original review).

### Programme R0 — Phase 0, WP0.1 and WP0.9: programme established, documents created — 3 Nov 2026

- **What:** the suite-wide review of 3 Nov 2026 was agreed and a revised six-phase programme adopted (Phase 0 baseline and verification → Phase 6 platform optimisation) with ten architectural principles and six governance requirements (capabilities, contract governance, sync-correct restore, independent versioning, notification architecture, repeatable testing). Sequencing changes S1–S12 were accepted, including: restore designed in Phase 2 as a new sync write (not clearing a deletion flag); fonts self-hosted at the end of Phase 2; a Clean-up gate after Phase 2; one release per app per phase.
- **Decisions recorded:** D1 Pete and Lex do not share a device (user isolation downgraded); D3 Device check is Pete-only; D6 primary device iPhone 16 Pro Max, iOS 27.2, launcher installed as a home-screen app; D8 bounded storage-headroom probe approved on the real phone; D2 programme documents kept in the Claude Project with copies supplied for the repository; D4 shared-library bundle versioning starts at 1.0.0.
- **Created:** `SuiteArchitecture.md` (includes the application inventory baseline, WP0.1), `SuiteImplementationPlan.md`, `SuiteReview.md` (disposition register, amendments and the original review verbatim).
- **Corrects the original review:** the UTC-date defect in Reading Tracker affects projected finish dates and month/year period starts for the whole of British Summer Time, not only the first hour after midnight (see `SuiteReview.md` §2).
- **Not changed:** no application, launcher or shared-library file; no version number. No data, storage, sync or backup behaviour touched. Existing changelog entries untouched; this section is new.
- **Tested:** documents only. Inventory facts come from static reading of the supplied files; storage keys and table names were extracted by pattern and are primary, not exhaustive. **Not established:** `pal-gcal.js`, `manifest.json` (not supplied), the on-hold apps.
- **Next:** R1 — launcher v11.63 with `pal-diag.js` (Device check) and the backup-manifest version fix.

### Programme R1 — Phase 0, WP0.2: Device check and launcher version fix — 4 Nov 2026

- **What:** the launcher (v11.64) gains an on-demand, Pete-only **Device check** (new shared file `pal-diag.js`), and the backup manifest now records the real launcher version. Details are in the P Apps Launcher v11.64 entry and the `pal-diag.js` section.
- **Facts established from Pete's 4 Nov uploads (recorded; nothing acted on yet):**
  - The launcher was at v11.63 and Reading Tracker at v3.99 (still requesting `pal-shared.js?v=3.89`), so programme targets moved: R1 launcher is v11.64 (not v11.63) and the Reading date fix will be the next Reading version after v3.99.
  - `manifest.json` was supplied: name/short_name "Pete's Apps", `start_url` `/PeteAppLauncher/index.html`, `display` standalone, `orientation` `portrait-primary`, background/theme `#0d1117` (older than the launcher's `#0E0D12`), icons 192/512 with a combined `any maskable` purpose, no `id` or `scope`. The Device check reports these on the phone so they can be judged there; no change made.
  - **`pal-gcal.js` is no longer live** (Pete, 4 Nov). Gigs & Trips v7.112 still loads `pal-gcal.js?v=3` and calls `PalGCal.*` (63 references, guarded only by `typeof PalGCal.listInstances`, which throws if `PalGCal` is undeclared). Whether calendar sync is retired and a Gigs & Trips release is needed is an open question for Pete. Phase 5 Calendar delivery can no longer assume the existing layer.
- **Not changed:** Gigs & Trips, Reading Tracker, `pal-shared.js`, any other app; no data, storage, sync or backup-file format change.
- **Next:** baseline run, then R2 (`pal-shared.js` 1.0.0 with `PalShared.VERSION` and `localISO`, and the Reading date fix).

### Programme baseline B1 — Device check reports, launcher v11.64 verified — 4 Nov 2026

- **Verified live (M):** launcher v11.64 deployment check, 7 of 7 passed (Pete, iPhone home-screen app). Desktop Safari and iPhone reports received.
- **Findings recorded in `SuiteImplementationPlan.md`:** about 1.15 M characters of `localStorage` in use on both devices with at least 68% headroom (probe cap reached), so the headroom half of the storage gate passes; Gym is 40% of usage; the origin also holds keys from non-suite pages; iPhone language en-GB, desktop en-US; local and UTC dates agree in winter; no service workers.
- **Known defect (not yet fixed):** the Device check's contract "age" reads `updatedAt` but contracts use `built`, so it shows "-". Queued as `pal-diag.js` 1.0.1 with the next launcher release.
- **Not changed:** no application, launcher or library file in this entry.

### Programme correction and baseline B2 — 4 Nov 2026

- **Correction to the R1 entry above:** it records `pal-gcal.js` as "no longer live". That was a misreading. Pete confirmed calendar sync is **active** and supplied `pal-gcal.js` (v3). Gigs & Trips v7.112 needs no release for this, and Phase 5 Calendar delivery can build on the existing layer. The earlier text is left as history.
- **Baseline B2 (iPhone home-screen app, every visible app opened, Device check):** every loaded app requests `pal-shared.js` with its own version as the tag except **Reading** (app v3.99, tag `?v=3.89`); Claims and Horizon were not loaded. About 1.25 M characters of `localStorage` used, headroom at least 68%. Keys from retired apps (`ehub.db.v2`, `meal_planner_data`, `pt_companion_v1_*`, `fs_v1`, about 190 KB) remain in the origin; no other repository is served from it. Nothing deleted.
- **Not changed:** no application, launcher or library file.

### Programme baseline B3 — failed-write and date-format audits (static) — 4 Nov 2026

- **WP0.4 (static reading, A):** Horizon, Gigs & Trips and Film & TV report a refused main save; Reading and Fortnight swallow it silently; Gym, On Budget and Claim Tracker have no try/catch, so a refusal throws out of the handler with no message and skips the contract and launcher notifications. No app has a global error handler. Storage gate S10 second half is therefore **triggered**; a small shared failed-write handler is proposed as the first item of Phase 1 (WP1.4). Not run: runtime fault injection.
- **WP0.10 (static, A):** about 25 date helpers across 11 files, mostly month-name formats via `en-GB`; Reading's `ukNumeric` is the only numeric dd/mm/yyyy helper; about 40 date inputs. Basis for D10 (UK date standard).
- **Not changed:** no application, launcher or library file.

### Programme R2 — Phase 0, WP0.2b and WP0.2c (Reading): library identity and the first date fix — 4 Nov 2026

- **Released:** `pal-shared.js` bundle 1.0.0 (`PalShared.VERSION`, `localISO`) and Reading Tracker v3.100 (BST date fix; library tag brought up to date). Details in their own sections.
- **Remaining WP0.2c:** Horizon (`todayISO()`, R3, v5.2) and Gym (default programme name, R4, v2.137). Both only err in the first hour after local midnight during BST, so they are lower urgency than Reading.
- **Not changed:** launcher, other apps, any stored data.

### Programme R3 and R4 — Phase 0, WP0.2c complete: Horizon v5.2 and Gym v2.137 — 4 Nov 2026

- **Released together** (one deployment check, two separate application versions): Horizon v5.2 and Gym Tracker v2.137. Both replace a UTC-date "today" with the local date (`todayISO()`); both only differed in the first hour after local midnight during British Summer Time.
- **WP0.2c status:** Reading (v3.100, verified), Horizon, Gym: fixed. A search of the other supplied files found four remaining `toISOString()` date uses and none is a defect: Gigs & Trips uses it twice for a once-a-day warning throttle and a storage-limit timestamp (a UTC day is acceptable there); Film & TV `addDaysISO` builds its date at local noon, which stays on the right day; Fantasy uses it only as a fallback when `todayISO` is missing. On Budget, Fortnight, Claims, Vault and the launcher have none.
- **Not changed:** the launcher and all other apps.

### Programme note — Horizon v5.2 / Gym v2.137 deployment check, and v11.65 — 4 Nov 2026

- Deployment check of Horizon v5.2 and Gym v2.137: 5 of 6 passed (version checks, both apps working, Horizon dates). T6 (library tags in the Device check) could not be shown for Horizon because the Device check could not see nested apps; that was a gap in the check, fixed in launcher v11.65, not an app defect. Horizon's v5.2 badge (T2) shows the new file loaded; its library tag is re-checked in the v11.65 deployment check.
- Horizon, Claims and Vault live inside other apps; the earlier Baseline B2 note that Claims and Horizon were "hidden" and "not loaded" is explained by this.

### Programme baseline B4 — no library version skew — 4 Nov 2026

- **Evidence (M, Device check on desktop Safari, launcher v11.65, every app opened):** every app requests `pal-shared.js` with a tag equal to its own version (Gigs 7.112, Fortnight 3.86, On Budget 3.117, Reading 3.100, Claims 2.26, Gym 2.137, Vault 1.10, Horizon 5.2 in both its launcher frame and its On Budget copy, Fantasy 1.66, Film 4.6) and `PalSync` is present in all. Reading's earlier lag (`?v=3.89`) is resolved.
- **Remaining Phase 0 work:** user-isolation determination, backup and sync verification, RLS evidence, test baselines, exit review.
- **Not changed:** no application, launcher or library file.

### Programme baselines B5 to B7 — backup, RLS and sync evidence, D10 scope — 4 Nov 2026

- **B5 backup export (launcher v11.65, desktop):** all 10 apps exported with status ok; every file parses and matches the manifest on size and record counts. Restore (import) not tested.
- **B6 Supabase RLS (Pete's read-only queries):** row-level security on for all 49 public tables; per-user and Pete/Lex-only policies as designed. Findings: `anon` and `authenticated` hold TRUNCATE, TRIGGER and REFERENCES on all tables (Supabase default; hardening candidate), `ff_api_cache` has no policy (probably Edge Function only), and the tables for retired or on-hold apps remain. - **Handshakes not moved (recommendation):** the four quick-add handshakes (Claims `CT_`, On Budget `OB_`, Gym `GYM_`, Reading `RT_`) were NOT moved onto `bridgeCall`. They write data and each carries safeguards (the same request id re-sent until answered, with the app replaying the stored result so a retry never saves twice; Reading and Claims verified live). `bridgeCall` sends once and gives up on a timeout, so a straight swap could lose or double-log an entry for no user benefit. Proposed instead: keep them, and give `bridgeCall` safe-retry (resend with the same id, app-side replay) before any move; new actions (not these four) use `bridgeCall` from now on. Decision for Pete.

Claims contract carries categories, 5 standard trips and ext; launcher reads them; fallback reads the saved copy when ext is missing. All 12 pages load with no errors. **Not tested:** a real quick-add end to end from the launcher, a real iPhone, a second device, Claims with your real data.

### Programme R14 — Phase 2, Batch A: contract groundwork and cloud contracts — 5 Nov 2026

- **Why:** the launcher's cards still depended on an app having been opened on that device (the old readers, plus the contracts the apps wrote into local storage). Pete asked for the contracts to be written to Supabase and pulled by the launcher so that "which device" and "which app was opened" no longer matter (D13 addition, 5 Nov).
- **Library (`pal-shared.js` 1.5.0, additive, nothing existing changed):** `PalContract.publish()` also accepts `app`, `schema` and `caps` (a few named true/false capabilities) and stamps `lib`; it now sends the contract to a new Supabase table `pal_contracts` (record key = app id; the search list is never sent). Sends wait 4 s after the last save, an unchanged contract is not re-sent for 10 minutes, and a send is flushed when the page is hidden. If the table does not exist the cloud copy switches itself off for that session without any error and the local contract is unaffected. New `PalContract.pullCloud()` reads the rows and applies a cloud contract only if it is newer than the local one, belongs to the signed-in user, is contract v1 with an app id equal to its key, is an app the launcher knows, and is 48 KB or less. New `PalContract.cloudStatus()`. New opt-in `PalBridge` (launcher-to-app request / reply protocol, same origin only); no app uses it yet and the existing OB / GYM / RT / CT handshakes are untouched.
- **Launcher (v11.67):** pulls cloud contracts 2.5 s after sign-in, when the page becomes visible again (at most once a minute) and redraws Today / Timeline / Needs attention if anything was applied; adds a `bridgeCall()` helper (unused so far); the library tag is now `pal-shared.js?v=11.67` (it was a stale `?v=11.38`, so an old cached library could have lacked the new functions); the backup-file check shows the file's date as dd/mm/yy (it used a locale date string).
- **Device check (`pal-diag.js` 1.2.0):** contract lines show app / schema / library / capabilities and an ISSUE note (version not 1, app id mismatch, no user, bad build time, older than 7 days, over 48 KB); new "Cloud contracts" section (last pull, last push, local contracts against cloud rows, a hint if the table is missing).
- **Database (run by Pete in Supabase):** `pal_contracts` table, row level security on, one policy set per user, no access for the `anon` role. Rollback: `drop table public.pal_contracts`. The code works whether or not it has been created.
- **Reaches the apps:** each app loads the library by its own version tag, so the new library reaches an app at its next release or when its cached copy expires. Until an app runs 1.5.0 it keeps writing local contracts only, exactly as before; the launcher still reads those.
- **Known limitation:** `built` is the writing device's clock, so a clock that is several minutes out can make an older copy look newer. The 10-minute unchanged limit and the "newer wins" rule bound the effect to the dashboard card.
- **Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, Supabase REST stubbed, label S for the server and A for the code):** 31 checks. Publish adds app / schema / lib / caps and keeps the v1 shape; nothing sent before 4 s; the cloud row has no search list; identical re-publish is not re-sent; a change updates the same row; a burst of 5 saves sends once; `clearAll` cancels a waiting send; a missing table disables the push after one 404 and `pullCloud` reports it without throwing while local contracts still write; pull applies a new app and a newer cloud copy, keeps a newer local one and rejects another user's, an app id mismatch, an unknown app, a bad build time, contract v2, an oversize copy and a bad key; in the real launcher the pull after sign-in writes `pal_x_gigs` and redraws, and the Device check shows 1.2.0, the contract meta and the Cloud contracts section; `bridgeCall` returned a result, an app error, an unknown-action error, TIMEOUT, NOT_READY and NO_FRAME; title and `LAUNCHER_VERSION` agree; the backup-file check shows 04/11/26 09:05. Regression: all 11 pages load with 0 errors on 1.5.0; the failed-save and normal-save checks in On Budget, Claim, Gym, Reading and Fortnight give the same results as before. **Not tested:** the live Supabase table and its row level security, two real devices, iPhone Safari (all covered by the deployment check).

### Programme R13 — Phase 1, WP1.6 part 2: `pal-fpl-proxy` v1.5 written, NOT deployed (accepted risk) — 5 Nov 2026

- **Outcome (Pete, 5 Nov):** closed as an accepted risk. v1.5 was written and tested offline but deliberately not deployed: the function only serves public Fantasy Premier League data and writes to its own cache table, it cannot reach any of Pete's data, and a hand-edit of a live function was judged to carry more risk than the benefit. The deployed function stays at v1.4 with Verify JWT off. The file is kept for later (deploy notes below). No deployment check is outstanding.
- **Source:** Pete supplied the deployed function (v1.4). It is Supabase infrastructure, not an app file, so no app version, `pal-shared.js` or launcher change; the function keeps its own version (v1.4 to v1.5), recorded in its header comment.
- **Finding:** the function is guarded only by the shared header `x-pal-key`, whose value is readable in the public `pal-shared.js`; Verify JWT is off. Its routes return public Fantasy Premier League data, and it writes to `ff_api_cache` with the service-role key. The weakness is therefore abuse, not data exposure: a caller who has seen the app source could (a) send any string as an id, which reached the upstream URL and became a cache row key, filling `ff_api_cache` with junk, and (b) use the function as a free FPL proxy.
- **Decision (recommended, accepted pending Pete's deploy):** do NOT enforce a Supabase login. The session token that apps hold comes from the launcher and expires (the apps' own error text says to reopen via the launcher to refresh it), so enforcing it would make Fantasy fail part-way through a session to protect public data. Verify JWT would also accept the public anon key, so turning it on alone adds nothing.
- **Change (v1.5, function only, app untouched):** every path id must be digits only and in range (entry id 1 to 99,999,999; player id 1 to 2000; gameweek 1 to 38), else 400. New optional secret `PAL_ALLOWED_ENTRY_IDS` (comma-separated entry ids): when set, entry routes serve only those managers (else 403); when unset, behaviour is unchanged. Checks run before the cache or FPL are touched. CORS, the key check, caching, retries and the stale fallback are unchanged.
- **Tested (Stage 1, label A):** the route check logic was run in Node against 21 cases, including every route shape the Fantasy app uses (bootstrap, fixtures, entry, picks, transfers, element-summary), bad ids (letters, decimals, encoded dots, zero, out of range, gameweek 0 and 39), allow-list on and off, and a leading-zero entry id. **Not tested:** the deployed function (no Deno or Supabase access here); Fantasy against the live function (covered by the deployment check).
- **Residual risk (accepted):** the shared key remains public, so anyone who has seen the app can still call the allowed routes. With the id checks and the allow-list the worst case is reading public FPL data for the allowed manager and the cached bootstrap, fixtures and player routes, and normal request volume. Rollback: redeploy v1.4.

### Programme R12 — Phase 1, WP1.1 version governance and WP1.6 part 1 database hardening — 4 Nov 2026

- **WP1.6 part 1 (database, run by Pete in Supabase, no file change):** `TRUNCATE`, `TRIGGER` and `REFERENCES` were revoked from `anon` and `authenticated` on all 49 public tables, and the default privileges were altered so new tables do not get them back. Before: 6 privilege rows x 49 tables. After: only `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE` remain, for both roles, on all 49 tables; row level security was already on for all 49. Effect: a leaked public key could previously have emptied a table with one `TRUNCATE`; it can not now. Rollback: `GRANT TRUNCATE, TRIGGER, REFERENCES ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO anon, authenticated;`. The apps never use these three privileges. Pete's post-change sync check is recorded when reported. **Not done (WP1.6 part 2):** `pal-fpl-proxy` still has Verify JWT off, guarded by the key in `pal-shared.js`; needs the function source.
- **WP1.1 (version governance):** the apps already tag `pal-shared.js` with their own version, and the Device check already listed each frame's title and tag, but nothing said whether they agreed or whether frames ran different library builds. Added: Device check `pal-diag.js` 1.1.0 prints each frame's loaded `PalShared.VERSION` and a new "Version check" section with a one-line RESULT, a MISMATCH line where the title version differs from the tag, and a LIBRARY SKEW line where frames run different `PalShared` builds. Launcher v11.66 adds two fields per app to the backup manifest, `appVersion` (from the frame's page title) and `library` (the frame's `PalShared.VERSION`). The existing manifest `version` field is unchanged (it still mixes the file's own version and schema value) so nothing that reads it changes.
- **Limits:** Reading and Horizon do not carry a version in their page title, so their title check is skipped and their `appVersion` is blank (their tag is still shown). Frames not yet opened are not checked.
- **Versions:** Launcher v11.66, `pal-diag.js` 1.1.0. No app, `pal-shared.js`, storage, sync or schema change.
- **Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, label A):** all 10 app frames loaded in the real launcher; Version check reports RESULT: OK, all on PalShared 1.4.0; a forced wrong tag (Gym ?v=2.100) is reported as MISMATCH and a forced older library (Vault 1.3.0) as LIBRARY SKEW with RESULT 2 issues; the manifest rows carry `appVersion` and `library` and the old `version` unchanged; title, badge, menu line and `LAUNCHER_VERSION` all v11.66; no probe key left; no page errors. **Not tested:** the real iPhone and the downloaded manifest file (covered by the deployment check).

### Programme R9 — Phase 1, Batch 1 fix: calendar button reworked — 4 Nov 2026

- **Deployment check R8.1 (4 Nov):** 3 of 6 passed (T1, T4, T6). **Failed:** R8.1-T2 (iPhone: no calendar opens), R8.1-T3 (desktop Gym: icon present, click does nothing), R8.1-T5 (On Budget: icon does not launch a calendar). Reading T5 also noted that the target date was hard to find: Reading's target-date boxes are only shown when the tracker is in "Target finish date" mode (Settings tracking mode, the New Tracker form, and the collection form); that behaviour is unchanged.
- **Cause:** R7/R8 opened the picker from script on a hidden helper input (`showPicker()` / `click()`). Browsers, iOS Safari in particular, refuse to open a native picker for an element the user did not directly touch, so the tap did nothing. The `!important` and keyboard fixes in R8 were correct but did not address this. This approach is abandoned.
- **Fix (`pal-shared.js` 1.4.0):** a real transparent native `<input type="date">` is laid over the icon (42 px wide, the height of the box, `z-index` 5), inserted as the next sibling of the text box, so the tap lands on a genuine date control and the device opens its own picker. Desktop also calls `showPicker()` from that click (skipped on iOS, where the tap opens it natively). The overlay is placed from the box's real rectangle and re-checked on resize, scroll, touchstart, focus and every 150 ms; it hides when the box is hidden or disabled and is removed when the box leaves the page. On change the chosen day is written into the box as dd/mm/yy and the box's `input` and `change` events fire. The value contract (ISO), typing and storage are unchanged.
- **Versions:** pal-shared 1.4.0; On Budget v3.122, Claim Tracker v2.31, Gym Tracker v2.142, Reading Tracker v3.105, Fortnight Tracker v3.91. Launcher unchanged.
- **Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, en-US, desktop and touch emulation):** in all five apps the overlay count matches the date boxes; at the icon position the top element is the overlay and a real tap or click lands on it; a desktop click calls `showPicker`; after the box is moved by a layout change the overlay follows; choosing a date writes dd/mm/yy and ISO `.value`; typing tests, seeded save and failed-write tests and the 11-page load all unchanged; syntax passes. **Not tested (cannot be, headless):** that the native picker actually opens on iPhone Safari and desktop browsers.

- **Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, en-US locale):** in all five apps a click on the text area opens nothing; a click on the icon opens the helper; choosing 2027-03-09 gives 09/03/27 in the box, 2027-03-09 as `.value`, `input` then `change` events, and the helper removed; typing and invalid-date behaviour unchanged; 11 of 11 pages load with no errors; seeded save and failed-write tests unchanged; script syntax passes. **Not tested:** whether the iPhone Safari picker actually opens from the icon (headless cannot open the native picker), the picker's own date labels on iOS, dark-mode look of the icon.

### Programme R6 — Phase 1, Batch 1 fix: date inputs show dd/mm/yy — 4 Nov 2026

- **Deployment check R5.1 (4 Nov):** 9 of 11 passed (T1, T3, T4, T6–T11). **Failed:** R5.1-T2 (Claim "add transaction" and edit-view date pickers show 11/04/2026 for 4 Nov; the card text is correct) and R5.1-T5 (Gym shows only a date picker in the wrong format).
- **Cause:** the pickers are native `type="date"` inputs. Their display order follows the device region, not the page. The pages were already `lang="en-GB"`, so the page cannot force UK order. Batch 1 changed displayed text only and left these inputs alone, which was the gap against D10 ("dd/mm/yy … also on inputs").
- **Fix (shared, additive):** `pal-shared.js` 1.2.0 adds `PalShared.ukDateInputs()`. It turns each `input[type=date]` into a dd/mm/yy text box (numeric keypad, placeholder dd/mm/yy, typing 271126 gives 27/11/26, 4.11.2026 is tidied to 04/11/26 on leaving the field, a red outline and tooltip on an invalid date). The element keeps its id, and its `.value` still reads and writes ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` (empty while the text is incomplete or invalid), so no app logic, stored data, backup or sync format changes. Inputs added later (modals, edit views) are picked up by a MutationObserver. Each of the five apps calls it once right after the library tag.
- **Trade-off:** the native calendar popup is gone for these fields; dates are typed. A calendar button could be added later if wanted.
- **Versions:** pal-shared bundle 1.2.0; On Budget v3.119, Claim Tracker v2.28, Gym Tracker v2.139, Reading Tracker v3.102, Fortnight Tracker v3.88 (version bump, library tag and the call only). Launcher unchanged.
- **Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium with an en-US locale, the failing case):** in all five apps every date input is converted (Claim 3, Gym 5, Reading 4, Fortnight 4, On Budget 5 at load), none left native; an input added later is converted; initial and set ISO values show as dd/mm/yy and read back as ISO; clearing works; typing 271126 gives 27/11/26 and 2026-11-27; 31/02/26 reads as empty with the red outline; 4.11.2026 tidies to 04/11/26. No page errors; all 11 pages load at the right versions; per-app seeded save and failed-write tests unchanged (bar shown, no throw, no bar on a normal save); script syntax passes. **Not tested:** iPhone Safari typing and keypad, a modal opened through the real UI in each app, saving a record entered through the new field.

# Shared Components

## `pal-shared.js`

Combined bundle of `pal-config.js` + `pal-sync.js` + `pal-utils.js`, concatenated in that load-order-critical order (config sets `window.PAL_CONFIG` before sync and utils reference it). Each section is byte-identical to its original standalone file. Loaded as `<script src="pal-shared.js?v=X.X">`. Rows handled by the sync section are shaped `{ user_id, record_key, data, updated_at }`; the library never touches an app's own localStorage or data model.

- **Why:** baseline B3 / B9 found that On Budget, Claim Tracker and Gym threw on a refused save with no message and Reading, Fortnight (and others) swallowed it; decision D10 asks for dd/mm/yy dates with one shared formatter and parser.
- **Change (section 5, additive; nothing above it changed):** `safeSet(key, value, label)` (localStorage write that never throws; on failure shows a red bar once per 30 s and records `PalShared.lastWriteFailure` / `writeFailures`), `writeFailure(label, err)`, `fmtDate(v)` (dd/mm/yy from ISO, timestamp or Date, local time), `fmtDateTime(v)` (dd/mm/yy hh:mm), `parseDate(str)` (d/m/yy, d/m/yyyy with / . - or space separators, or ISO, to ISO; two-digit year means 20yy; invalid dates return an empty string). `VERSION` is `'1.1.0'`; `localISO` is unchanged.

All other apps keep their current tag and keep working on whichever copy they have cached; none of them calls the new functions yet.
- **Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium):** `fmtDate` for ordinary, leap-day and invalid inputs and for a BST timestamp (2026-07-01T23:30Z shows 02/07/26); a 4,000-day format-then-parse round trip with no mismatch; `parseDate` accepted and rejected cases; `safeSet` returning false twice under a forced quota error with one bar shown and two failures counted, and returning true normally. **Not tested:** Safari, a real quota failure.

### PalShared bundle 1.0.0 — section 5 added: bundle version and `localISO()` — 4 Nov 2026 (Suite WP0.2b)

- **Why:** the file had per-section versions but no version of its own, so nothing (including the Device check) could say which copy an app had loaded; and there was no safe helper for "local date as `YYYY-MM-DD`" (the cause of the Reading BST defect, v3.100).

Nothing above it was changed; `todayISO()` already returned the local date and is untouched.

Every other app keeps its own tag (`?v=<its version>`) and therefore keeps the previous copy until it is next released; that is safe because the change is additive, and the Device check shows which copy each app has loaded. The launcher still requests `?v=11.38`.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium): `localISO` for BST midnight and 23:59, both daylight-saving change days, winter, an invalid Date and the default; `todayISO()` agrees; PalSync, PalContract and PAL_CONFIG still present; the real launcher (v11.64) runs against the new file with no errors. The only line removed from the file is the first header comment line (reworded to name the bundle version).

### pal-contract v1.1 — optional `until` on attention items — 3 Nov 2026

- **Why:** an alert an app computes when it saves outlives its situation until the app is next opened (found in the launcher feeds review: Fortnight's "Hours target at risk" stayed on after its fortnight ended).
- **Change (section 4 only, three lines of code and comments):** `attention` items may carry `until`, a `YYYY-MM-DD` string kept to 10 characters like `due`; the launcher hides the alert from the day after it (launcher v11.60). Not accepted on `upcoming`. The payload version stays `v:1`; an app that does not send `until` behaves exactly as before, and an app running an older copy of the file simply has the field dropped by the existing field list.
- **Affected apps / pickup:** none changed by the file alone. Fortnight Tracker v3.86 is the first to send it (it loads the file as `?v=3.86`, so it picks up the new copy). Every other app keeps its older cached copy until its own version tag next changes, and does not use the field.
- Tested (Stage 1, real file in headless Chromium): `until` stored on attention items, absent when not sent, an over-long value clipped (and therefore not a valid date), not stored on upcoming items, payload version 1; the earlier launcher suites (284 checks in all) pass against the new file. Not tested: every other app loading the new file (they do not change until their next release).

### pal-contract v1 — new section 4 of `pal-shared.js` — 2 Nov 2026

- `window.PalContract` (`publish`, `read`, `clearAll`): an optional, read-only summary an app publishes for the launcher under `pal_x_<appId>`: `{ v:1, appId, userId, built, summary, upcoming[≤30], attention[≤10], search[≤400, reserved] }`; `open = { view?, id? }` is turned into a `PAL_OPEN` message by the launcher. It is a derived cache: nothing reads it back into an app, deleting it loses nothing.
- Safety: `publish()` never throws and does nothing without a user id; strings and lists are capped; 48 KB per key ceiling (search list trimmed first); written through `PalSync.cacheSet`. The launcher ignores a contract whose `userId` is not the signed-in user and clears every `pal_x_*` key on sign-out.
- Existing sections (pal-config v1.2, pal-sync v1.13, utils) are unchanged except the file header and "SECTION n of 4" comments (diffed: 10 comment lines). Pickup: an app gets section 4 when its own `?v=` tag next changes; apps that do not call it are unaffected.
- First consumers: Claim Tracker v2.22, On Budget v3.115, Gigs & Trips v7.110; launcher v11.35 reads it.

### Header notes moved out of the code — comment-only slimming (18 Oct 2026)

- **Why:** `pal-shared.js` was 57 KB, of which about 38 KB were comments, most of it the long per-version header notes for pal-config and pal-sync. Every app downloads and parses this file on first open (and again when an app's `?v=` tag changes), so the history was being paid for on every cold launch while the same history already lives in this changelog.
- **Change:** the file header, the pal-config header and the pal-sync header (v1.0 – v1.13 notes) were replaced with short pointer comments. The original text is preserved **verbatim** in "Archived headers" at the end of this section. Inline explanatory comments next to the code were left in place. 57,709 → 39,040 bytes (gzip ≈ 19.7 KB → 13.5 KB).
- **Code unchanged — proven:** the old and new files, minified with comments removed (terser, no compress/mangle), are identical (12,322 characters). `PalSync`, `PAL_CONFIG` and the utils expose exactly the same keys in both. No version number inside the file changed (pal-config v1.2, pal-sync v1.13).
- **Affected apps / pickup:** each app loads it as `pal-shared.js?v=<own version>`, so an app receives the slimmed copy the next time its own version tag changes. Launcher (`?v=11.23`) and Gym Tracker (`?v=2.116`) pick it up in this release; all other apps keep running the identical-code previous copy until they are next released. No behaviour differs either way.
- **Not done (changed from the original Phase 2 plan, on evidence):** (a) asking the parent for a session from `initSession()` — the v11.22 timeline shows the launcher's push already arrives within ~3 ms of the app's load, so it would add a message and a second session event for no measurable gain; (b) a single shared `?v=` for every app — it would force a simultaneous release of all nine apps for each future shared change, and the file is now 13.5 KB gzipped. Both can be revisited if a slow-open capture points at them.
- Tested (Stage 1): see the v11.23 and Gym v2.116 entries (all nine app pages load with the slimmed file, no page errors). Not tested: Safari / phone.

- The three separate `<script>` tags (`pal-config.js`, `pal-sync.js`, `pal-utils.js`) were replaced with one `pal-shared.js` tag. No code inside any section changed; the purpose was fewer requests.

### `PalSync.trimIfLarge(key, maxKB)` — TI-086

**Introduced in Test & Issues v1.75**

- New shared function, purely additive, added to the public return block. Deletes a localStorage key once it exceeds `maxKB`, so the app's existing pull from Supabase repopulates it fresh. Size measured as UTF-16 bytes (`(key.length + raw.length) * 2`).
- Safety rule: skips entirely if `PalSync.retryQueueLength() > 0` (writes still pending). Returns a result object (`{ trimmed, reason, sizeKB, ... }`) rather than logging, so each app reports it in its own way.
- Must be called only after a completed pull with a live session. Never call it in `onNoSession` (no cloud copy to restore from, so trimming would be real data loss).
- Explicitly **not** valid for Gigs & Trips: its bespoke sync layer never routes through `PalSync.table()`, so `retryQueueLength()` says nothing about its pending writes.
- Reason: a Safari storage-quota error found in Gigs & Trips was traced to shared per-origin storage pressure across the suite; `ti_v1` was the largest single contributor at ~2 MB.
- Framed in the source as a drift/staleness guard, not a permanent size reduction: normal save-on-edit rewrites the full dataset afterwards.
- Tested: all four branches (missing key; under threshold; over threshold with no pending writes → trims; over threshold with pending writes → does not trim) once in Node for TI-086; not re-tested per app.
- Affected applications (adopted):
  - Test & Issues v1.75 (TI-086): 500 KB, `onSession` made async, called after `syncPull()`.
  - Film & TV Tracker v2.7 (FTT-039): 2048 KB, deliberately above the real ~1.2 MB library; safety net only. ⚠ Superseded: the real library is ~2.5 MB; the call was removed in v3.0 (FTT-041) because it deleted the local copy after every pull.
  - Fortnight Tracker v3.73 (FT-065, 3 Oct 2026): 500 KB, called inside the `pullFromCloud()` success callback.
  - ⚠ FT-065 says the mechanism was rolled out "across the suite this round … and several others"; the other apps are not named in the supplied material.
- Follow-up: Test & Issues v1.76 (TI-087) found the trim never fired in the reported quota case.
- Further follow-up: Test & Issues v1.77 (TI-089) stops caching its ~2 MB locally at all; see `PalSync.cacheSet()` below. The `trimIfLarge('ti_v1', 500)` call is left in place and is now effectively inert for that key.

### `PalSync.cacheSet(key, value, opts)` and `PalSync.storageUsage()` — TI-089

**pal-sync section v1.13. Introduced in Test & Issues v1.77.** Purely additive: two new members on the public object, no existing function changed, so any app that does not call them behaves exactly as before.

- `storageUsage()` — read-only scan of the origin: `{ totalKB, keys: [{ key, kb }] }`, largest first, same `(key + value) * 2` UTF-16 basis as `trimIfLarge`. Returns `null` if localStorage is unavailable.
- `cacheSet(key, value, { maxKB, cloudSafe })` — quota-safe write for a key that is only a cache of Supabase. Never throws. Returns `{ stored, mode, kb, ... }`:
  - `mode: 'cloud-only'` — value is over `maxKB`, the caller asserts `cloudSafe` (nothing unsynced), there is a live session and `retryQueueLength() === 0`: nothing is written and a stale copy of the key is removed (`freedKB` reported).
  - `mode: 'local'` — written.
  - `mode: 'failed'` — the browser refused; `quota: true` when the reason was space.
  - In every case where any of the four conditions does not hold, it writes rather than skips.
- The library cannot see an app's own failed pushes, so `cloudSafe` is the caller's claim. Not valid for Gigs & Trips (bespoke sync; `retryQueueLength()` says nothing about its pending writes) — same rule as `trimIfLarge`.
- Adopted by: Test & Issues v1.77 (300 KB cap). Available to every other app; none has adopted it yet.
- Cache-busting: Test & Issues loads `pal-shared.js?v=1.77`. The launcher still loads `?v=10.87` (it does not use the new functions) and other apps keep their existing query strings, so they keep running the previous copy until they next bump it — safe because the change is additive.
- Tested: see Test & Issues v1.77 (unit checks of every `cacheSet` branch and `storageUsage`, plus `trimIfLarge` regression). Not tested in a real browser.

### pal-sync section — version history

Recorded in the pal-sync section header of `pal-shared.js` (no dates given). App cross-references are listed only where an app changelog records them.

- **v1.13 — storage helpers (TI-089).** `storageUsage()` and `cacheSet()`; additive, see the section above. Affected: Test & Issues v1.77.
- **v1.12 — opt-in shared mode.** `table(name, { shared: true })` and `fetchTableRows(name, { shared: true })`. Shared fetch drops the `user_id` filter (RLS is the boundary), orders by `record_key` then `user_id`, and collapses duplicate `record_key`s to the newest `updated_at`. Shared upsert PATCHes by `record_key` alone and omits `user_id` from the PATCH body (no forked copy, no ownership change); POST of a new record still stamps the caller's `user_id`. The flag is carried in the retry queue. Compaction stays per-user. Callers without the flag behave byte-for-byte as before.
  - Affected: Film & TV Tracker v1.8 (FTT-013) — `pal_film_tracker` titles, services and settings. Must be deployed together with the app.
- **v1.11 — tombstones no longer forgotten after one pull.** `pull()` no longer strips every `_deleted:true` record from `merged`; only deletes the cloud has confirmed leave the working set. An unconfirmed local tombstone whose id already exists in cloud is re-pushed on every pull (`retriedDeleteCount`). Root cause traced via On Budget ON--049 / ON--050 (resurrection of deleted records).
  - Consequence: `merged` can now contain `_deleted:true` records, so every app must filter `!record._deleted` at render/calc time.
  - Audit recorded in the header: Reading Tracker and Test & Issues needed filtering added; Fortnight Tracker had it for codes but not bundles; On Budget, Gym Tracker and Claim Tracker already compliant. Fortnight Tracker's follow-up is v3.33 (FT-030).
- **v1.10 — tombstone compaction**, the suite's only sanctioned hard `DELETE`: `countCompactableTombstones(table, days)` and `compactTombstones(table, days)`. Targets rows that are both tombstoned (`data->>_deleted = true`) and older than the threshold (default 90 days, clamped to a 30-day minimum). Not automatic; apps show a count-then-confirm button. Gigs & Trips and Meal Planner (bespoke shared sync) out of scope.
- **v1.9 — pagination and persisted retry queue.** `fetchTableRows()` requests 1,000-row pages with a `Range` header, ordered by `record_key`, `Prefer: count=exact`, looping until the `Content-Range` total is reached, and fails loudly if pagination stalls. The 401 retry queue is mirrored to localStorage key `pal_retry_queue_v1` and rehydrated at load; entries are `{ tableName, prefix, id, data }`. Because the origin is shared, any app with a live session can flush any app's stranded writes.
- **v1.8 — 401 retry queue and shared error hints.** `table().upsert()` queues a write that fails with 401 and still re-throws; the queue flushes automatically on the next session arrival. New `flushRetryQueue()`, `retryQueueLength()`, `errorHint(status, message)` (lifted from Gym Tracker's local `syncErrorHint()`).
  - On Budget v3.19 (ON--031) wired `onRetryFlushed` and shows "N pending sync".
  - Gym Tracker v2.52 (GYM-048) removed its own `syncErrorHint()` wrapper (added in v2.29).
- **v1.7** — `tombstone()` takes an optional `updatedAtField` (camelCase apps had been building tombstones by hand).
- **v1.6** — `PalSync.setSession(token, userId)` for sessions obtained outside the `PAL_SESSION` postMessage flow (Reading Tracker and Gigs & Trips standalone logins cited). Launcher v10.96 (PET-101) uses it via `feedPalSyncSession()`.
- **v1.5** — thrown errors carry `.status`.
- **v1.4** — local-only records are pushed exactly as they are, including `_deleted:true` ones (offline deletes reach the cloud). On Budget v3.16 migrated against "pal-sync.js (now v1.4)".
- **v1.3** — optional `preFetchedRows` (4th arg to `pull()`), new `fetchTableRows(tableName)`, and the tie-break changed to cloud-wins (`>=`). Used by On Budget v3.16 (seven record kinds, one fetch) and Fortnight Tracker v3.17 (preFetchedRows pattern from Test & Issues).
- **v1.2** — `pull()` takes `updatedAtField` (Test & Issues uses camelCase `updatedAt`; previously every comparison silently evaluated false).
- **v1.1** — optional `prefix` per `table()` instance (several record kinds in one table).
- **v1.0** — extracted from Claim Tracker's sync layer as the one canonical pattern.

**Known library property recorded by several apps:** `table().pull()` only pushes records whose id is missing from cloud (or unconfirmed tombstones). It does not push an edit to a record that already exists in cloud. Horizon v1.16 and Reading Tracker v3.30 (MR-016) each worked around this with explicit direct upserts.

**App migrations onto pal-sync recorded in app changelogs:** Fortnight Tracker v3.9 (FT-003); On Budget v3.16; Horizon v1.16; Film & TV Tracker v1.0 (built on it). Gigs & Trips is deliberately not on PalSync (bespoke sync; GIG-055 "closed: leave as-is").

```text
 * pal-config.js
 * ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Single source of truth for app configuration.
 * This is the ONLY file containing the Supabase credentials.
 * All app HTML files load this first and read from PAL_CONFIG.
 *
 * Loaded via <script src="pal-config.js"></script> in each HTML file.
 *
 * v1.1 (FF-002 follow-up): added FF_PROXY_KEY — the shared header
 * value fantasy-football-tracker.html sends to pal-fpl-proxy, matching
 * the PAL_PROXY_KEY secret set on that Edge Function (see its own
 * header comment for the `supabase secrets set` command). Lives here
 * rather than hardcoded in fantasy-football-tracker.html specifically
 * so it survives every future release of that app unchanged — this
 * file is edited once and is never part of a per-app release diff,
 * unlike the app HTML files which get regenerated wholesale each time.
 * v1.2 (FTT-001): added TMDB_API_KEY / TMDB_READ_TOKEN for
 * film-tv-tracker.html's search and metadata/availability enrichment.
 * Same reasoning as FF_PROXY_KEY above — a personal, non-commercial
 * TMDB key, safe to use client-side (read-only public metadata API,
 * same risk posture as the Supabase anon key above), kept here once
 * rather than hardcoded per-release into the app file. Only
 * TMDB_READ_TOKEN (the v4 Bearer token) is actually used by the app;
 * TMDB_API_KEY (the v3 key) is stored alongside it for reference/
 * future use only, since TMDB issues both from one account.
 * ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 */

=== pal-sync header (lines 99-344) ===
/**
 * pal-sync.js
 * ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Shared Supabase sync helper for Pete's Apps.
 * v1.0 — extracted from Claim Tracker's sync layer, which was the
 * most robust of four slightly-different implementations found
 * across the suite (Claim Tracker / On Budget / Test & Issues used
 * proper bidirectional last-write-wins merge; GigsAndTrips did too
 * but with tombstones kept forever and a different field name;
 * Gym Tracker and Fortnight Tracker did a cloud-replaces-local
 * approach with their own tombstone workarounds). This file is the
 * one canonical pattern going forward.
 * v1.1 — added an optional `prefix` per table() instance. Some apps
 * (Test & Issues) share ONE Supabase table across multiple record
 * kinds using a record_key prefix ('app_', 'issue_'), where more than
 * one kind carries an `id` field — without prefix scoping, pulling
 * "apps" would also merge in "issues" that happen to expose `.id`.
 * Each table() instance now optionally scopes itself to one prefix;
 * omitting it (Claim Tracker's usage) is unchanged and fully backward
 * compatible — prefix defaults to '', so id === record_key as before.
 * v1.2 — pull() hardcoded the merge timestamp field as `updated_at`.
 * Claim Tracker's own records use that name, but Test & Issues' apps
 * and issues use `updatedAt` (camelCase) — so for that app, EVERY
 * comparison silently evaluated `'' > ''` (false), meaning an existing
 * local record could never be updated by a genuinely newer cloud copy.
 * This wasn't a hidden risk, it was total breakage for that field
 * convention. pull() now takes an optional updatedAtField (3rd arg,
 * default 'updated_at' — unchanged for existing callers).
 * v1.3 — two fixes surfaced while planning On Budget, which shares one
 * table across SEVEN record kinds (far more than Test & Issues' two):
 * (1) pull() did its own full-table GET every time — fine for one or
 * two kinds, wasteful for seven near-identical fetches of the same
 * rows. pull() now accepts an optional 4th arg, preFetchedRows; when
 * provided, it skips the network call and merges against those rows
 * instead. New PalSync.fetchTableRows(tableName) does the one fetch a
 * multi-kind app needs, shared across all its table() instances.
 * Existing 3-arg callers (Claim Tracker, Test & Issues) are unaffected
 * — they keep doing their own single fetch exactly as before.
 * (2) the tie-break on an exact timestamp match was local-wins (`>`).
 * On Budget's own hand-rolled merges (already in production, proven)
 * use cloud-wins-on-tie (`>=`) — that's what makes a push-then-pull on
 * the same device converge cleanly instead of re-diverging. Adopted
 * `>=` as the one canonical choice; Claim Tracker and Test & Issues
 * inherit this too, since a tie is an edge case rare enough that
 * consistency across apps matters more than which side wins it.
 * v1.4 — the "push local-only records up" step in pull() excluded
 * anything with _deleted:true. Fine for apps that splice a deleted
 * record out of its local array immediately (Claim Tracker, Test &
 * Issues) — there's no local tombstone left to exclude. But On Budget
 * keeps _deleted:true records in their local arrays deliberately, so a
 * delete made while offline survives until it's confirmed synced. With
 * the old exclusion, that offline tombstone would never get pushed by
 * a pull — it would just be silently stripped from the merged result
 * (pull()'s output has always dropped _deleted records, correctly),
 * with the cloud never having been told. Other devices would then never
 * see the deletion. Local-only records are now always pushed up exactly
 * as they are (including a _deleted:true one), regardless of which
 * pattern the calling app uses — a strict correctness improvement, not
 * a behavior choice, since a tombstone that never reaches the cloud
 * defeats the entire point of tombstoning.
 * v1.5 — thrown errors only ever carried a message string. Gym Tracker's
 * retry queue needs to tell "session token expired (401) — worth queuing
 * for automatic retry once a fresh token arrives" apart from any other
 * failure, and parsing a status code back out of message text is fragile.
 * Errors now carry a .status property (the HTTP status, where available)
 * alongside .message — purely additive, no existing catch that only reads
 * .message is affected.
 * v1.6 — some apps (Reading Tracker, GigsAndTrips) have a second, standalone
 * auth path — an email/password login with its own refresh-token flow —
 * for when the app is opened directly rather than through the launcher.
 * Until now there was no way to hand a token obtained that way to this
 * library; _token/_userId were only ever settable via the internal
 * PAL_SESSION postMessage listener. New PalSync.setSession(token, userId)
 * lets an app feed in a session from any source, so a standalone-auth path
 * can use the same table()/pull()/upsert() machinery as the normal
 * launcher path instead of needing a second, parallel sync implementation.
 * v1.7 — tombstone() always stamped the dead record's timestamp as
 * `updated_at` (snake_case), with no way to override it. Every camelCase
 * app (Test & Issues, Gym Tracker, Fortnight Tracker, Reading Tracker)
 * noticed this during their own migration and worked around it by never
 * calling tombstone() at all — building the tombstone object by hand
 * instead, since the hardcoded field wouldn't refresh whatever their own
 * merge actually reads. Not a live bug (every app already sidesteps it),
 * but a landmine for the next migration that assumes the helper "just
 * works" regardless of field convention. tombstone() now takes an
 * optional updatedAtField (3rd arg, default 'updated_at' — unchanged for
 * existing callers, e.g. Claim Tracker's and On Budget's).
 * v1.8 — only Gym Tracker had any handling for a push failing because the
 * session token expired mid-use (401): it queued the record and retried
 * once a fresh PAL_SESSION arrived. On Budget, Test & Issues, Claim
 * Tracker, and Fortnight Tracker had none — a 401 during upsert() was
 * just logged and dropped by the caller, relying on the next full pull()
 * to notice the local record is newer than cloud and push it again. Not
 * data loss, but inconsistent, and something every app would otherwise
 * have to reimplement by hand (as Gym Tracker did). Two additions, both
 * purely additive:
 * (1) table().upsert() now auto-queues itself internally whenever a
 * PATCH/POST fails with status 401, then still re-throws exactly as
 * before — existing callers that catch and log the error see no change
 * in behaviour. The queue auto-flushes the next time a session arrives,
 * via initSession()/setSession(), before any app code runs — no app
 * needs to remember to call anything for the common case. New
 * PalSync.flushRetryQueue() is also exposed for a manual/explicit flush,
 * and PalSync.retryQueueLength() for a UI to show "N pending".
 * (2) PalSync.errorHint(status, message) — Gym Tracker's syncErrorHint()
 * pulled out into the shared library, so every app gets the same plain-
 * English translation of a 401/403/404 instead of a bare status code.
 * v1.9 — two latent-bug fixes, no API changes, no app-side changes needed:
 * (1) PAGINATION. fetchTableRows() did one GET with no Range header, and
 * Supabase/PostgREST caps a single response at 1,000 rows by default. No
 * table is near that yet, but Reading Tracker history and Gym sessions
 * grow forever and tombstones accelerate it — and a capped pull wouldn't
 * error, it would silently truncate. Worse, pull()'s push-local-only-up
 * step would then treat the missing rows as "not in cloud" and re-push
 * them. fetchTableRows() now requests pages of 1,000 with a Range header
 * (ordered by record_key for stable pages) and Prefer: count=exact, then
 * loops until the Content-Range total confirms every row is in hand —
 * robust even if the server's max-rows is ever configured lower than
 * 1,000. Single-page tables behave exactly as before: one request.
 * (2) PERSISTED RETRY QUEUE. The v1.8 401 retry queue was memory-only —
 * a queued write followed by a tab close or launcher iframe eviction was
 * gone until the next full pull happened to reconcile it. The queue now
 * mirrors to localStorage ('pal_retry_queue_v1') on every change and
 * rehydrates at script load, so a stranded write survives eviction and
 * flushes on the next session arrival. Queue entries no longer hold live
 * table() references (unserialisable) — they store {tableName, prefix,
 * id, data} and the flush reconstructs a table() on demand. Deliberate
 * consequence: localStorage is shared across the suite's origin, so ANY
 * app with a live session flushes ANY app's stranded writes — a write
 * stranded by Gym Tracker gets rescued the moment On Budget next opens,
 * instead of waiting for Gym specifically. A double-flush race between
 * two simultaneously-open apps is harmless (upserts are last-write-wins
 * with a fresh updated_at); a read-modify-write race on the stored queue
 * between two apps queueing at the exact same moment could in theory
 * drop one entry, accepted as vanishingly unlikely at this scale and
 * self-healing via the next pull. Non-401 failures during a flush are
 * dropped, same as v1.8 (documented behaviour, not a regression).
 * v1.10 — tombstone compaction, the suite's ONE sanctioned use of hard
 * DELETE. Soft-delete tombstones are kept forever by design (they stop
 * resurrection on pull), but they accumulate without bound and every
 * pull fetches all of them. countCompactableTombstones(table, days) and
 * compactTombstones(table, days) target only rows that are BOTH
 * tombstoned (data->>_deleted = true) AND stale (updated_at older than
 * the threshold, default 90 days, clamped to a 30-day minimum). Safety
 * argument: a device offline longer than the threshold does a fresh
 * bootstrap on return, and bootstrap treats cloud as authoritative — a
 * compacted tombstone therefore has nothing left to protect against.
 * Live rows and recent tombstones are untouchable by construction (the
 * WHERE clause, plus RLS scoping everything to the caller's own rows).
 * Deliberately NOT automatic: apps surface it as a count-then-confirm
 * button. GigsAndTrips and Meal Planner (bespoke shared sync) are out
 * of scope — their shared-data tombstone policy needs its own thinking.
 * v1.11 — pull()'s final line unconditionally dropped every _deleted:true
 * record from `merged`, regardless of whether the cloud had actually
 * confirmed the deletion. Every calling app rebuilds its local array
 * straight from `merged`, so this meant: delete something, and on the
 * VERY NEXT pull — success or failure of that delete's own tombstone
 * push — the local record of the deletion itself was gone, not just the
 * (correctly) hidden record. If the tombstone push had failed for any
 * reason (network blip, 401, offline), the cloud still held the old live
 * row, and with local memory of the delete now wiped too, a LATER pull
 * would freely adopt that stale row as if it were legitimate unseen data
 * — the deleted record resurrects, permanently, with no further chance
 * to self-correct. Traced through On Budget ON--049 and ON--050: the
 * second bug was an app-level retry sweep (compare _deleted:true local
 * records against cloud confirmation) that could never fire, because by
 * the time it ran, pull() had already erased the local tombstone it
 * needed to check. Root cause was here, one layer below any app's own
 * logic, affecting every app and every table using table().pull().
 * Two changes, no signature change, existing 3-arg and 4-arg callers
 * both unaffected other than getting the fix:
 * (1) merged no longer strips _deleted:true unconditionally. A record
 * only leaves merged once the CLOUD independently confirms the
 * deletion (its own row for that id also carries _deleted:true) — at
 * that point it's already removed from the working map by the existing
 * "cloud tombstone wins" branch earlier in pull(), so nothing extra is
 * needed to drop it. Anything still _deleted:true in the map by the end
 * is, by construction, one the cloud hasn't echoed back yet, and now
 * stays in merged so the calling app's local array keeps remembering it
 * across pulls instead of forgetting after one cycle.
 * (2) an unconfirmed local tombstone whose id already exists in cloud
 * (so the existing "local-only" push skips it, since that only fires
 * for ids missing from cloud entirely) now gets its own explicit retry
 * push every pull, until the cloud confirms it. Previously such a
 * tombstone was pushed exactly once, at the moment of deletion, with no
 * second chance if that single push failed.
 * Consequence every calling app needs to know: merged can now contain
 * _deleted:true records it never used to. Every app in the suite is
 * documented as filtering !record._deleted at render/calc time — that
 * pattern is what makes this safe; an app that instead relied on pull()
 * having already scrubbed deletes for it will start showing tombstoned
 * records until the cloud confirms them. Audited alongside this release
 * (see each app's own changelog): Reading Tracker and Test & Issues had
 * no such filtering anywhere and needed it added; Fortnight Tracker had
 * it for codes but not bundles. On Budget, Gym Tracker, and Claim
 * Tracker already filtered consistently and needed no changes for this.
 *
 * v1.12 — opt-in SHARED mode for tables that two known users read and
 * write together (first user: Film & TV Tracker, pal_film_tracker).
 * Everything above was strictly per-user: fetchTableRows(), upsert()'s
 * PATCH and the compaction filters all hard-coded user_id=eq.<me>, so
 * even when a table's RLS let both users in, each only ever saw their
 * own rows. table(name, { shared: true }) and fetchTableRows(name,
 * { shared: true }) change that, and ONLY for callers that pass the flag
 * — every existing app behaves byte-for-byte as before.
 * Shared mode: (1) fetch drops the user_id filter (RLS is the boundary)
 * and collapses duplicate record_keys to the newest updated_at, ordered
 * by record_key then user_id so pagination stays stable; (2) upsert()
 * PATCHes by record_key alone and omits user_id from the PATCH body, so
 * one user editing the other's record updates it in place instead of
 * forking a second copy or taking ownership; POST (new record) still
 * stamps the caller's user_id; (3) the flag rides along in the retry
 * queue so a queued shared upsert is replayed as shared. Compaction is
 * left per-user on purpose (see v1.10 note on shared-data tombstones).
 *
 * v1.13 (TI-089) — storage helpers. PURELY ADDITIVE: two new functions on
 * the public object, nothing existing changed, so every app that does not
 * call them behaves byte-for-byte as before. Why: every app on this origin
 * shares ONE browser localStorage quota, and Safari on the Mac enforces
 * about 5 MB (UTF-16, i.e. ~2.5 M characters) of it. The suite had
 * reached ~3.3 MB before Test & Issues (a ~2 MB cache of data that is
 * already in Supabase) tried to add itself and was refused.
 *   storageUsage() — read-only origin scan: { totalKB, keys:[{key,kb}] }
 *     largest first, same (key+value)*2 UTF-16 basis as trimIfLarge().
 *     Returns null if localStorage is unavailable.
 *   cacheSet(key, value, opts) — quota-safe write for a key that is only
 *     a CACHE of Supabase. Never throws. opts.maxKB + opts.cloudSafe:
 *     when the value exceeds maxKB AND the caller asserts nothing is
 *     unsynced (cloudSafe) AND there is a live session AND the retry
 *     queue is empty, the local copy is NOT written (and a stale one is
 *     removed) — mode 'cloud-only'. In every other case it tries the
 *     write and reports mode 'local' or 'failed' (with .quota true when
 *     the browser refused for space). The library cannot know about an
 *     app's own failed pushes, hence cloudSafe being the caller's claim.
 *     Not valid for an app whose sync bypasses table() (Gigs & Trips):
 *     retryQueueLength() says nothing about its pending writes.
 *
 * Loaded via <script src="pal-sync.js"></script> AFTER pal-config.js
 * in each app HTML file. Depends on window.PAL_CONFIG (SB_URL, SB_KEY).
 *
 * Does NOT touch localStorage or any app's data model — this only
 * knows about Supabase rows shaped { user_id, record_key, data,
 * updated_at }. Each app still owns its own local storage, envelope
 * shape, and rendering.
 * ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 */
```

## `pal-gcal.js`

Shared Google Calendar access layer, kept separate from `pal-shared.js` on purpose (pal-shared.js loads in every app; this module was unproven). Scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events`. The Google Identity Services script must load before it. App metadata is stored in `extendedProperties.private` under the key `petegcal` (`META_NAMESPACE`). Access is client-side only: a GIS access token (~1 hour), silent refresh while the page is open, no refresh token.

Public API: `init`, `signIn`, `signOut`, `hasToken`, `getTokenExpiry`, `requestTokenRefresh`, `errorHint`, `withAppMeta`, `readAppMeta`, `listEvents`, `listInstances`, `createEvent`, `updateEvent`, `deleteEvent`, `getEvent`.

Affected applications: PeteGCal (first consumer) and Gigs & Trips. ⏸ Both consumers were put on hold at launcher v11.01 (2026-10-04); Gigs & Trips is back in the launcher from v11.24 (PET-128), PeteGCal is still on hold. The module itself is unchanged.

### v3 — GIG-115

**Gigs & Trips v7.102**

- `listEvents` gains optional `opts`: `singleEvents` (default true; `false` returns recurring masters plus individually changed/cancelled instances; `orderBy=startTime` is only sent when expanding), `showDeleted`, `updatedMin`, `pageSize`.
- New `listInstances(calendarId, masterEventId, timeMin, timeMax, opts)`, paginated.
- Defaults unchanged, so PeteGCal and every existing call behave exactly as before.
- Tested in Node with a stubbed fetch (default parameters identical to v2; no `orderBy` when un-expanded; pagination; instances URL and encoding).
- Gigs & Trips v7.103, v7.104, v7.105 and v7.106 record `pal-gcal.js` as unchanged (still v3). v7.105 adds the write path for repeating events on top of the existing `createEvent` / `updateEvent` (with `expectEtag`) / `deleteEvent`; the event metadata for a series carries `kind:'series'` alongside `app:'gigs-and-trips'`.

### v2 — `updateEvent` `expectEtag`

**Gigs & Trips v7.97**

- `updateEvent(calendarId, eventId, patchBody, meta, opts)` with `opts.expectEtag`: if the event's etag in Google differs, the update is refused with error code `etag-mismatch`, status 412, `e.data` = current event. Reuses the GET that the meta merge already makes, so no extra call.
- Callers that do not pass `opts` are unaffected.
- Gigs & Trips script tag moved to `?v=2`; PeteGCal still loads `?v=1` and is unaffected.
- ⚠ ID discrepancy: the `pal-gcal.js` header attributes v2 to GIG-102; the Gigs & Trips v7.97 changelog attributes it to GIG-115 ("reduced"). Both preserved.

### v1 — PGC-002

**Introduced with PeteGCal — launcher v10.98 (PET-103 / PGC-003)**

- New shared module: Google OAuth (sign-in, silent token refresh about 5 minutes before expiry), list/create/update/delete/get wrappers, and `withAppMeta` / `readAppMeta` helpers. `init` takes `onAuthChange`, `onTokenRefreshed`, `onAuthError` and `onInitFailed` (fires if the Google script never loads after ~20 attempts).
- Underlying API calls proven via the `gcal-test.html` spike page.
- Adopted by Gigs & Trips v7.77 (GIG-072), reusing PeteGCal's OAuth Client ID (one Client ID per origin).
- Constraints recorded in the Gigs & Trips backlog against the original version: `listEvents` hard-coded `singleEvents=true` and `orderBy=startTime` (made optional in v3); `updateEvent` with `meta` makes two calls (GET then PATCH); the metadata key is shared with PeteGCal (AD-9: keep `petegcal`, add an `app:'gigs-and-trips'` field — done in Gigs & Trips v7.94).

## `pal-diag.js`

On-demand Device check, loaded by the launcher only when Pete opens it (P menu row "Device check" or the Home jump). Not loaded by any app; the launcher works without it.

### pal-diag 1.3.0 — Fonts section — 5 Nov 2026 (launcher v11.80)

- **Change:** new "Fonts" section in the Device check: font files fetched from this site on this page load, requests to Google font hosts (expected 0), the font faces and their load state, and whether DM Sans and Bricolage Grotesque are usable. Otherwise as 1.2.0. Details in Programme R26.

### pal-diag 1.2.0 — contract meta, issues and cloud contracts — 5 Nov 2026 (launcher v11.67)

- **Change:** Contracts lines show app, schema, library and capabilities and flag issues; new "Cloud contracts" section. Otherwise as 1.1.0. Details in Programme R14.

### pal-diag 1.1.0 — version check — 4 Nov 2026 (launcher v11.66)

- **Change:** App frames lines show the loaded `PalShared` version; new "Version check" section (RESULT line, MISMATCH, LIBRARY SKEW). Otherwise as 1.0.1. Details in Programme R12.

### pal-diag 1.0.1 — nested frames and contract age — 4 Nov 2026 (launcher v11.65)

- **Change:** frame scan now descends up to two levels (`parent > child`), reporting only nested frames that the parent has opened; contract age reads `built`. Same read-only behaviour and storage probe as 1.0.0; ASCII-only file. Details and tests are in the P Apps Launcher v11.65 entry.

### pal-diag 1.0.0 — new — 4 Nov 2026 (Suite WP0.2)

- **What:** builds a plain-text report, format `device-check/1`, shown in a sheet with **Copy report** and **Close**. Sections: report header (launcher version, user name, time), device (user agent, home-screen mode, viewport, safe areas, viewport meta, connection), time and date (time zone, local date versus UTC date, flagged when they differ), localStorage (key count, size by group, largest keys, write headroom), origin storage (`navigator.storage.estimate`, persistence, IndexedDB names), `pal_x_*` contracts (size, schema, truncated user id, age), app frames (loaded or not, title, `pal-shared.js` version tag, PalSync present), service workers, and `manifest.json` / install details.
- **Read-only, with one exception:** a storage-headroom probe writes a scratch key (`__pal_diag_probe`) in 250 KB steps then 10 KB steps, capped at 2.5 million characters, and removes it in a `finally` block; a stale probe key from an interrupted run is removed first. A save by another app in the same few milliseconds could in principle fail while the probe holds space (approved by Pete, D8). No tokens, keys, email addresses or record contents are reported; user ids are truncated to 8 characters.
- **Network:** one same-origin `fetch` of `manifest.json`. Nothing is sent anywhere.
- **Affected applications:** launcher only (v11.64).
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium at 430 px, Europe/London, clock fixed at 23:30 UTC on 10 Jul 2026): report header and sections, local/UTC date difference flagged, contract row with truncated user id, frame states, manifest fields, probe key absent afterwards and existing data untouched, storage filled to the limit (probe measures about 0 KB headroom and still cleans up), Copy and Close, double-run guard, no page errors; file contains ASCII only. **Not tested:** real iPhone home-screen app, Safari storage limits (quota behaviour differs from Chromium), `navigator.storage.persisted` on iOS, IndexedDB listing on iOS.

### v11.65 — Suite WP0.2 — Device check sees apps nested inside other apps — 4 Nov 2026

- **Found by:** the Horizon v5.2 / Gym v2.137 deployment check, test T6 ("Horizon is not shown although opened"). Horizon, Claim Tracker and HTML Vault are not top-level launcher frames: they are lazy iframes inside On Budget (Horizon, Claims, Vault via its tabs) and similar parents, so the v11.64 Device check, which only looked at the launcher's own `iframe.app-frame` elements, always reported them as not loaded. The apps and the launcher were not at fault; the T6 instruction was wrong (it said Horizon is switched on in Standalone settings).
- **Change (`index.html`, `pal-diag.js` 1.0.1):** the Device check now looks up to two levels inside each loaded app frame and lists nested frames as `parent > child` with title, `pal-shared.js` tag and whether `PalSync` is present; a nested frame appears only once its parent has opened it. The contract "age" now reads `built` (v11.64 looked for `updatedAt`, which contracts do not have, so age always showed "-") and prints minutes, hours or days.
- **Why a launcher version:** the launcher loads `pal-diag.js?v=<LAUNCHER_VERSION>`, so the new file is only fetched when the launcher version changes. `LAUNCHER_VERSION`, `<title>`, desktop badge and menu line: v11.65. No other launcher behaviour changed.
- **Data and compatibility:** none touched.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium): a page with a top-level frame, an unopened frame, a nested frame two levels deep and a third level (not reported); contract age for 5 minutes, 3 days and no timestamp; the real launcher: title, badge, menu text, backup manifest all v11.65, Device check row Pete-only, no probe key left, no page errors. **Not tested:** the real iPhone nesting (On Budget → Horizon tab). Covered by the deployment check.

### v11.59 — PET-166 — Storage panel can be closed; Clear / Postpone / Ignore on every alert; Needs attention collapses to one row on a phone — 3 Nov 2026

- **Reported (Pete, 3 Nov, after v11.58):** (1) once the Storage and clear section is opened it cannot be closed; (2) Needs attention needs postpone, ignore **and clear**, where clear never returns; (3) on a phone Needs attention should be a whole collapsed section with a refresh button and a badge with the number of active alerts that expands; (4) the Fantasy refresh in that section is no longer needed.
- **Cause of (1):** the only control that closed the panel (Storage details) lives inside Alert settings, which is not open when you arrive by tapping the storage alert.
- **Change (`index.html` only; no app, `pal-shared.js`, storage format, sync or schema change):**
  - **Storage panel:** a **Close** button in its header, and **Esc** closes it. It can also be closed when no storage alert is showing.
  - **Row actions (all screen sizes):** each alert now has **Clear**, **Postpone** and **Ignore**. Postpone opens Tomorrow / 3 days / 7 days / Cancel in place (the old Tomorrow and 7d buttons moved here). Ignore is as before (kept under "n ignored · Show again"). **Clear** (`pxClear`) is gone for good: it is not counted as ignored, "Show again" never restores it, and an **Undo** row stays for 8 seconds. It is stored in the same synced snooze map as the value `c<date>`; that value sorts after any date, so older launchers (which treat any value as hidden and only prune dates) keep it hidden. Cleared entries are forgotten after 180 days. An alert whose id carries a date or phase (the promoted, elapsed and feed alerts, the Gym and Reading reminders, Gigs clashes) is cleared by id; one with a stable id (On Budget "bills past due", Claims "expiring soon") is cleared together with its due date and text, so if the situation changes (2 bills past due instead of 1) it is a new alert and shows again.
  - **Phone (width 599 px or less):** Needs attention is one collapsed row: title, a **badge with the number of active alerts** (red when any needs action, amber for coming up, grey for info only, a green tick when none), a chevron, and a **refresh button** that runs Refresh all (it spins while it works and the section stays collapsed). Tap the row to expand and again to collapse. The Refresh all button in the home header is hidden there while the section shows, and returns if the section has nothing to show. Tapping a card's badge expands the section and filters to that app. Resizing across the breakpoint redraws it. **Desktop and tablet are unchanged** (always expanded).
  - **Clean-up:** the **Refresh Fantasy now** button is removed from Alert settings (Refresh all, the card's Fantasy freshness line and the pull-down do it; the Fantasy and Other apps status lines stay).
