### v11.58 — PET-165 — The "Browser storage is n% full" warning becomes actionable: see where the space goes and clear what is safe — 3 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** the storage warning showed 87% on the iPhone; "no use unless there is something we can do to help".
- **Background (from this changelog):** every app shares one origin and so one localStorage quota (about 5 MB counted as UTF-16 on Safari). Earlier incidents were Test & Issues' `ti_v1` (~2 MB), the Film & TV library (~2.5 MB, since moved to IndexedDB) and Gigs & Trips' duplicate `gat_v1_clean`. PET-160 only warned and named the largest key.
- **Change (`index.html` only; no app, `pal-shared.js`, storage format, sync or schema change):**
  - **Storage panel** (`pxStoragePanel`): opens when you tap the storage alert or from Alert settings → Storage details. Shows a bar, "n% of about 5 MB", the 12 biggest items with a plain name, size and a tag (Older copy / Cache / App data / Other), a **Clear n items (size)** button and a per-row **Clear** only where it is safe, and **Copy report** (every key, size and kind, to paste into the chat). Confirm dialog lists exactly what goes and the space it frees; the result message says what was freed and the new percentage.
  - **What counts as safe (`pxStorClassify`), re-checked at the moment of clearing:** `fn_tracker_v3` / `v4` only while `fn_tracker_v5` exists (Fortnight reads v5 first and writes only v5, and never removed the older ones); `reading-tracker-v3`..`v5` only while `reading-tracker-v6` exists (the app removes them itself on migration); `gat_v1_clean` only while `gat_v1` exists (retired by Gigs STORAGE-001); `ti_v1` (the Test & Issues local copy; the app is on hold and keeps its data in the cloud); the Fantasy squad and advice caches (`ff_squad_cache*`, `ff_advice_cache*`, rebuilt when Fantasy loads; the Fantasy card asks you to open the app until then).
  - **Never offered:** the apps' live data (`gym_tracker_v1`, `reading-tracker-v6`, `on_budget_v1`, `fn_tracker_v5`, `claim_tracker_v1`, `gat_v1`, `ftt_v1`), an older key whose newer key is missing (it is then the only copy), launcher summaries, and any unknown key. `pxStorClear` ignores a request to clear anything not in the safe set, whatever the caller asks for. **Nothing is cleared while the sync retry queue holds changes.**
  - **Alert text:** now names the largest item in plain words and says how much can be cleared ("Largest: Test & Issues: local copy (1.4 MB). About 2.1 MB can be cleared. Tap to see."), or "Tap to see where it goes." when nothing is safe. Tapping it opens the panel instead of a toast. The 10-minute cache of the storage scan is reset after any clear.
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, desktop badge, menu line, inline comment: v11.58.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, the real file with the real `pal-shared.js` and real localStorage filled with realistic sizes; JS syntax check): **212 checks, all passing** — the v11.54–v11.57 suites re-run (71, 43, 35, 39; one expectation updated for the new alert wording) plus **24 new**: the safe set is exactly reading v5 + fortnight v4 + `ti_v1` when v6 / v5 exist; live and unknown keys never safe; older keys not offered when the newer key is missing; retired launcher copy and Fantasy caches offered while settings are not; the alert wording and that tapping it opens the panel; tags and Clear buttons; a cancelled confirm removes nothing and the confirm text names each item and size; clearing refused while changes are queued; a row Clear removes only its key; Clear all removes only the safe keys and every other key keeps exactly its length; the message and percentage; the alert disappears once under the threshold; hard guard (live / unknown keys cannot be cleared even when named); Storage details toggle; Copy report contents; the "only live data" wording; phone 390 px with no sideways overflow.
- **Not tested:** the iPhone itself (what is actually using the space there is unknown until the panel is opened on it), real Safari behaviour of `confirm` and the clipboard, the real sizes of the apps' data.
- **Known limitation:** if the space is taken by the apps' live data (for example a large Gym Tracker copy), nothing is offered, by design; the panel says so and **Copy report** gives the exact breakdown. The next options would be app changes (keep the large copy in IndexedDB, as Film & TV did in v3.0, or a cloud-only mode through `PalSync.cacheSet`).

### v11.57 — PET-164 — Launcher feeds, Phase 4: the launcher pulls the other apps' cloud data without you opening them — 3 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** "next" — Phase 4 of the launcher feeds plan: bring the other apps' cloud data to the launcher without opening them, and make Refresh all do it.
- **Spike findings (read from the code, before building):** (1) a loaded frame can be released safely: every launch helper (`switchTo`, `ensureLoaded`, `gymEnsureFrame`, `rtEnsureFrame`, the budget and claims equivalents) loads the frame whenever `loaded[x]` is false or the frame has no real `src`, so resetting `loaded[x]` and `_frameDone[x]` and pointing the frame at `about:blank` leaves it in the state of an app never opened. (2) Four apps already answer a ready ping that means "boot finished and the first cloud pull has settled": Gym (`GYM_ACTION` ping / `GYM_PONG`), Reading (`RT_`), On Budget (`OB_`), Claims (`CT_`). (3) Fortnight, Gigs & Trips and Film & TV have no ping. (4) None of the apps opens a window or prompt on load (every `window.open` / `confirm` is behind a user action).
- **Change (`index.html` only; no app, `pal-shared.js`, storage, sync or schema change):**
  - **`pxWarmApp` / `pxWarmRunDue`:** for Gigs & Trips, Reading, Film & TV, On Budget, Fortnight and Claims, in that order and **one at a time**: set the (hidden) frame's `src`, wait for the app's own sync to finish, wait 1.5 s for a save / republish to land, release the frame, redraw the cards and Needs attention. The apps do their normal sync, write their saved copy and republish their summary themselves; the launcher reads and writes none of their data.
  - **"Finished" is decided by:** the ready ping, polled every 250 ms (cap 45 s), for Reading, On Budget and Claims; for the three apps with no ping, by watching the frame's own `fetch` calls pass through (a pass-through wrapper installed when its document is created, not altering requests or responses): done when at least one request has been made, none are in flight and 2.5 s have passed since the last, with 4 s minimum after load; 10 s if it makes no request at all; 30 s cap.
  - **Safety rules:** never an app that is already loaded or has a `src` (left running); if the user opens the app during the warm-up the frame is **not** released and carries on as a normal open; a failed or timed-out app is still released and is not retried for 10 minutes; Pete-only apps (On Budget, Fortnight, Claims) are skipped for Lex; Gym keeps its existing once-per-session warm-up (`pxGymWarm`, PET-155) untouched and Fantasy keeps its own feed.
  - **When:** 9 s after sign-in; then at most every 30 minutes per app, checked each minute and on return to the tab, **only while Home is showing and the page is visible**, never offline, never on Data Saver; and on **Refresh all / pull-down** for any app not refreshed in the last 5 minutes (the button shows which app it is on; the message adds "n apps updated from the cloud"). Stamps are kept in `pal_x_f_warm` (cleared at sign-out with the other `pal_x_` keys).
  - **Cards:** an app refreshed this way after it last published shows "Synced from the cloud · 3 min ago" on its freshness line.
  - **Alert settings:** a "Refresh other apps from the cloud (loads them out of sight)" switch (nine switches now) and a status line ("Reading 4 min ago · On Budget failed 12 min ago …"). `pal_feeds_off = '1'` stops it as well.
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, desktop badge, menu line, inline comment: v11.57.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, fake clock, the real launcher with the real `pal-shared.js`, and **stub app pages that follow the real protocols** (PAL_SESSION, the RT / OB / CT ping and pong, fetch-based pulls with delays); JS syntax check): **188 checks, all passing** — the earlier suites re-run (v11.54 71, v11.55 43, v11.56 35; the Refresh all tests run with the new switch off) plus **39 new**: a ping app waits for its pong, not a fixed time; the app ran and its summary was published; the frame is released with `src` about:blank, `loaded` and `_frameDone` false; `switchTo` and the quick-add re-open pattern work normally afterwards (the app loads a second time); a no-ping app with three sequential fetches is not cut off early, its responses reach it unchanged, and it ends shortly after going quiet; an app that makes no request ends after the "nothing to pull" wait; a never-ready app fails at the cap, is still released, is not retried for 10 minutes and is retried after 11; an app the user opens mid-warm is not released and stays visible; already-loaded frames, Gym and Fantasy are never chosen; Lex gets only the shared apps; a full run refreshes all six in order with never more than one frame at a time and releases every one; a second run straight away does nothing; the 5-minute (Refresh all) and 30-minute (automatic) rules; kill switch, warm switch, offline, Data Saver, not on Home, hidden page, signed out; two overlapping runs (the second does nothing); "Synced from the cloud" on the card; status line; Refresh all showing the app name, the toast and the restored button; no page errors.
- **Not tested:** the real apps and the real Supabase (the stubs follow the protocols the apps use; each app's real sync time and behaviour in a hidden frame are for the deployment check), a real phone / Safari, memory and data use on a phone, the light theme, a second device.
- **Known limitations:** Refresh all can now take up to about a minute when everything is due (six apps, one after another; the page stays usable). An app that is already open in the launcher this session is not reloaded, so it keeps its own session's data. The fetch-quiet rule is a heuristic for the three apps with no ping; if one of them syncs in several bursts more than 2.5 s apart it may be released a little early and picked up on the next refresh.

### v11.56 — PET-163 — Launcher feeds, Phase 3: freshness line and attention badge on every card, Refresh all, pull-to-refresh — 3 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** "next" — Phase 3 of the launcher feeds plan: make the cards consistent about freshness and attention.
- **Change (`index.html` only; no app, `pal-shared.js`, storage, sync or schema change; the only network use is the existing Fantasy feed):** the elements are added to the cards by script, outside each card's `.card-stat`, so the card markup and every `statX()` function are as before.
  - **Freshness line** (`pxRenderChips`) at the foot of every card that has a summary (Gigs, Gym, On Budget, Fortnight, Claims, Fantasy): "From the app · 3 h ago" is the last time that app published on this device, amber after 2 days; the Fantasy card shows "Live from FPL · 3 min ago" when the launcher's own read is newer than the app's squad cache, otherwise "From the app · …". On Fantasy it is a button: tap to read FPL now (it does not open the app). The text ages on the existing minute tick without a redraw. Cards with no summary (Reading, Film & TV, Horizon, HTML Vault) show none. This replaces the line PET-162 placed inside the Fantasy stat.
  - **Attention badge** (`pxRenderBadges`) in each card's header: the number of that app's current Needs attention items (snoozed and ignored are not counted), red when any is Action required, amber when Coming up, grey when only Info. Tapping it does not open the app: it shows only that app's items in Needs attention with a "Showing … only · Show all" row and scrolls there; tap it again or "Show all" to clear; the filter clears itself when that app has nothing left.
  - **Refresh all:** a button in the home header (`#homeRefresh`, created by `pxEnsureRefreshBtn`) and a pull-down gesture at the top of Home on a touch screen (80 px; ignored when the page is scrolled down, when the gesture is mostly sideways, or with more than one finger; an indicator reads "Pull to refresh" / "Release to refresh"). Both run every feed now (`pxFeedRun(…, true)`), re-read every card from the apps' saved copies (`refreshCardStats`) and say "Refreshed" (or that live updates are off, or that a live update failed). A second call while one is running does nothing.
- **Not included, on purpose:** the plan's "next item" footer on every card (it would repeat lines the cards already show); the old "Last updated on this device" note under Needs attention is kept; the warm-up of the Supabase-backed apps is Phase 4.
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, desktop badge, menu line, inline comment: v11.56.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, fake clock, the real file with the real `pal-shared.js`, mocked `pal-fpl-proxy`; JS syntax check): **149 checks, all passing.** The v11.54 suite (71) and the v11.55 feed suite (43) re-run with the card checks updated for the freshness line, plus **35 new**: freshness text for 2 h / just now / amber after 2 days, no line without a summary, line outside the stat and surviving stat redraws, no duplicates after repeated refreshes, ageing on the tick; badge counts, colours, accessible name, absent when empty, snoozed and ignored not counted; badge tap filters, shows the Showing row, does not open the app, Show all and second tap clear it, filter clears itself; Refresh all (2 feed requests, button restored, "Refreshed", single run for two quick calls, no request under the kill switch with the right message); Fantasy chip as a button (Live after a refresh, From the app when the app cache is newer, tap refreshes without opening the app, stat no longer carries its own line); pull gesture (120 px refreshes with the indicator, 40 px does not, scrolled-down page ignored, mostly-sideways ignored); phone 390 px cards with badge and line have no sideways overflow. The tests found and fixed one bug before release: a mostly-sideways swipe still refreshed.
- **Not tested:** a real phone / Safari touch (the gesture is exercised with synthetic touch events), iOS rubber-band overscroll behaviour, the light theme, real app summaries on the live site, a second device.
- **Known limitations:** a card's "From the app" time is when the app last published on this device, which for an app that republishes on every save is its last save, not the last time it was opened. Phase 4 will refresh the other apps from the cloud in the background.

### v11.55 — PET-162 — Launcher feeds, Phase 2: the launcher refreshes the Fantasy card and Needs attention from FPL itself — 3 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** "Next" — Phase 2 of the launcher feeds plan: refresh the FPL data and update the launcher card without opening the app.
- **Change (`index.html` only; `fantasy-football-tracker.html`, `pal-shared.js`, `pal-fpl-proxy` and every other app untouched):**
  - **Feed registry** (`PX_FEEDS`, `pxFeedRun`, `pxFeedsTick`): a feed runs at sign-in (4 s after), on return to the tab, and about every 15 minutes while the page is visible; only if its switch is on, the Fantasy card is showing, and nothing is already running. After a failure it waits 5 minutes, doubling to a 2-hour cap, and keeps the last good data. A feed that lacks something (no proxy key, no FPL entry id) skips quietly and tries again in 10 minutes. The whole mechanism sits behind the existing `pal_feeds_off = '1'` kill switch.
  - **Fantasy feed** (`pxFeedFantasy`): `/bootstrap` and `/entry/<id>/picks/<current gw>` through `pal-fpl-proxy` (normal proxy cache, header `x-pal-key` from `PAL_CONFIG.FF_PROXY_KEY`, **2 requests per run**; the entry id is read from `ff_settings_local_u_<uid>`). Result kept as a small display-only overlay in `pal_x_f_fantasy` (`v:1`, `userId`, `fetchedAt`, gameweek, points, squad value, bank, rank, next gameweek and deadline, flagged players, finished-gameweek stamp). It is under the `pal_x_` prefix, so sign-out clears it with the other summaries; it is ignored for another user and after 7 days; it is never written to an app's data or sent anywhere.
  - **Fantasy card:** points, gameweek, squad value, bank and the next-gameweek line come from the overlay when it is newer than the app's squad cache (`cachedAt`) and not for an earlier gameweek; otherwise the app's figures as before. A new line says which: "Live from FPL · 3 min ago" or "From the app · 3 Nov" (the age text updates each minute without redrawing the card).
  - **Deadline without the app** (`pxMergeFeeds`): the next deadline FPL reports replaces the app's own `ff-gw-<n>` deadline item in the contract view, or creates the Fantasy view when the app has never published one, so the Timeline and the PET-160 deadline and "No locked-in squad" alerts work even when the app has not run for weeks. Nothing is added once the deadline has passed; other published items are kept.
  - **New alerts** (`pxFeedAttention`): "n players flagged for GW n" within 72 hours of the deadline (same injured / suspended / unavailable / doubtful rule as the app's `ffAvail`; watches the locked-in squad when it is for the next gameweek, otherwise the current picks): Action inside 24 h when a starter is out, Coming up when a starter is flagged, Info for bench only. "GW n: 62 pts (average 51)" with overall rank for 48 hours after a gameweek finishes (first-seen time is kept so a refresh does not bring it back).
  - **Alert settings:** a "Fantasy live updates (fetches FPL data)" switch (eight switches now), a status line (updated n min ago · n requests this session / last try failed / skipped: reason / off) and a **Refresh Fantasy now** button.
- **Not changed:** the live match poll `ffpLiveTick` (still once a minute during live matches), the pitch chips, the app's own alerts, storage formats, sync, schema.
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, desktop badge, menu line, inline comment: v11.55.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, fake clock, the real file with the real `pal-shared.js`, a mocked `pal-fpl-proxy` served through the page's network layer; JS syntax check): **114 checks, all passing** — the 71 from v11.54 re-run (switch count updated to 8) plus **43 new**: exactly 2 requests with the right paths and the `x-pal-key` header; overlay contents and size; TTL (no request within 15 min, refresh after 16); no request on a hidden page; skips (no entry id, non-numeric id, placeholder key) with zero requests; failure, 5-minute backoff, doubling, recovery; kill switch (even forced), Fantasy switch off, another user's overlay, 7-day expiry, sign-out `clearAll`; a deadline synthesised with no app contract, then the day-before deadline and "No locked-in squad" alerts from it; a stale app deadline replaced without duplication and other items kept; nothing after the deadline; BST (10:00Z shown as 11:00 on the right date); flags at 96 h (none), within 72 h (Coming up, names), within 24 h with a starter out (Action), after the deadline (gone), bench only (Info), locked-in squad preferred; GW result text, rank, 48-hour expiry and no return on refresh; card before / after the feed ("Live from FPL · just now", 62 pts, GW 10, £103.4m, £1.2m, Next GW11), the age text ticking, the app cache winning when newer; settings panel status and Refresh button; no page errors.
- **Not tested:** the real FPL data through the real `pal-fpl-proxy` (the mock follows the response shape the app already reads), the real entry id, a real phone / Safari, the light theme, the timer running for real over hours, a second device.
- **Known limitations:** flagged players come from the bootstrap list at fetch time (up to 15 minutes old). Only the current gameweek's picks are fetched, so a transfer made for the next gameweek is reflected in the flags only through the locked-in squad. Everything still runs only while the launcher is open.

### v11.54 — PET-161 — Planned gym session alert clears when the session is logged or the day is marked "Missed - ill" — 3 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** link the gym calendar alerts and the Gym Tracker so the alert goes away once a session has been logged or set to missed or sick.
- **Finding:** the PET-160 session alert came from the Gym summary the app last published. That summary is only rewritten when the Gym Tracker saves, and `publishContract()` (Gym v2.132) skips a session already done but never skipped a day flagged "Missed - ill" (Gym v2.130, a `{kind:'illness', date}` record in `scheduleEntries`). So an ill day kept its alert, and a session logged on another device did not clear it here until the app ran here.
- **Change (`index.html` only):** `pxGymClosed(u)` reads the Gym Tracker's own saved copy (`gym_tracker_v1`, enveloped or bare, same reading pattern as `pxGymReminders` / `statGym`) each time Needs attention is drawn. The session alert is dropped when (a) a non-deleted session exists on that date for that plan (the app's own `planDoneOnDate` rule; the plan id is taken from the summary item id `gym-<date>-<planId>`), or (b) the date has a non-deleted `kind:'illness'` record. A missing, unreadable or un-parsable copy keeps the alert. `pxClockTick` now also runs when `gym_tracker_v1` changes in another tab, so a session logged there removes the row at once; logging inside the launcher already redraws through `GYM_DATA_UPDATED`.
- **Not changed:** the Gym Tracker (no plain "Missed" mark exists in it; **Ignore** on the alert clears that one session for the day because the alert id carries the date and plan), the Gym summary, the Timeline (it still lists a planned session on an ill day), `pal-shared.js`, storage, sync or schema.
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, desktop badge, menu line, inline comment: v11.54.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, fake clock, real file with the real `pal-shared.js`; JS syntax check): **71 checks, all passing** (the 56 from v11.53 re-run plus 15 new): no local copy, empty copy, session for this plan and date (including one still in progress), bare and enveloped copies, session for another plan, same plan on another day, deleted session, ill day, undone ill day (tombstone), ill on another day, ordinary schedule entry, corrupt copy; a plan id containing `-` and `_`; the rendered row removed by a `storage` event from another tab; the Gym food / drink reminder unaffected alongside.
- **Not tested:** the live Gym Tracker writing real data, a second device syncing (the launcher only sees this device's copy, which the existing once-per-session Gym warm-up refreshes), a real phone / Safari.
- **Known limitation:** a plain "Missed" (not ill) cannot clear the alert because the Gym Tracker has no such state. It would need a small Gym Tracker change (a per-session or per-day record in `scheduleEntries`, the same pattern as the ill flag).

### v11.53 — PET-160 — Needs attention is time-aware: upcoming items are lifted in as they come up, Fantasy lock-in alert, sync and storage warnings — 3 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** phase 1 of the launcher feeds plan ("Launcher Feeds & Needs Attention: Phased Deployment Plan"). Pete wants things highlighted in Needs attention on the day and before as they come up, because having to tap to clear them works as a reminder; a "no locked-in squad for FPL" alert from the day before the deadline; no server-side work.
- **Problem found:** apps decide urgency when they save, so an alert was only as current as the app's last run (Fantasy raised its deadline alert only if the app ran in the 24 hours before the deadline; On Budget's "due in 3 days" and Claims' expiry warning are likewise frozen at publish). The apps' `upcoming` lists are already date-safe, but never became attention items.
- **Change (`index.html` only; launcher-only, no new network call, no app, `pal-shared.js`, storage-format, sync or schema change):**
  - **Promotion** (`pxPromote`): `upcoming` items become attention items as they near. Deadlines with a time: ≤48 h Coming up, ≤24 h Action required, with "in n h" (Fantasy `GW n deadline`); deadlines with a date only (Claims submission day): tomorrow Coming up, today Action. Bills: due today Action, due in the next 3 days Coming up (grouped, one line per group). Gigs and trips: on the day Coming up, the day before Info. Planned gym session today: Info, Coming up after 18:00. Film released today: Info. Holiday today / tomorrow: Info. Claim payment expected today: Info. Promoted alerts rank below the apps' own at the same level; at most 3 per app.
  - **Elapsed** (`pxElapsed`): a bill, payment or Claims date that fell due *after* the app last published (and within 7 days) shows as one Info line per app, "n dates passed since <app> last ran … check in the app". Info only, because the item may already be cleared on another device (see Phase 4 of the plan).
  - **Fantasy lock-in** (`pxFantasyLock`): "No locked-in squad for GW n" from the day before the deadline (Coming up), Action on deadline day, until the deadline passes. Deadline from the app's published `ff-gw-<n>` item; locked-in state from `ff_locked_card_u_<uid>` (its `gw` must equal n and it must hold 11 starters; the app removes the key when nothing is locked).
  - **Platform warnings** (`pxHealthItems`): changes waiting in the persisted sync retry queue (`pal_retry_queue_v1`) for 3 minutes or more (Coming up); browser storage ≥ 4 MB (Coming up) or ≥ 4.6 MB (Action) of ~5 MB, naming the largest key (read at most every 10 minutes). Shown with a 🛠️ "P Apps" icon; tapping shows the detail instead of opening an app.
  - **Replaces two frozen alerts while their switch is on** (`PX_SUPERSEDED`): Fantasy `ff-deadline-<n>` and On Budget `ob-due-soon`. With the switch off, or the kill switch on, the apps' own alerts show exactly as before.
  - **Ids carry the phase / day** (`p:<id>:24`, `:48`, `:0`, `:1`, `p:fflock:<gw>:<level>`) so Tomorrow / 7d / Ignore only hide that phase: ignoring the day-before alert does not hide the day-of alert.
  - **Alert settings:** a button under the list opens seven switches (Deadlines and lock-in, Bills and payments, Gigs and trips, Planned gym sessions, Film & TV releases, Holidays, Sync and storage warnings), kept per device in `pal_promote_prefs`. `localStorage pal_feeds_off = '1'` (or `PAL_CONFIG.PX_PROMOTE_OFF`) turns every new alert off.
  - **Clock tick** (`pxClockTick`): once a minute and on return to the tab, Needs attention is redrawn only if the set of alerts has changed (a deadline moved into its next phase, midnight rolled over, a warning appeared). The early return in `pxRenderAttention` now also allows a platform warning on its own.
- **Deliberately not included:** a backup-age alert (the staleness layer was removed at PET-092); Fortnight's "Hours target at risk" expiry (needs the optional `until` field, Phase 5 of the plan); anything from the network (Phase 2 onward).
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, desktop badge, menu line, inline comment: v11.53. `pal-shared.js` (pal-contract v1), `pal-search.js` and every app file untouched.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium with a fake clock, the real file served locally with the real `pal-shared.js`; JS syntax check): **56 checks, all passing.** Fantasy deadline at 96 h (nothing), 47.5 h (Coming up), the day before (deadline plus lock-in Coming up), deadline day (Action "in 4 h", lock-in Action with a different id from the day-before one), locked for an older gameweek (still alerts), locked for this one (lock-in gone), after the deadline (nothing), the app's frozen alert replaced with no duplicate, and returning when the Deadlines switch is off; bills due today / next 3 days / beyond, `ob-due-soon` replaced and `ob-overdue` kept, ranking; gig, trip, session (before and after 18:00), release, holiday, payment and Claims submission day; the 3-per-app cap; elapsed bill, Claims date and no Fantasy elapsed; sync-queue alert after 3 minutes and its clearing, storage at 4.3 MB and 4.8 MB, switch off; Tomorrow on the day-before alert leaves the deadline-day alert; another user's contract ignored; kill switch; per-group switch; rendered box, settings panel (7 switches), unchecking and re-checking, midnight tick redraw into Action required, platform row tap; **differential run against v11.52 with the kill switch on: identical attention list**; same console errors as v11.52 on load; no sideways scroll at 390 px with the settings panel open.
- **Not tested:** the real Fantasy / On Budget / Claims / Gigs summaries on the live site, a real phone / Safari, the light theme, the localStorage size reading on a real device, a second device, the 60-second timer running for real (the test calls the tick directly).
- **Known limitations:** alerts are only as good as the last summary an app published (an item cleared on another device can still show until the app runs here; hence Info for elapsed items). The "no locked-in squad" alert assumes locking in is part of the weekly routine for the signed-in user; Ignore hides it for that gameweek only. Everything still only runs while the launcher is open.

### v11.50 — PET-157 — Reading card week view with streaks; daily "Read today" reminder in Needs attention — 3 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** on the Reading card show a week view, coloured by whether he read, one row for books and one for audio, with a streak view; and set a daily reminder in Needs attention to read.
- **Week view:** a new "This week" block between the progress line and the shelf. Monday to Sunday with weekday and date on each column; row 📖 books and row 🎧 audio. A day is green with a tick if read, red with a cross if missed, a solid ring for today until read, faint for days to come and for days before the first log ever (so a new user is not shown a wall of red). Each row ends with its own current streak; the header shows the combined streak.
- **Where the days come from:** the Reading Tracker's saved copy (`reading-tracker-v6`), as the shelf does. Every Book List item's `readingEntries` (type audiobook = audio, otherwise book) plus the older trackers' `entries` (tracker type `audible` = audio). Deleted books and trackers are skipped. Nothing new is stored; no contract, sync or schema change.
- ⚠ **Streak rule differs slightly from the Reading Tracker's Stats streak:** the launcher counts back from yesterday while today is still open (the header then reads "N-day streak · read today" in red); the app's Stats streak shows 0 until the first log of the day. Same dates otherwise. The app's Stats also counts entries of deleted books; the launcher does not.
- **Reminder:** Needs attention gets "Read today" (Action required) from 18:00 each day until anything is logged that day (any book or audiobook), with "Keep your N-day streak going · <most recently read book>" or "Nothing logged yet today". Worked out in the launcher from the saved data (same approach as the v11.47 Gym reminders, `pxReadingReminders()`), so it needs no contract and no running app. Only for a signed-in user with something on the Book List or any logged reading. Tomorrow / 7d / Ignore hide that day's reminder only (the id carries the date). The time is the constant `PX_READ_REMIND_AT`. Re-checked every minute, on returning to the tab, on `RT_DATA_UPDATED` and when `reading-tracker-v6` changes in another tab. The Needs attention box now also shows when the Reading reminder is the only item (it used to need an app contract).
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, desktop badge, menu line, inline comment: v11.50. `pal-shared.js` untouched. Pairs with reading-tracker.html v3.91 (dates on the Stats calendar); neither requires the other.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium with a fixed clock and a stub `pal-shared.js`, the real file): no page errors; version in title; week at 430 px and 1280 px (Monday start, Sunday edge, today ring, future and pre-first-log days faint); book and audio rows separate; tracker `audible` entries count as audio; deleted book and deleted tracker ignored; streaks per row and combined, including counting from yesterday; no data or empty list hides the week; reminder shown at 19:00 with the streak and book, not shown at 09:00, cleared when today's log appears, hidden by Tomorrow, absent when signed out or with no data.
- **Not tested:** the real Reading Tracker in its frame with live Supabase, a second device, a real phone or Safari, the light theme visually, many days of real data, a real 18:00 crossing while the page stays open (simulated by the clock only).

### v11.49 — PET-156 — Reading card shows the "this month" shelf (spines or covers); tap a book to log pages / chapters for it — 3 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** on the Reading Tracker card show the cover when there is one, show the same shelf as the app's this-month view with covers as in the app, and select the book from the shelf to update the page or chapter in the quick input.
- **Shelf:** drawn under the progress line from the same saved data the app uses (`reading-tracker-v6`) and follows the app's rules: books finished this month, then active unfinished books, books before audiobooks, at most 8 (a "+N more in the app" note if there are more). Each book is a spine (colour, thickness and height from page count, bookmark line for progress, tick when finished, headphones and aqua cap for audiobooks, your icon, "?" when no page count) or, when the book has a cover and is set to Cover (`shelfStyle`) or the app's per-device Covers toggle (`rt_bk_covers`) applies, a 72 × 108 cover tile with the title behind it, a progress bar or tick. A book set to Spine stays a spine. Deleted records and books not marked Reading are not shown.
- **Pick a book:** tapping an unfinished book selects it (raised, outlined, "Logging to: …"), moves the Book / Audio tag and the placeholder to match its type (Page reached / Chapter reached), clears the box and focuses it. The progress line above shows that book. Finished books are not tappable. The Book ⇄ Audio tag still works and selects the most recently read active book of the other type. The selection is held in memory only; nothing new is stored.
- **Logging:** the box sends the picked book's `itemId` with the page / chapter. Needs reading-tracker.html v3.90; an older Reading Tracker is refused with a message before anything is sent (it would otherwise log to a different "current book").
- ⚠ **Behaviour change:** the card used to show and (before v3.76) log against the first book in the manual queue. It now shows the most recently read active book, the same "current book" the Reading Tracker's own quick-log uses, and says "No book marked Reading" when none is active (it showed "All caught up"). The daily-target bar and today's target are unchanged, computed for the shown book.
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, desktop badge, menu line, inline comment: v11.49. `pal-shared.js` untouched. No storage, sync or schema change. Launcher compatibility: other cards, Timeline, Today board, search unchanged.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium at 430 px, stub `pal-shared.js`, a stub Reading Tracker frame answering the ping and the log): no page errors; version in title, badge and menu; shelf slots and order (finished, active, audiobook; inactive and deleted excluded); spine / cover / audiobook / tick / "?" rendering; default pick is the most recently read active book; tapping switches book, mode, placeholder and progress line; the log carries the picked `itemId`, kind and value; Book ⇄ Audio returns to a book; the app's Covers toggle is honoured and an explicit Spine is not overridden; an older Reading Tracker is refused with nothing sent and the entry kept; no data hides the shelf.
- **Not tested:** the real Reading Tracker inside the frame with live Supabase, a second device, a real phone or Safari, the light theme and desktop layout visually, real cover images from Open Library / Google Books, many covers on one shelf, the app's own light theme.

### v11.48 — PET-155 — Fixes from the v11.47 deployment check: version badge; Gym quick-add is one search box; reminders more dependable — 3 Nov 2026

- **Deployment check of v11.47 / Gym v2.134 (Pete, 3 Nov):** Gym v2.134 T1 – T9 all passed. Launcher **v11.47-T1** (version), **T2** (reminder set for 10:36 did not show), **T3 / T4** (blocked by T2) and **T5** failed. Pete's notes: the desktop label does not match the version (the phone is right); Saved items should be grouped into food and drink; and "input on launcher doesn't need to distinguish food and drink, just search for existing, if adding new open the actual app".
- **v11.47-T1 — cause and fix:** the desktop header badge (`.nav-version` inside `#navHome`) is hard-coded in the nav markup and still read **v11.46**; v11.47 updated the title and the menu line only. ⚠ The v11.47 entry's "Version sync" line was therefore incomplete. v11.48 sets all three (title, desktop badge, menu line) and the Stage 1 run now reads all three from the rendered page.
- **Quick-add redesign (PET-155; the T1 / T5 notes):** the Gym card's row is **one search box and Add** — no Drink / Food switch, no amount, no protein box. Typing searches saved **foods and drinks together** (each pill shows 🍽 / 💧, kcal, protein and ml; an empty box shows the favourites of both kinds). **Add on a saved item logs one of it at its own saved numbers** through the Gym Tracker (new `GYM_ACTION quickAddSaved { kind, name }`, same reqId replay protection); picking a pill chooses its kind, typing an exact name works too (a favourite wins a tie). **A name that is not saved opens the Gym Tracker's Food & drink dialog with the name filled in** (`PAL_OPEN { view:'intake', name }`) and logs nothing. The card now always shows both lines (water; calories and protein) — the mode that swapped them is gone. The confirmation popup shows only the metrics the item counts toward (calories with what is left, protein, water). Removed: `gymQuickToggleKind`, `gymQuickSetKind`, `gymQuickAmt`. `quickAddWater` / `quickAddMeal` still exist in the Gym Tracker but the launcher no longer sends them. Needs `gym-tracker.html` v2.135.
- **v11.47-T2 — reminder that did not show: cause not proven.** The reminder logic passed its clock-controlled tests (a due reminder appears, clears on logging, and re-checks each minute), so the likeliest cause is that the launcher only sees **this device's copy** of the Gym data: a reminder saved on another device or tab reaches it only after the Gym Tracker has run and pulled there. v11.48 narrows that gap: (1) the Gym frame is loaded quietly once per session, six seconds after sign-in, so it pulls the latest from the cloud (and `GYM_DATA_UPDATED` then re-checks); (2) Needs attention re-checks when another tab changes `gym_tracker_v1` (`storage` event). If it still does not show, the device the reminder was set on and the device the launcher was viewed on are what to compare. Other things that would hide it: the launcher left on another tab rather than Home, and any food or drink (of the reminder's kind) logged after (time − 30 minutes).
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, desktop badge, menu line, inline comment: v11.48. `pal-shared.js` untouched. No storage, sync or schema change.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, stub `pal-shared.js`, real Gym frame inside the launcher): **27 new checks, all passing**, plus the whole earlier suite (57 Gym, 17 launcher) re-run green and the legacy-data differential still identical. New checks: badge, title and menu line all v11.48; the row is one input plus Add; empty box lists favourites of both kinds; searching shows foods and drinks with icons and numbers; picking a saved drink and Add logs 150 kcal / 30 g / 500 ml through the Gym frame and the popup shows calories, protein and water; an exact saved food name logs that food; an unsaved name opens the Gym dialog with the name filled in and logs nothing; the card shows both lines; a `storage` event brings a due reminder up at once; the Gym frame is loaded about six seconds after sign-in and not before.
- **Not tested:** a real phone / Safari, the real `pal-shared.js` and `PalContract`, live Supabase and a second device (so the cross-device reminder path is verified only up to "the frame loads and the launcher re-checks"), a time zone other than UTC.
- **Known limitations:** unchanged from v11.47 (a reminder is an in-launcher item, not a phone notification; cleared by logging only). The background Gym load is one extra frame load per session; it can be removed by deleting `pxGymWarm()`.
- **Flagged, not changed:** **PET-155 follows PET-154**; backlog not supplied.

### v11.47 — PET-154 — Gym card counts food and drink together; food & drink reminders in Needs attention — 3 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov, with Gym Tracker v2.134 / GYM-120):** reminders to log food and drink should appear in Needs attention at the time set in the Gym Tracker's settings; the Gym card should follow the new "one intake" totals. The launcher's quick-add inputs stay as they are ("just use existing elements").
- **Gym card (display only):** the water line = drinks **plus any ml carried by foods**; the calories / protein line and bars = foods **plus any calories / protein carried by drinks**. It reads the new optional `volumeMl` (foods) and `calories` / `protein` (drinks) fields from `gym_tracker_v1`; records without them add 0, so existing data shows exactly what it did before. The food block now also shows when only drinks carried calories.
- **Needs attention — reminders (`pxGymReminders()`):** the Gym Tracker stores reminders on its water-target record (`waterTargets[].reminders = [{id, time:'HH:MM', label, kind:'any'|'food'|'drink', on}]`). The launcher works out which are due **itself, from that saved data**, rather than from a published summary: a summary is only refreshed when the Gym Tracker runs, and a reminder has to appear at 12:00 whether or not the app has been opened. A reminder is due from its time today until something of its kind is logged at or after (time − 30 minutes); it appears as an *Action required* item "Log <label>" (default "Log food or drink" / "Log food" / "Log a drink") with sub-line "Reminder for HH:MM", and opens the Gym Tracker's Food & drink dialog (`PAL_OPEN { view: 'intake' }`). Only shown when the Gym contract is present for the signed-in user (same gate as every other Gym item).
- **Refresh:** a one-minute timer and `visibilitychange` re-check, and `GYM_DATA_UPDATED` triggers a check, so logging a meal clears its reminder at once. Needs attention is only redrawn when the set of due reminders changes (`_pxGymSig`), so the box does not flicker.
- **Snooze / Ignore:** each day's reminder has its own id (`intake:<reminder id>:<date>`), so **Tomorrow / 7d / Ignore apply to that day's reminder only**; the same reminder is due again the next day. Uses the existing synced `attn_snooze` map, no schema change.
- **Quick-add confirmation popup:** a drink that carries calories / protein (e.g. a protein shake) also shows "Also counts: 150 kcal · 30 g protein"; a food that carries ml shows "Also counts: N ml toward water". The quick-add inputs, messages (`quickAddWater` / `quickAddMeal`) and the reqId replay protection are unchanged. Needs `gym-tracker.html` v2.134 for those rows (older versions simply omit them).
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, menu version line, inline comment: v11.47. `pal-shared.js` is not touched (no `?v=` change). No storage, message or sync change.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, stub `pal-shared.js`, clock fixed to 3 Nov 2026 13:30, simulated sign-in): **17 checks, all passing** — a due food reminder shows as Action required with its sub-line; one already satisfied (food at 08:20 after 07:30) is hidden; a not-yet-due reminder, an Off reminder and a 23:59 reminder are hidden; after running the clock to 15:00 the drink reminder appears with **no reload**; a food logged now clears the lunch reminder at once through `GYM_DATA_UPDATED`; a drink at 14:40 clears the 15:00 reminder (30-minute lookback) while one at 14:10 does not clear 14:50; snooze keys are `gym:intake:<id>:<date>`; Ignore hides that item for the day; on 4 Nov the same reminder is due again under a 4 Nov id; clicking the item opens the Food & drink dialog inside the real Gym Tracker frame; Gym card on new data shows 800 / 2500 ml and 650 kcal · 48 g (original launcher on the same data: 500 ml, 500 kcal · 18 g — the intended difference). **Differential run on legacy-shaped data** (no new fields): Gym card text and Needs attention box identical to v11.46.
- **Not tested:** a real phone / Safari (background timers are throttled when a tab is hidden — the `visibilitychange` re-check covers that), the real `pal-shared.js` / `PalContract` (the stub supplies the contract), live Supabase and a second device, a device time zone other than UTC (times use the device's local clock; stamps compare as absolute times), Lex's account.
- **Known limitations:** (1) a reminder is an in-launcher item, **not a phone notification** — nothing alerts you while the launcher is closed. (2) Reminders are read from this device's local copy of Gym data, so a second device shows them after the Gym Tracker has run there once and synced. (3) "Logged" is judged from the record's last-updated time, so removing one from a favourite's stepper also counts as activity for that moment. (4) A reminder is cleared by logging only; there is no "done without logging" button other than Ignore.
- **Flagged, not changed:** the Gym Tracker and launcher backlogs were not supplied, so **PET-154 follows PET-153** in this changelog (not confirmed against a backlog).

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** when matches are on, show the scores next to each player on the squad, locked-in view and the launcher card's squad view; simplify Customize layout to just the order with every element full width on mobile; for Needs attention, an option to ignore an alert or be reminded the next day; the Film card's favourites doubled on desktop. Nothing shows for a club with no match or one not started. The chips come from the summary `fantasy-football-tracker.html` v1.65 writes (new `m` on each player: fixture id, opponent, side, score, state, minutes, kick-off; **v1.65 is required for the scores**, a v1.64 summary shows the pitch as before). **Live refresh:** while any match in the summary is live (or kicks off within ten minutes / started within three hours), the launcher reads `/fixtures` through `pal-fpl-proxy` (header `x-pal-key` from `PAL_CONFIG.FF_PROXY_KEY`, forced fresh) **once a minute**, only while the page is visible and the Fantasy card is showing, and redraws the card; it uses only the fixtures named in the summary and stores nothing. Without `FF_PROXY_KEY` it simply shows what the app last wrote. ⚠ **New cross-app dependency:** the launcher now calls the FPL proxy itself (read-only, one small request a minute during live matches).

A card that is not an embedded app now **always shows** (an old "hidden" setting no longer hides it). **Phone and tablet: every card is full width** (a saved "half" pair stacks, CSS only, below 1100 px); desktop is unchanged. The launcher shortcut subtitle now reads "Order of the cards".
- **PET-151 — Needs attention:** each alert has **Tomorrow**, **7d** and **Ignore**. Tomorrow hides it for the rest of today and it returns tomorrow (the same snooze as the old "1d"); 7d as before; **Ignore** hides it until brought back — stored in the same synced `attn_snooze` map as a snooze with no end date (`9999-12-31`), no schema change. When any are ignored the list ends with **"n ignored · Show again"**, which brings them all back. On a phone the three buttons sit on their own line under the alert. **Sync:** the snooze map now carries a write time `t` on both sides and, when both have one, the newer whole map wins (so Show again can delete and another device's change is not undone by an old copy); a row written before this release falls back to the earlier merge. ⚠ Two devices changed offline: the later write wins and the other change is lost.
- ⚠ **PET-152 follow-up (deployment check T5 failed):** the desktop card still showed one row of four because the tracker's summary only held four and its saved data is no longer in `ftt_v1`; fixed in `film-tv-tracker.html` v4.4 (FTT-054), launcher code unchanged.

The tracker's own summary may only hold four, so when its saved data (`ftt_v1`, same origin) has more, the same ordering rule is applied to that; `film-tv-tracker.html` was not supplied and is unchanged.
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, the header badge, the menu version line and the inline comment read v11.45. `pal-shared.js` unchanged.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, stub `pal-shared.js`, mocked network, clock fixed to 3 Nov 2026): **60 checks, all passing** — Customize layout list, no old controls, ▲ / ▼ swap, Home order follows, saved to the layout cache, old half / hidden settings, a saved half pair full width and stacked at 390 and 820 px with the desktop grid unchanged; Needs attention Tomorrow / 7d / Ignore with their stored dates, footer and Show again, next day (clock moved on 26 h) the snoozed alert returns and ignored ones stay hidden, newer-remote and newer-local sync cases; Film favourites (summary of four plus tracker data → eight on desktop in two rows of four, four on phone and tablet, summary of eight, three, summary only); Fantasy card scores (live, finished within six hours, old and not-started hidden, opponent side, placement inside the plate, tooltip), the live read (fixtures read once, 3-1 then FT, unrelated fixtures ignored, no more reads when nothing is live, no key, hidden page), a v1.64 summary without scores; **differential run against v11.44** (summary without scores, four favourites): Fantasy card, Film card, card order / display and console errors identical. Layout screenshots checked at 390 and 1360 px.

### v11.38 — PET-142 — Universal Search — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 2 Nov):** approve Stage B3. Earlier decisions applied: Vault is not indexed; finance search covers bills and labels, not transactions; `pal-search.js` is a separate, lazily loaded file; Lex searches only her own apps.

The same keys pressed inside an app are forwarded (`PAL_SEARCH`, sent by `pal-shared.js`). `pal-search.js` is fetched on first use only; if it fails to load a message appears and nothing else is affected. `PX_APPS` gains `reading`. Apps that publish only a search list (Reading) no longer make the Needs attention box or the time tabs appear (`pxLive()`).
- **`pal-search.js` v1 (new):** grouped results per app (top 5 each, "Show all N"), every word must match (title match ranks above detail match; diacritics and case ignored), matches highlighted, date and kind on each row, up/down/Enter/Esc, focus kept inside the dialog and returned on close, `role=dialog` / `combobox` / `listbox` / `option` with `aria-activedescendant`, full-screen sheet on phones with safe-area padding, empty state listing which apps are searchable (with counts, "N of M" when an app held more than it published, and an "as of" date when stale), "No matches" state naming what was searched. Result text is inserted as text nodes, never HTML. Choosing a result opens the app and, where the app supports `PAL_OPEN`, the record.
- **Where the index lives:** apps publish rows through `PalContract.publishSearch()` into IndexedDB (`pal_x_db`, one record per app), **not localStorage** — measured first: at 64 KB per app localStorage kept only 100 of 700 gigs and 200 of 1,500 titles. Measured with realistic volumes: Gigs 700 rows / 101 KB, Film 1,500 / 165 KB, Reading 800 / 98 KB, Claims 400 / 53 KB, Bills + labels 330 / 40 KB in IndexedDB, and 21 KB in total in localStorage for the small summaries (unchanged mechanism).
- **User separation:** only records whose `userId` is the signed-in user are read; Pete-only apps are skipped for Lex; sign-out empties the index. Vault, Fortnight, Fantasy and Horizon publish no search rows.
- `pal-shared.js?v=11.38`. Version updated: `<title>`, bar badge, menu version line, inline note.
- **Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, real files, Supabase mocked):** search suite 28/28 (open/close/toggle and focus, labelled modal, empty state with counts, highlighting, venue / detail-line matches, diacritics, multi-word AND, each app's result format, no-match state, markup shown as text, arrow-key active option, Tab containment, 18,000 rows loaded from IndexedDB and searched in about 6 ms, Enter opens Gigs and the Band A record, Ctrl+K from inside an app, sign-out empties the index, Lex cannot find Pete's claim but finds her own items, failed script load); earlier suites re-run: launcher 21/21, pilot apps 23/23, B2 apps 17/17, B2 launcher 6/6, backups 30/30; all ten apps open with the same page errors as the original files. Phone screenshot reviewed.
- **Not tested:** Safari / iPhone (IndexedDB in same-origin iframes, the on-screen keyboard over the overlay), real data volumes in the live apps, VoiceOver, opening a specific record in apps other than Gigs & Trips, Gym and Film (see their entries).
- **Known limitations:** each list is only as fresh as the last time that app ran on this device (and an app must be an updated version to have published one). Reading, Claims and On Budget open the app but not a specific record. Gigs repeat occurrences are not indexed (the series is).

### v11.28 — PET-132 — "Concourse" look and feel: phone and desktop layouts, Today board — 1 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 1 Nov):** a look-and-feel refresh of the launcher in the same family as Gigs & Trips v7.109 (GIG-122) and the apps refreshed since, with its own character, **without changing functionality**. Built from the approved "Concourse" design canvas. Pete's four decisions were all the recommended option: **slim top bar with labelled tabs on desktop** (no left dock); **Today board** as a sticky right column on desktop and under the date on phone; **keep today's emoji inside the coloured tile**; **remove the pinch-zoom block**.
- **Responsive, not device-sniffing:** under 700 px = phone, 700 – 1099 px = tablet (the phone layout in a centred 560 px column), 1100 px and over = desktop. One DOM, plain CSS media queries; a `matchMedia` listener records the layout on `<html data-layout>` and keeps it current when a window is resized or a phone is turned.
- **Look:** the family palette in the existing CSS variable names (paper `#F4F0E6` / deep ink `#0E0D12`; lime `#CBF55C` on the primary action and active ring, ink on paper in light), Bricolage Grotesque for the date, titles and big figures, DM Sans for the rest (Google Fonts; system fonts offline). Follows the launcher's own light / dark setting as before. New variables for separator, accent, ring, ok / amber / bad. One colour per app, shared by the bar tile, Today line and card: Gigs `#FF6B9A`, Gym `#FF7A45`, On Budget `#7DB5FF`, Fantasy `#37C97E`, Film & TV `#8B7CFF`, Reading `#F2C14E`, Fortnight `#4FD8CB`, Claims `#FF8A6B`, Vault `#B9B5C6`, Horizon `#5EE0A0` (Film & TV and Claims no longer share a teal; Gigs is no longer violet in the bar and orange on its card). `--card-tx` gives a darker text colour per app in light.
- **Top bar:** each app icon is the existing emoji inside a 34 px tile in the app's colour, in a 44 px tap area (was 30 – 38 px). The active app wears a lime ring (ink in light). Phone: home mark + version badge, a scrolling icon row with a fade at the edge under 500 px, theme, user. Desktop: the home mark with "Apps" and the version, then labelled tabs (icon + name) with a colour underline on the active app. Nav buttons are now `<span class="nb-ic">` + `<span class="nb-lb">`; `data-target`, `title`, order and show / hide from the layout panel are unchanged.
- **Home:** a hero (weekday and time of day, the date in large type, "Pete's Apps" and "N things on the board today") and the **Today board**: up to five one-line facts — next event, today's workout (done / ill / planned), Food & Travel headroom, pages to today's reading target (follows the card's Book / Audio mode), Fortnight days done and hours. A line only appears for a card that is showing, so Lex has no On Budget or Fortnight line; tapping a line opens that app exactly as the card does (Fortnight opens its Live tab). Built from values the stat functions already work out: each calls `todaySet()`, `renderTodayBoard()` draws. **No new storage key, no new read.** Tiles: 22 px corners, coloured icon tile, larger type (the old 9 – 11 px inline sizes are lifted to 12 px by CSS, the old hex colours mapped to the theme's ok / amber / bad).
  - **Gigs & Trips:** the hero is a ticket stub (weekday / day / month on a dashed stub, name, venue · time, countdown chip) with the next three below and the clash line as a chip; same values as before.
  - **Gym:** the Mon – Sun strip is larger with the same meanings; water / nutrition bars thicker.

### v11.20 — PET-124 — Faster launch: no wait on the auth call, loading screen, idle prefetch, opt-in timeline — 18 Oct 2026

- **Why (performance):** Pete reported the apps are slow to open the first time. Code review plus headless timing (Chromium, throttled CPU and network) showed the shared JS is not the cause (about 17 KB of real code, the rest comments; parse cost about 1 ms). The launcher itself was putting a Supabase round trip in front of every launch, and an app's HTML (130 KB gzipped for Gym) was only fetched on the tap. This is Phase 1 of a phased speed plan agreed in the same conversation; principle: open from local data first, Supabase stays the master and reconciles afterwards; no sync, merge or schema behaviour changes.
- **Change (`index.html` only):**
  - **Optimistic boot:** a stored `sb_session` with more than 5 minutes of life left (`expires_at`) and a known user is used straight away; the refresh then runs in the background. A definitive rejection of the refresh token (400/401/403) still returns the user to the login screen (message "Session expired — please sign in again"), just after launch instead of before it; a network failure keeps the session. A session with under 5 minutes left, no `expires_at`, or an unknown user takes the old blocking path unchanged. The fast path waits for DOMContentLoaded first, because the old path only reached `onSignedIn()` after a network await, i.e. after the whole script had evaluated.
  - **Single-flight refresh:** `refreshLauncherSession()` now shares one in-flight request (Supabase rotates refresh tokens, so overlapping refreshes could present the same token twice). New `sbRefreshSessionEx()` reports the HTTP status; `sbRefreshSession()` kept as a wrapper.
  - **`PAL_REQUEST_SESSION`:** answered immediately when the held token has more than 5 minutes left and a refresh is already running or one finished (or the page opened) within 2 minutes; the refreshed token is broadcast to loaded frames when it lands. Otherwise (stale token, or a 401 follow-up) it refreshes first, exactly as before. Gym asks at start-up, so its first sync no longer waits for an auth round trip.
  - `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Supabase origin (hint only; the real URL still comes from `PAL_CONFIG.SB_URL`).
  - Card stats are drawn after the first paint (requestAnimationFrame + setTimeout) instead of before it.
  - "Opening <app>…" screen over an app frame that is visible but has not finished loading; cleared on the frame's load event, on leaving the frame, or after 20 s.
  - **Idle prefetch (`PREFETCH_TARGETS = ['gym','budget']`):** after the home screen is drawn and the browser is idle, the HTML of Gym and On Budget and the `pal-shared.js?v=` each one names are fetched into the HTTP cache. Nothing is executed or placed in an iframe, so no sync starts and no `loaded[...]` flag changes (quick-add readiness untouched). Skipped on Data Saver; On Budget skipped for non-Pete users; failures ignored.
  - **Opt-in `?perf=1` timeline:** small panel (Copy / Hide) with timestamped launcher marks (boot, session refresh, home shown, card stats, frame src/load, `PAL_SESSION` pings, prefetch). Absent without `?perf=1`; nothing stored. The launcher also accepts `{type:'PAL_PERF', label}` messages from apps for later phases.
- **Unchanged:** all app files, `pal-shared.js` (still `?v=10.87`), data structures, localStorage keys, sync, quick-add helpers, `ensureLoaded()`, backup/export, layout, card content.
- **Compatibility:** works with every current app version (no app change). Mixed deploy safe.
- Version: title, nav badge and DEPLOYMENT comment set to v11.20.
- Tested (Stage 1): `node --check` on all inline scripts; Playwright (real Chromium) run of the real `index.html` and real app files with Supabase mocked inside the page, 25 scenarios: fresh stored session opens without waiting for a slow auth call (auth 2 s: old launcher usable at 2.10 s, new at 0.12 s; auth 300 ms: 0.44 s vs 0.20 s); background refresh stores the new session once; under-5-minute token takes the old blocking path; 400 on background refresh returns to login and clears the session; network failure keeps the session; expired stored session plus rejected refresh shows login; no session shows login with no auth call; unknown user not trusted; session request during a running refresh answered in under 400 ms with exactly one auth call in total; session request with a stale token refreshes first; prefetch fetches Gym and On Budget (and each one's own `pal-shared.js?v=`) once each, starts no iframe, and the later Gym open is served from cache; Data Saver and non-Pete cases; loading screen shows for a cold frame and not for a warm one; no panel without `?perf=1`, panel with it, nothing stored; all nine apps open from the launcher and Home returns with no launcher errors.
- Not tested: a real phone or Safari/iOS PWA, live Supabase (token rotation behaviour against the real auth service), real GitHub Pages cache headers (the test server sent `max-age=600`, assumed to match), a second device, the quick-add flows in a browser (code unchanged).

### v11.18 — PET-122 — On Budget card quick-add reliable on first open / slow load — 18 Oct 2026

- **Why (bug):** same class of failure as the Gym card fixed in v11.17 (PET-121); the On Budget Spend / Bills quick-add shared the weak parts of the old flow.
- **Investigation (code evidence, v11.17 / On Budget v3.99):** (1) `switchTo()` sets `loaded[budget] = true` when loading *starts*, so `ensureLoaded('budget')` returned a half-loaded frame and the `OB_ACTION` message was lost (shown as a misleading "check the app before retrying"); (2) fixed 15 s load cap, 800 ms settle and 4 s reply wait, no re-send; (3) a new `reqId` on every submit, so a retry after a late save created a second entry, and the app's duplicate guard only replied "Already added" (no stored result / category); (4) the app's first `syncPull()` rebuilds `months[mk].transactions` and `bills.tx` from the merge, so an entry added while the pull was awaiting was dropped from local state until the next pull (it was never lost from the cloud, because the add pushes itself). No readiness signal existed.
- **Change (`index.html`):** new `obEnsureFrame()` (starts the load without trusting `loaded[budget]`), `obWaitReady()` (`OB_ACTION` `ping` / `OB_PONG` `ready`, every 0.5 s, up to 45 s) and a rewritten `obQuickSend()` (one fixed `reqId`, re-sent every 2 s for up to 20 s until the reply arrives). `obQuickSubmit()` uses them; the Add button shows "…" while waiting and is restored afterwards. Typed input is cleared only on a confirmed save. Messages: "did not finish loading (or needs on-budget.html v3.100) — nothing saved, your entry is still here" (no pong) vs "No confirmation from On Budget — check the app before retrying, it may have saved".
- **Unchanged:** the Gym helpers and `gymQuickSubmit()` (the Gym block is byte-identical to v11.17), shared `ensureLoaded()` (still used by the other launch paths), the confirmation popup, card display. The On Budget helpers are deliberate copies of the Gym ones rather than a shared generalisation, so Gym behaviour could not change. ⚠ Candidate shared-platform improvement: one generic ready-ping / re-send helper for all card quick-adds.
- **Compatibility:** needs `on-budget.html` v3.100. An older On Budget never answers the ping, so the card shows the not-ready message after 45 s with nothing saved and the entry kept. The old v11.17 launcher with On Budget v3.100 still works (cold-load test).
- Version: title, nav badge and DEPLOYMENT comment set to v11.18.
- Tested (Stage 1): see the On Budget v3.100 entry (shared run). Not tested: a genuinely cold load on a phone or slow network, live Supabase, a second device, the Gym card in a browser (code unchanged, verified by diff only).

### v11.17 — PET-121 — Gym card quick-add reliable on first open / slow load — 18 Oct 2026

- **Why (bug):** Pete reported quick-add failing when Gym Tracker had not been opened yet or was slow to load.
- **Root causes found:** (1) `switchTo()` sets `loaded[target] = true` when it *starts* loading, so `ensureLoaded('gym')` returned immediately for a frame still loading and the message went to a page with no listener; (2) a cold first load can exceed `ensureLoaded`'s fixed 15 s cap and its fixed 800 ms settle delay; (3) the reply wait was a fixed 4 s, and a late save followed by a retry created a duplicate; (4) the app's first cloud pull could replace its arrays after the entry was added.
- **Change (`index.html`):** `gymEnsureFrame()` starts the load itself; `gymWaitReady()` pings (`GYM_ACTION` `ping` / `GYM_PONG` `ready`) every 0.5 s for up to 45 s; `gymQuickSend()` then sends with one fixed `reqId` and re-sends every 2 s for up to 20 s until the reply arrives. The Add button shows "…" while waiting; inputs are kept if nothing was confirmed. Messages distinguish "did not finish loading / needs v2.115" (nothing saved) from "no confirmation, it may have saved".
- **Unchanged:** drink and food behaviour, popup, card display, the shared `ensureLoaded()` used by other cards.
- Version: title, nav badge and DEPLOYMENT comment set to v11.17. Needs `gym-tracker.html` v2.115.
- Tested (Stage 1): see the Gym v2.115 entry (shared run). Not tested: a genuinely cold load on a phone or slow network.

### v11.10 — PET-114 — On Budget quick-add stays on the launcher with a 5-second confirmation popup — 10 Oct 2026

- **Why:** the Food and Bills quick-add inputs on the On Budget card saved the transaction and then switched to the On Budget app. Request: just deliver the transaction, show a pop-up for 5 seconds confirming it (ideally with the new balances and what remains on the spending element), then leave the user on the launcher with the card showing the new values.
- **Change (launcher only):**
  - `obQuickSubmit()` no longer calls `switchTo('budget', …)` after a successful save; the user stays where they were.
  - New popup `#obConfirm` (`showObQuickConfirm()` / `hideObQuickConfirm()`): auto-hides after 5 s, tap to dismiss, `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"`. Title `✓ Food £4.50 · label` (or `Bills`; Food adds "(uncleared)" in manual clear mode). Food rows: Card balance (Increasing mode) or Left to spend, Headroom, Food this week £ left/over of budget. Bills rows: Cleared balance and the forecast line. The label is inserted as text, never HTML.
  - Balances are read from On Budget's `dashboardSummary` in the `on_budget_v1` localStorage envelope, which `save()` has already written before it replies. A stale-data guard ignores a summary whose `computedAt` is older than the request start (minus 1 s); the confirmation then shows without balances.
  - `refreshCardStats()` is called explicitly after success (in addition to the existing `OB_DATA_UPDATED` refresh) so the card shows the new values straight away.
- **Unchanged:** the `OB_ACTION` / `OB_QUICKADD_RESULT` message protocol; failure and `NO_ACK` handling (toasts, nothing cleared, no popup); the double-submit guard; card tap-through to the Spending and Bills tabs. `on-budget.html` is unchanged (v3.91) and `pal-shared.js?v=10.87` is unchanged. No data, storage or sync change.

### v11.03 — PET-107 — Quick-add label suggestions

- **Why:** retyping the same shop or bill name on the card is the slowest part of a quick-add. Typing in a label box now shows tap-to-fill pills of matching saved labels. Nothing shows until there is text and a match.
- **Sources (read-only, from the `on_budget_v1` localStorage key the card stats already read):** Food uses On Budget's saved label list (`data.ftLabels.items`, deleted ones skipped). Bills uses the names on its own past transactions (`data.bills.tx`), de-duplicated case-insensitively, skipping deleted and skipped entries and the generic `Spend` / `Income` fallback names. Food and Bills lists are kept separate. Re-read on each focus of a label box, so it is current without any messaging to the app.
- **Matching:** case-insensitive substring; labels that start with the typed text rank first, then most used, then most recent; at most 5 pills. Hidden when the only match is exactly what is typed, when the box is cleared, on blur, and after a successful save.
- **Picking:** tapping a pill fills the label (pill taps do not steal keyboard focus) and moves focus to the amount if it is empty, otherwise leaves it on the label. It does not open the app or save. Labels are inserted as text, never HTML.
- **Failure behaviour:** no key, unreadable JSON or no matches means no pills and no error; typing and saving work exactly as in v11.02.
- Launcher-only: `on-budget.html` stays v3.83, no data, sync or message-protocol change. Version: title, nav badge and DEPLOYMENT comment set to v11.03.
- ⚠ Suggestions come from this device's local copy, so a fresh device shows none until On Budget has loaded and synced once; v3.82's local cache trim can also briefly empty them until the next pull. Bills suggestions can include recurring-bill names, since those transactions carry names too.
- Tested (headless jsdom, real `index.html`): no pills before typing, no data / corrupt data, Bills de-duplication and ranking, deleted/skipped/generic exclusions, Food-only labels not leaking into Bills, Food list and deleted exclusion, exact-match hiding, pick behaviour and focus, no app open on pick, HTML-safe rendering, blur hide, v11.02 rows intact. ### v11.02 — PET-106 — On Budget card: inline Food / Bills quick-add inputs

- **Why:** the card's two launch buttons (+ Food Spend, + Bills Spend) opened On Budget and then a sheet, so adding a spend meant launch, wait, type, save. They are replaced by two inline rows on the card, **Food** and **Bills**, each with an amount, an optional label and an **Add** button. Typing the amount and pressing Add (or Enter / the keyboard's Done) saves the entry and opens On Budget.
- **How it works:** the launcher posts `{ type:'OB_ACTION', action:'quickAddFood' | 'quickAddBills', amount, label, reqId }` to the On Budget iframe and waits up to 4 s for `OB_QUICKADD_RESULT`. On Budget does the save itself (see On Budget v3.83), so there is no second write path in the launcher, and Supabase sync, balance maths and label history stay the app's. Only on `ok:true` are the inputs cleared and the app opened.
- **Safety:** if there is no reply (for example an older `on-budget.html` that ignores the action) nothing is cleared, a toast says there was no confirmation and to check the app before retrying, and the row is re-enabled. The row is disabled while a save is in flight, so a double tap cannot add twice; the app also ignores a repeated `reqId`.
- **Amount entry:** same pence-first entry as On Budget's sheets (type `450` for £4.50), so muscle memory is identical. Inputs are 16 px (no iOS focus zoom). Tapping or typing in the inputs does not trigger the card's own tap-to-open.
- **Defaults:** Food saves as the Food category, dated today. Bills saves as an outgoing, cleared transaction dated today (the Add transaction sheet's own defaults). Travel/Other, income, uncleared and "Not today?" still need the sheets. The card's two data columns still link to the Spending / Bills tabs (`launchOBAction`, unchanged). `launchOBAddSpend()` is no longer called by the card but is left in place.
- ⚠ **Needs `on-budget.html` v3.83.** Upload both files together.
- Version: title, nav badge and DEPLOYMENT comment set to v11.02. `pal-shared.js?v=10.87` deliberately unchanged (no shared-code change).
- Tested (headless jsdom, real `index.html`, real `on-budget.html` v3.83 in the launcher's iframe, real `pal-shared.js` fetched from the repo): penny formatting, empty-amount block, Food and Bills end-to-end saves with correct entry values and Bills balance, app opens on the right tab, inputs cleared on success, double-submit guard, card tap suppression, and an old v3.82 app in the iframe (nothing saved, input preserved, warning toast, launcher stays on home). Test harness patched jsdom's `postMessage` to supply `origin`/`source` as browsers do. Not tested: a real browser, a phone keyboard (layout, Enter/Done key, iOS zoom), live Supabase sync of the new entry, a second device, Lex's account (the card is pete-only).

### v10.96 — PET-101 — Layout changes now sync between devices

- Bug: layout edits on one device never reached another.
- Root cause: `loadLayoutConfig()` / `saveLayoutConfig()` only talk to Supabase when `PalSync.hasSession()` is true, but the launcher never passed its own `sbSession` to PalSync, so layout only lived in each device's `pal_layout_cache`.
- Fix:
  - New `feedPalSyncSession()` calls `PalSync.setSession()` on sign-in (before `applyUserView()` → `loadLayoutConfig()`), on each token refresh, and clears it on lock.
  - New `pal_layout_dirty` localStorage flag: an unconfirmed local edit wins over the cloud copy on load and is re-pushed.
  - Cloud read extracted to `syncLayoutFromCloud()`, also run on `visibilitychange` (skipped while the layout panel is open).
  - Publishes the local layout if the cloud has no row yet; save failures report `PalSync.errorHint` (401/403/404); not signed in reports "Saved on this device only".
- First use: `pal_layout` was empty, so the first device to open v10.96 publishes its layout.
- Requires the `pal_layout` table and RLS from v10.89. `pal-shared.js` unchanged (`?v=10.87` kept).
- Tested: two-device simulation against a fake Supabase with the real pal-shared.js; the same suite fails all cloud checks on v10.95. Not tested: real browser/Supabase, physical phone, Lex's view.

Runs standalone (launcher) and nested inside Fortnight Tracker's Claims tab (FT-041, FT-062). ⚠ The changelog had no section for this app before this entry: the uploaded file was v2.20 (CLA-017), and CLA-001 – CLA-017 live only in the file's inline comments, which were not turned into changelog entries here.

The "Expected payment date" prompt now shows and accepts dd/mm/yy or dd/mm/yyyy (ISO still accepted) through `PalShared.parseDate`; the stored value is still ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. The weekday no longer appears in these dates.
