### v2.26 — CLA-023 — Launcher quick-add (CT_ACTION) — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete):** add a claim from the launcher on a card of its own (Claims also lives inside Fortnight).
- **What changed:** the app now answers `CT_ACTION` messages: `ping` (replies `CT_PONG {ready, version}`; ready = first cloud pull settled), `quickAddExpense {amount, category, reason, reqId}` and `quickAddMileage {tripId, reqId}`. They build the same entries as `addExpense()` / `addMileage()` (today's date, unclaimed; a standard trip uses its saved miles and deduction, no passengers), save through `mutateEntry()` and reply `CT_QUICKADD_RESULT {reqId, ok, msg, kind, amount, label, toClaim}`. Rejected: non-positive or over £100,000 amounts, unknown category, empty reason, unknown trip. A repeated `reqId` replays the stored reply and never saves twice.
- **Data/sync:** none new; entries are the existing shape, so backup/import and the Fortnight-embedded copy are unaffected.
- ⚠ **Known limitation:** the launcher card saves through the standalone Claims frame. If Fortnight's nested Claims tab is also open in the same session its in-memory list is not refreshed until it re-pulls; the entry is already in the cloud and local storage.
- Tested (headless Chromium, real launcher + real app in its iframe, mocked Supabase): expense and mileage saved with correct fields, cloud write sent, duplicate request id saved once, bad category / negative amount / unknown trip refused; older claims suites updated for the new version. Not tested: a phone, a second device, the nested Fortnight copy open at the same time.

### v2.25 — CLA-022 — Payment date corrected; Submit Day setting; version visible — 2 Nov 2026

- **Report (Pete, deployment check of v2.24):** (T6) a claim marked claimed on 27 Oct, to go in the 6 Nov submission, showed as overdue; (T3) wants the claim (submission) date settable in Settings and shown on a card in the app; (T1) could not see the version on desktop or phone.
- **Cause (T6) — my mistake in v2.24:** the expected payment was computed from the month the entry was *marked claimed* (27 Oct → pay day 28 Oct), but a claim is paid in the payroll of the month of the **submission that picks it up** (marked 27 Oct → submitted 6 Nov → paid 27 Nov). **Fix:** `defaultPayDate()` = pay day (setting) in the month of the first submission on or after the day it was marked claimed (`submissionFor()` / `payDateForSubmission()`); weekends still move back to Friday. A manually set expected date is unchanged. Batches that v2.24 showed as past due because of the old rule recover on their own.
- **Submit Day (T3):** new optional setting `submitDay` (default 6, weekends move back to Friday; Settings › Submit Day) now drives "Next submission" (previously a fixed 6th in `nextSubmissionDate()`). The existing hero line "Next submission: <date> · in N days" now also shows "Paid in that month's payroll · expected <date>". `submitDay` is copied through the same three load sites as `payDay` (flat migration, envelope load, JSON import) so it survives reload and old backups.
- **Version (T1):** the page header is hidden when Claim Tracker is nested in Fortnight Tracker (`?embedded=ft`), so the version now also appears in **Sync & Backup › Version** and at the foot of **Settings**.
- Version updated: `<title>`, header badge, rail footer, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=2.25`.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium): claimed 27 Oct → expected Fri 27 Nov and not past due; Submit Day 10; next submission follows the setting; hero shows the expected payment; drawer and Settings show v2.25; settings survive reload; old backup imports with defaults; all v2.24 checks re-run (38/38). Not tested: live Supabase sync of `submitDay` between devices.

### v2.24 — CLA-021 — Submitted / Paid tracking and expected payment date — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 2 Nov; Stage C):** better status tracking and expected reimbursement dates; claims are normally paid in **the same month's payroll**.
- **Model (additive, optional):** on a claimed entry `paid_date` (ISO) and `expected_pay_date` (ISO, only when the default is overridden); one optional setting `payDay` (default 28). Status is derived per **claim batch** (entries marked claimed together share `claimed_date`): *Submitted* (no `paid_date`) or *Paid*. Existing entries, backups and cloud rows are unchanged and load as *Submitted* with a default expected date.
- **Expected date rule:** the pay day in the month of submission, moved back to the previous Friday if it is a weekend; if that is already before the submission date it rolls to the next month. **The default pay day 28 is an assumption — change it in Settings › Pay Day.** An "Expected date" button sets a date for one batch (empty = back to the default).
- **UI:** each "Claimed …" banner shows `Submitted · expected <date>` (red "past due" after it) or `Paid <date>`, with **Mark paid** / **Undo paid** and **Expected date** buttons. Unclaiming an entry clears its payment fields.
- **Launcher (existing contract):** a batch submitted in the last 60 days and past its expected date gives an *Action required* item "Claim payment past due" (older unpaid batches only show "Submitted" in the app, so the first load does not alert for every historic batch); an expected payment within 30 days appears in the 7 / 30-day lists as "Claim payment expected" (labelled expected, never merged into On Budget). Summary gains `awaitingPayment`. Search subtitle shows submitted / paid.
- **Compatibility:** the local-load copy of settings only copied known fields, so `payDay` was added to the three copy sites (flat-file migration, envelope load, JSON import); cloud settings replace the whole object so `payDay` travels. Export/import and backups carry the new fields; an old backup imports with the default.
- Version updated: `<title>`, header badge, rail footer, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=2.24`.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, mocked Supabase): default date rules (weekend, roll-over, pay day 15); past-due vs 60-day cut-off; Mark paid / Undo paid stamp and clear both entries of a batch; override and invalid date; unclaim clears fields; Pay Day survives reload; export carries fields; an old backup imports with pay day 28; launcher attention / upcoming / summary values; phone screenshot reviewed. Not tested: live Supabase sync of the new fields between two devices, Claim Tracker nested inside Fortnight Tracker.

# Fantasy Football Tracker

`fantasy-football-tracker.html`. The source states the same entries are kept in the changelog comment at the top of the app's script block. Versions are mirrored in five places: `<title>`, the nav badge (`#navVer`), `pal-shared.js?v=`, the `FF_VERSION` constant, and the export backup `appVersion` (which reads `FF_VERSION` from v1.48).

Supabase tables used: `ff_settings`, `ff_squad_cache`, `ff_score_history`, `ff_advice_cache`, `ff_transfer_log`, `ff_external_check`, `ff_manual_lineup`. Live data comes through the `pal-fpl-proxy` Edge Function.

### v1.66 — FF-040 — Injured and unavailable players marked clearly on every pitch and on the launcher card — 3 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** on any update from FPL, make sure injured players are marked on the squad view, including in the launcher card.
- **Finding:** the pitch only had a 12 px dot on the shirt (and none for status `n`), the list views had the 🚑 / 🩹 note, and the launcher summary carried no availability at all, so the launcher card could never show an injury.
- **New helper `ffAvail(el)`** (one source for everything): `null` for a fit player; otherwise level `out` (status `i`, `s`, `u`, `n`, or doubtful with 25% or less: the app's existing `isEffectivelyUnavailable` gate) or `doubt`, a short word ("Injured", "Susp.", "Out", "75%", "Doubt") and the full wording. A fit player with only news text is left unmarked on the pitch, as before (the list views still show 🩹).
- **Pitches (Squad, Next Week, Advice squads, anywhere `ppHtml` is used):** the dot becomes a 16 px badge on the shirt (red **+**, amber **!**) and the plate gets a short chip under the name; the tooltip / aria-label carry the full wording and FPL news. ⚠ A doubtful player with 25% or less now shows red (as "out"), where the old dot was amber for every doubtful player.
- **Launcher summary `ff_locked_card`:** each player who is not fully fit gains an additive `a` (`lv`, `s` FPL status, `c` chance of playing, `w` short word, `t` news up to 90 characters). Same key, same `v: 1`; fit players carry no `a`; older launchers ignore it. Launcher v11.52 draws it.
- **Following FPL's updates:** every path that loads squad data (Refresh from FPL, the automatic refresh after an app update, the synced copy, the cached copy at open) already re-renders Next Week, which republishes the summary, and the launcher is told only when the content changed. A squad refresh now also replaces the session's full player list (`_allPlayersCache`) from the same fresh bootstrap, so the status of a player brought in by a planned transfer is current too (it used to stay as first fetched for the whole session).
- **Not touched:** `ff_squad_cache`, `ff_manual_lineup` and Supabase sync, backups, import / export, Advice logic and prompts, transfers, the proxy. No storage key or table change.
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, `#navVer`, `FF_VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=1.66`, header comment. ⚠ Bumping `FF_VERSION` makes each device auto-refresh its squad cache once on first open (existing behaviour), which is also what writes the first summary with `a`.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium at 390 px, stub `pal-shared.js`, the real file; JS syntax check): **16 checks, all passing** — `ffAvail` for fit, fit-with-news, injured, suspended, unavailable, `n`, doubtful 75% / 25% / no chance; pitch badges and chips and their tooltips; news text escaped; the summary carries `a` only for unfit players (13 fit players carry none) and is rewritten when FPL changes a status (recovered player drops out, newly injured player appears, news cut to 90 characters); no page errors; no sideways scroll; screenshot checked.
- **Not tested:** the live FPL feed through the real proxy (real status and news values), Supabase sync, Safari / Firefox, a real phone, a second device, the app inside the launcher's iframe, the full Squad / Next Week / Advice tabs with a real squad (the pitch renderer and the summary writer were run on their own against the real file), earlier suites v1.62 / v1.61 / v1.59 / v1.58 (not supplied this time).
- **Known limitations:** (1) FPL status is as of the last squad refresh; the per-minute match tick does not re-read player data. (2) A fit player with news only is not marked on the pitch. (3) The launcher card only updates when the app has been opened (it cannot call FPL itself).

### v1.65 — FF-039 — Live match scores next to each player (Squad, locked-in, launcher summary) — 3 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** when matches are on, show the scores next to each player on the squad, the locked-in view and the launcher card's squad view. Read as the **score of the player's club match** (players' points were already shown).
- **Squad and Next Week (locked-in) pitches and the Next Week list cards:** each player of a club with a match on shows a chip under his name — **"● 2-1 AVL"** live (red), **"FT 3-0 BRE"** finished — coloured good / bad for his position as in the This week box. The Squad tab (that gameweek's own squad) keeps the score all week; the locked-in view (next gameweek's squad) shows a finished score only for six hours after kick-off, so old results do not linger. No chip for a club with no match or one not started. The Squad list view already had the This week box.
- **Live refresh:** while any match is live (or kicks off within ten minutes / started within three hours) and the page is visible, the app re-reads `/fixtures` once a minute (`x-pal-force-fresh`, the proxy's normal route) and updates the chips **in place** (no re-render: scroll, selection and open sheets untouched), then rewrites the launcher summary. Nothing is stored beyond what is already stored.
- **`buildMatchStateByTeam`** also records the fixture id (`fid`) and, in a double gameweek, now prefers the live match, else the latest started, else the first (it used to keep the last fixture). Other readers of the match state are unaffected.
- **Launcher summary `ff_locked_card`:** each player gains an additive `m` (`f` fixture id, `n` opponent code, `h` home, `s` / `o` own / opponent score, `st` 0 not started / 1 live / 2 full time, `mn` minutes, `k` kick-off) when his club has a match in the current gameweek; launcher v11.45 shows it and keeps it live. Same key, same version field, nothing else changed (older launchers ignore the extra field).
- **Not touched:** `ff_squad_cache`, `ff_manual_lineup` and Supabase sync, backups, Advice, prompts, transfers. No storage key, table or proxy change.
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, `#navVer`, `FF_VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=1.65`, header comment.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, stub `pal-shared.js`, mocked `pal-fpl-proxy` with one live, two recently / long finished, one not-started and several blank clubs; clock fixed): **26 checks, all passing** — Squad pitch chips (live, opposite-side view, finished all week, none where no match), colour by outcome and position, placement inside the plate; Next Week pitch (live shown, finished within six hours shown, older hidden) and list cards; opponent chips unchanged beside the score; launcher summary `m` values (live, finished, not started, absent for blank clubs) with all v1.64 fields kept; live tick (one read, chips updated in place without re-render, Next Week and summary follow, FT, no read when nothing is live, a match about to start is polled and appears when it begins, no read on a hidden page); double-gameweek choice; phone 390 no sideways scroll. **Earlier suites re-run against v1.65: v1.62 50/50, v1.61 18/18, v1.59 31/31, v1.58 69/69** (version strings updated). **Differential run against v1.64** (no live matches): Advice body, Recommended team, External tab, prompt, gameweek records, stored checks, localStorage keys, backup and console errors identical; the Squad and Next Week bodies differ only by the new (empty) chip element in each plate.
- **Not tested:** the live FPL feed through the real proxy (including how fast it reflects goals), Safari / Firefox, a real phone, a second device, the app inside the launcher's iframe.
- **Known limitations:** (1) chips show the match score, not the player's own live points (points still update on a refresh). (2) The six-hour window uses kick-off, not the final whistle. (3) The per-minute read stops when the page is hidden, so scores can lag after returning until the next tick. (4) A club with two matches on the same day shows the live one, else the latest started.

### v1.62 — FF-036 — Simple reasoned lineup advice from each AI, votes by position beside your locked-in squad, and accept-into-locked-in — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 2 Nov):** instead of the consensus view, show the votes from each AI; does the advice give reasons to keep or remove; very simple advice from the AI on which players to remove and what to replace them with, with reasons, so a tap on any player gives a very clear view of any AI's reasons for removal or bringing in (change the prompt and JSON collection if needed); show my current locked-in squad in the votes for each position; let me tap a player who disagrees with my locked-in squad and accept the advice so it updates my locked-in squad. (Deployment check of v1.61 not yet returned.)
- **Prompt and JSON (schemaVersion 7):** the reply schema gains **`lineupChanges`** — a list of swaps, each `outId / outName` (a player currently starting in my squad), `inId / inName` (a player currently on my bench), a one-sentence `reason` (under 200 characters) and `confidence` — and **`captainReason`**. New step 7c tells the AI the swaps must reproduce `recommendedXI.starting` exactly from my current XI, may be an empty array, and must not be padded. The export payload gains `currentStartingXI` and `currentBench` (names) and its `schemaVersion` is 7. The importer accepts and sanitises the new fields (non-object entries dropped; the field is simply absent on an older reply, and `lineupChanges: []` is kept as "no changes"; a reply containing only `lineupChanges` is no longer rejected as having no expected fields). **Older (v6) replies still import and work**: their swaps are worked out from the difference between their XI and your locked-in XI (same-position pairs first), with the reason taken from their notes on either player or their overall reasoning and labelled "from its notes — no specific reason given". The External tab's detailed body shows the swaps, reasons and captain reason.
- **Votes by position (replaces the Consensus heading):** a grid per position (GK / DEF / MID / FWD): one row per squad player (a fixture tag under his name); column **You** = your locked-in team (✓ starting, GK / B1–B3 bench order) then one column per source (App, Claude, GPT, Gemini): ✓ starts, · benches, **OUT** (red) = that source wants him taken out of your XI, **IN** (green) = wants him brought in, C / V = its captain / vice pick. Rows where any source disagrees with you have an amber border and sort first; each position header shows how many You and each source start; a captain / vice-captain row shows yours against each source's (amber where different). Source chips still switch a source in or out. Tapping a row opens the player sheet. Below the grid, **"Suggested changes to your locked-in team"** lists each player any source wants out ("3 of 4 say remove"), with each source's replacement (price, position, opponent, confidence), the **reason** and an Accept button, and who keeps him. The overlay pitch, Where to choose and the position detail (previous Consensus content) move into a collapsed **"Overlay pitch, where to choose and position detail"** section.
- **Each AI sheet** now opens with the same simple **"Suggested changes to your locked-in team"** (OUT → IN, reason, confidence, the incoming player's opponent, Accept) or "would change nothing", replacing the earlier IN / OUT line; the pitch and list follow as before.
- **Tapping a player (pitch, bench strip or votes row)** now always compares with **your locked-in team**: "Advice on X", a summary line (Remove: … · Keep: … for a starter; Bring in: … · Leave on the bench: … for a bench player), then one card per source: Keep / Remove / Bring in / Leave, "Replace with Y" or "Bring in for Z" with price, opponent, confidence, **"Why:" the reason**, the AI's notes on both players (fitness, start likelihood, confidence, sources), its captain reason and any transfer-out advice. The previous per-sheet comparison bases (app XI / that AI's XI) are removed in favour of this one clear basis.
- **Accept & lock in:** each swap has a two-tap button (the first arms it — "Tap again to lock in", re-sets after 6 s — the second applies it) that uses the **existing Next Week code**: `substitutePlayer` (same rules: a goalkeeper only for the bench goalkeeper, legal formation, the armband moves with a substituted captain), `persistManualLineup`, then `lockInSquad` (refreshes the lock-in time, the Gameweek-performance record and re-runs Advice). A tap on a captain / vice pick has "Accept: make him captain / vice-captain & lock in" (`setManualCaptain` / `setManualViceCaptain`). **Refused with a plain message** when: there are unsaved Next Week changes (lock them in or reset first), the planning gameweek's deadline has passed, the swap is illegal, or there is no squad / analysis yet. A confirmation toast reminds you to make the same change in the FPL app. If the squad was never locked in, accepting locks it in (the draft is what Advice was using). No new storage key or table: the existing `ff_manual_lineup` record is what changes.

### v1.61 — FF-035 — Advice squads always show the team each player plays next; double gameweeks and blank gameweeks handled — 2 Nov 2026

- **Report (Pete, 2 Nov):** "In the advice squad it is not always showing the teams they are playing." (Deployment check of v1.60 not yet returned.)
- **Cause:** (1) the Advice tab has no Pts / Next / £ switch and shows points, so since v1.33 only the captain and vice (v1.59) showed an opponent; every other plate showed none. (2) `buildNextFixtureByTeam` stored one fixture per team, so in a **double gameweek the second fixture overwrote the first** (only one was ever shown, and which one depended on fixture order). (3) A team with **no fixture** showed a bare dash.
- **Fix:** every plate on the app's Recommended team, each AI sheet and the Consensus (starters and bench strips) now shows the opponent chip(s) under the name; the list views show a "vs / @ opponent (H/A) · FDR" line on every card (including the app's bench cards and the Consensus's benched-by-everyone cards). A team with no game that gameweek shows **"No fixture"** on Advice plates. Fixtures: the first fixture keeps the existing fields; further ones are recorded in an optional **`also`** array (absent for a single game), and the plates, `fixtureLineHtml` ("vs AVL (H) · FDR 4/5 & vs TOT (H) · …"), the player-sheet replacement blocks and Where to choose all show every fixture. The Advice plates' Pts line still shows. `pal_x_fantasy`, backups and the export prompt are unchanged.
- **Other tabs:** Squad and Next Week plates still follow their own Pts / Next / £ setting and keep their dash for "no fixture"; they do now show a second chip in a double gameweek (same function). Squad caches written by an older version are rebuilt automatically on open (app version changed, existing mechanism), which is when `also` appears. No stored-data change otherwise.
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, `#navVer`, `FF_VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=1.61` (file itself unchanged), header comment.
- **Launcher:** `index.html` not supplied and not changed; nothing it reads changed.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, stub `pal-shared.js`, mocked `pal-fpl-proxy` with one team blank and one team double that gameweek): **v1.61 suite 18 checks all passing** — all 15 plates (pitch and bench strip) show an opponent or "No fixture" on the app team, Claude sheet, Gemini sheet and Consensus, positioned below the name; the blank team says "No fixture" and the double team shows two chips; single-game teams show one; the fixture map has `also` only for the double team; every list card in the app team (bench included), an AI sheet and the Consensus has the opponent line and the double team shows both joined by "&"; player sheet advice and Where to choose still work; Squad plates still hide the opponent in Pts mode; Next Week keeps its dash; phone 390 has no sideways scroll and plates stay in the pitch with two chips. **Earlier suites re-run: v1.60 23/23, v1.59 31/31, v1.58 69/69** (the C/V-only expectations in v1.59 were updated to "every plate"). **Differential run against v1.60:** Squad and Next Week bodies, External tab list, prompt, gameweek records, stored checks, localStorage keys, backup and console errors identical; the only difference is the opponent line now present on the app team's list cards.
- **Not tested:** a real double / blank gameweek from the live FPL feed (the mock reproduces the shape), Safari / Firefox, a second device, the app in the launcher's iframe.
- **Known limitations:** (1) two chips make a plate one line taller; on a phone the chips stack. (2) A postponed or rearranged fixture follows FPL's fixture data: FPL moves it to a later gameweek, so it shows "No fixture" until then. (3) The first fixture is the first in FPL's fixture order, not necessarily the earliest kick-off.

### v1.60 — FF-034 — Tapping a player on a proposed squad shows what every source says, and who it would bench / bring in — 2 Nov 2026

- **Deployment check of v1.59 (Pete, 2 Nov):** all tests passed — v1.59 verified. **New request in the same message:** in the Recommended and Consensus team, tapping a player should bring up all the advice from the different AIs and, where there is advice to bench him and bring in another player, show that player and the advice too.
- **Change:** a tap on a pitch plate in the app's Recommended team, any AI sheet or the Consensus pitch (including the bench strip) adds **"What each source says"** at the top of the player sheet, above the stats. One card per source (App, then each current AI reply): whether it **starts or benches** him; the source's own note on him (fitness, start likelihood and confidence badges, summary, sources; for the App its HOLD / MONITOR / SELL decision and reasons); a C / V chip if it picks him as captain / vice; and any **transfer-out advice** naming him (replacement, free or −4 hit, confidence, reason). Where a source benches him, a **"Brings in"** block shows each player it starts who is not in the comparison XI (same position first; if none, flagged "formation change"; up to three) with price, position, next opponent and difficulty, injury status and news, and **that same source's note on him**. Where a source would start a player who is not in the comparison XI, an **"Instead of"** block shows who it drops. Tapping the replacement's name opens his sheet the same way.
- **What it is compared with:** the XI the tap came from — the app's recommended XI (Recommended team), that AI's XI (an AI sheet; the sheet says so), or **your locked-in team** (Consensus, matching its + / − marks). Only replies for the current planning gameweek are used. With no current AI reply there is no section. Taps from the Squad or Next Week tabs are unchanged.
- **Note on existing behaviour surfaced by testing:** the app's own XI already benches a player when an AI gives a confident "unlikely to start / injured" flag, so after importing such a reply the app card may itself say "Benches him".
- **Code touched:** `ppTap` records the tap's base, `openPlayerDetail` injects the section before `.pd-stats` for that one call; new FF-034 block (`tvPlayerAdviceHtml` and helpers) wrapped in try/catch so a fault cannot stop the sheet opening. `playerDetailHtml` unchanged. **No data, storage key, Supabase table, backup, proxy, export-prompt or launcher-contract change.**

### v1.59 — FF-033 — Captain / vice-captain always visible with their opponent; Consensus becomes an overlay with a "Where to choose" block — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 2 Nov):** on proposed squads make the captain and vice-captain visible with their opponent below them; and a way to overlay the squads from the different AIs to see where to make a choice.
- **Captain / vice-captain (app Recommended team, every AI sheet, Consensus):** always badged **C** / **V** on the pitch, and the next opponent with its difficulty colour sits directly under the player whatever the Pts / Next / £ label setting is (other players still follow the setting; in Next mode there is still one opponent line per plate). In the list views the C / V cards carry a C / V tag and a "vs / @ opponent (H/A) · FDR" line. The app's own Recommended team previously showed no C / V at all; it now shows the app's captain and vice pick (the algorithm's suggestion, as in "Captain pick").
- **Consensus overlay:** each source has a colour (App = accent, Claude orange, ChatGPT green, Gemini blue, Other purple). Every starter plate carries **one dot per source** (filled = that source starts him) beside the existing green / amber ring and vote count; each source's captain / vice pick is lettered **C / V in its colour** under the player, and every captain / vice candidate shows its opponent. The source chips at the top are **switches**: click one to leave that source out of the comparison and everything (rings, votes, shape, rows) recomputes; at least two must stay on (otherwise a prompt says so); switch state is in memory only.
- **"Where to choose":** under the pitch, each contested player (grouped by position, with how many places that position has to fill, e.g. "pick 0–1 of these") with a chip per source (✓ starts / ✗ benches, in the source's colour), next opponent and FDR, expected points (ep_next) and any injury / news line; then each captain candidate with who names him captain or vice, his opponent and expected points. The existing shape / position / captain / vice / transfer rows remain.

### v1.58 — FF-032 — Advice: External review panel on the right (desktop), a team sheet per AI, and a Consensus sheet — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 2 Nov):** on desktop, put the external prompt and the advice copy/paste on the right of Advice instead of a separate tab, as a collapsed section; show each imported AI's advice as a collapsible recommended team like the app's own (app + each AI = up to four team sheets); add a fifth that shows where they all agree and which positions or players are in disagreement; give each squad view a collapsed section holding that AI's detailed advice.
- **Desktop (≥ 1100 px):** the **External tab is hidden**. Its two cards (Review session, External team news check: generate / copy / download / paste-and-import) move into a **collapsed "External review — prompt & import" section** in a right-hand column of Advice (sticky, scrolls on its own, same 2-column pattern as Next Week). The same DOM nodes are moved, not cloned, so every id, handler and typed text is preserved. `switchTab('external')` (including **Get External Review**) on desktop lands on Advice and opens the panel. Resizing across 1100 px moves the tools back and forth; resizing to desktop while on the External tab switches to Advice. **Phone and tablet are unchanged** (External tab, bottom bar). The Advice body's old two-column flow is now a single column on desktop to make room for the panel and the pitches.
- **A team sheet per AI:** under the app's own *Recommended team*, one collapsible **Recommended team — Claude / ChatGPT / Gemini / Other AI** per import, in that order. Each is drawn with the same pitch / list renderer as the app's own team (so the Pitch / List toggle works), from the AI's starting XI, bench order and captain / vice (names resolved to your 15 squad players with the existing `resolveNameToId`). Header chips: gameweek, shape, age; a Delete button. Inside: what differs from your locked-in team (IN / OUT, + / − marks), captain, transfer verdict, and a **collapsed "Detailed advice from …"** section holding everything the External tab list shows (squad basis, per-player news, key updates, XI reasoning, transfer recommendation, notes). Warnings for: a reply for another gameweek (not drawn, not used), a reply with no XI, names that could not be matched, and an illegal shape. Default state: AI sheets and their detail collapsed, Consensus open; open / closed state is kept across re-analysis (in memory only).
- **Consensus team (the fifth view):** compares the app's recommended XI with every AI sheet that is current and fully matched (11 starters). One pitch / list of every player any source starts: **green ring** = all start him, **amber ring** with votes (e.g. 2/3) = split, faded bench strip = nobody starts him, + / − = a unanimous call that differs from your locked-in XI. Summary chips ("9 of 11 agreed", "2 places in dispute between 3 players"), then rows for **shape** (each source's formation, flagged if they differ), **each position** (agreed names, split names with votes, flagged where sources start different numbers), **captain**, **vice-captain** and **transfer verdict** (each source's pick, flagged agree / differ). Sources left out are listed ("Not compared: …"). With no imports it shows a one-line hint; with the app alone nothing is compared.
- **Code touched:** new FF-032 block before `renderAdvice` (`externalTeamViewsHtml` and helpers; wrapped in try/catch so a fault cannot stop Advice rendering); `renderAdvice` stores its data and inserts `#extTeamViews` after Recommended team; the per-AI body of `renderExternalChecksSection` extracted unchanged into `externalCheckBodyHtml` (shared by the External tab list and the sheets); `refreshExternalTeamViews()` called after import, delete, cache load and remote pull; `applyLayout` / `switchTab` extended (`placeExternalTools`, `openExtPanel`); `ppHtml` / `ppPlateHtml` / `pitchBoardHtml` gain optional `vclass` / `vote` / `benchPlain` (no effect unless set). **No data, storage key, Supabase table, backup, proxy, export-prompt or launcher-contract change.**
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, `FF_VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=1.58` (file itself unchanged), header comment — and the nav badge `#navVer`, which ⚠ **still read v1.56 in v1.57** (pre-existing drift, corrected here). The export backup `appVersion` reads `FF_VERSION`.
- **Launcher:** `index.html` was not supplied and is **not changed**. Nothing it reads changed (`pal_x_fantasy` contract, `ff_squad_cache` summary, `FF_DATA_UPDATED`, app name / file / theme message).
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, stub `pal-shared.js`, mocked `pal-fpl-proxy` with a 15-man squad, clock fixed to 3 Nov 2026): **69 checks, all passing** — desktop 1360: External tab hidden, panel right of the advice column and collapsed, tools inside it, `switchTab('external')` and Get External Review open it, prompt generated in the panel; imports from three AIs give sheets in order claude, chatgpt, gemini then consensus; Claude's pitch has exactly its 11 starters (names such as "Cole Palmer" / "Anthony Gordon" resolved) and its bench in its order, IN / OUT and C / V marks correct, detail collapsed then shows key updates, news, reasoning and notes, Pitch / List toggle, open state survives re-analysis; consensus agreed / split / benched sets equal an independent calculation (9 agreed, 3 split with votes 3/4, 3/4, 2/4, 3 benched), shape, position, captain and transfer rows flag the differences, delete recomputes it; edge cases (stale gameweek, unmatched name, reply with no XI); reload rebuilds the sheets from saved data; phone 390 and tablet 820 keep the External tab with prompt, import and all three checks, Advice has no sideways scroll; resize phone ↔ desktop keeps typed text; player sheet opens from a consensus plate; versions agree. **Differential run against v1.57 (same scripted workflow, phone width):** Squad and Next Week bodies, the app's Recommended team, the rest of the Advice body, the External tab list, the generated prompt, saved gameweek records, stored external checks, localStorage keys, the backup file and the console errors are identical.

### v1.56 — FF-028, FF-029, FF-030

- **FF-028 — Formation picker for the best teams.** The *Best overall scoring XI* and *Best squad within the FPL budget* sections each get a **Formation** row: **Auto (best)** (unchanged behaviour) or 3-4-3, 3-5-2, 4-3-3, 4-4-2, 4-5-1, 5-2-3, 5-3-2, 5-4-1. It combines with the existing Overall / GW n toggle, so "best GW n 4-4-2" is the 11 highest scorers of the current gameweek in that shape. Best XI: the best GK plus the top *d / m / f* outfielders by the ranked points. Best squad: the same exact solver restricted to the chosen formation (`builderRelaxed` / `builderBestSquad` take an optional formation), and the XI shown from that squad is built in the same shape. Preference `ff_builder_formation` (JSON `{xi, squad}`, unscoped display pref, not in backup), like `ff_builder_scope`. Card intro text updated.
- **FF-029 — Free Hit: keep the squad from before it.** The squad cache now stores `activeChip` (from the picks response's `active_chip`). While `freehit` is live for the current gameweek, the previous gameweek's picks (the squad FPL gives back afterwards; if that gameweek was itself a Free Hit it steps back one more) are saved inside the **existing** `ff_manual_lineup` record under the non-numeric key `preFreeHit` — `{fhGw, baseGw, savedAt, picks[15], entry_history{bank,value}, restored}`. No new table, no schema change; per-gameweek lineups are untouched and older builds ignore the key. Next Week gets a card: **↩ Restore pre-Free-Hit squad** makes Next Week, lock-in, Advice and *Export locked-in squad* start from that squad (`planningBaseCache()` at the three `buildProjectedSquad` call sites); the Next Week lineup for the planning gameweek is re-seeded from the pre-Free-Hit lineup (positions, bench order, captain) and must be locked in again. **Use the Free Hit squad instead** switches back. A confirm appears first if a locked-in lineup would be replaced. Planned / locked transfers apply on top of whichever base is in use. If the previous gameweek's picks cannot be fetched, the card says so and offers Retry; nothing is written. The capture only runs after saved lineups are loaded and the remote copy has been pulled (`markLineupReady`), so it can never overwrite lineups that were not loaded yet. The Squad tab is unchanged (it correctly shows the Free Hit team during the Free Hit week).
- **FF-030 — Club shirts.** Pitch shirts (Squad, Next Week, Advice recommended XI, Best XI / Best squad, player detail) now show the club code on the chest and use the club's colours (`TEAM_KITS`, keyed by FPL `short_name`; body + collar trim; label colour chosen by contrast). A club not in the table falls back to the old position colour. The position is still shown by pitch row and the bench tag. The list view is unchanged.
- Versions: `<title>`, `#navVer`, `pal-shared.js?v=`, `FF_VERSION` (and so the backup `appVersion`) all 1.56; a v1.55 cache is refreshed once automatically so `activeChip` is present. No `pal-shared.js`, Supabase schema, proxy or launcher change assessed as needed (`index.html` not supplied; squad cache only gained one field).
- Stage 1 testing (Node + jsdom on the real page, synthetic 20-club league): formation solver vs brute force on 6 leagues × (season, gameweek) × 8 formations — XI points identical, squad legal (2/5/5/3, ≤3 per club, ≤ budget), squad XI in the chosen shape, and Auto equals the best fixed formation (600 checks, 0 failures); UI: chip row, persistence, GW toggle keeps the formation, pitch row counts for XI and squad (14 checks); Free Hit: snapshot saved from GW-1 only when `freehit` is live, card and restore, banner, lineup re-seeded, lock-in and Advice picks use the restored squad, restored flag survives a reload with no re-fetch, switching back, no card outside a Free Hit, failed GW-1 fetch, existing per-gameweek lineups preserved (25 checks); shirts: kit colour, club code, unknown-club fallback, text contrast. A Chromium screenshot of Best XI at phone width checked shirt legibility.
- Not tested: real FPL data / a real Free Hit response (`active_chip` value `freehit` is FPL's documented chip name but was not seen live), real Supabase sync or a second device, physical phone, launcher. Kit colours are approximate home-kit colours; the club list was checked against the 2026-27 Premier League line-up.

### v1.53 — FF-025

- New: two collapsed sections at the bottom of the Squad tab, below Gameweek performance.
  - **🏆 Best overall scoring XI** — the 11 highest season-total-points players that make a legal formation (1 GK, 3–5 DEF, 2–5 MID, 1–3 FWD), best formation chosen automatically, with the XI's total cost, points and formation. Ignores budget and the 3-per-club rule (a warning shows if the XI has more than 3 from one club). Cost is the XI only, not a full 15.
  - **💷 Best squad within the FPL budget** — the legal 15-man squad (2 GK / 5 DEF / 5 MID / 3 FWD, max 3 per club, total price ≤ budget) that maximises the starting XI's season points; leftover money buys the best bench (tie-break only). Budget defaults to £100.0m, is editable (£40m–£200m, remembered) and has a "Use my value + bank" button reading `entry_history.value + bank` from the loaded squad. Shows squad cost, bank left, XI points, formation, XI by position and bench.
- Injuries: every player row gets an availability pill built from the existing `isEffectivelyUnavailable` / `injuryRiskLabel` helpers — 🚑 (at risk: injured, suspended, unavailable, or doubtful ≤25%) or 🩹 (milder flag or FPL news text), plus the status dot and news text. Each section has a summary line ("2 of 15 flagged: …" or "No injury or availability flags"). Flagged players are shown, not hidden. Opt-in checkbox "Skip injured / unavailable players" (default off) removes at-risk players from the pick.
- Data: the full player list is not in the trimmed squad cache, so it is fetched from the existing `/bootstrap` proxy route the first time either section is opened and held in memory for the session (also fills `_allPlayersCache` if empty). 🔄 Refresh players forces a fresh fetch (`x-pal-force-fresh`). Nothing new is cached in localStorage or Supabase.
- Algorithm: best XI is exact (greedy). Best squad is exact: per-position knapsack DP over (starters, bench, cost) with dominance pruning, combined over the 8 formations by max-plus convolution; the club limit is restored by best-first branch-and-bound that excludes one player of an over-represented club per branch (first legal solution popped is provably optimal). Limits: 250 nodes / 4 s; if hit, the result is labelled "Best squad found" instead of "Provably the highest-scoring…", with a greedy repair fallback so a legal squad is always returned. Ranking is on season total points (past performance, not a forecast).
- Storage: two display preferences only — `ff_builder_budget_tenths`, `ff_builder_exclude_flagged` (unscoped, like `ff_show_position_best`). Not in the JSON backup (preferences, not data). No data-model, Supabase, proxy or `pal-shared.js` change (only the `?v=1.53` cache-bust tag). Launcher: squad cache shape untouched, no `index.html` change assessed as needed (`index.html` not supplied, not tested).
- Stage 1 testing:
  - Solver vs exact MILP (SciPy/HiGHS) on 8 synthetic ~600-player leagues (three with one club hoarding the top scorers) × 4 budgets × with/without "skip flagged" = 64 runs: XI points identical in all 64, legal squad (15, 2/5/5/3, ≤3 per club, ≤ budget) in all 64; bench tie-break equal in 63 (the 64th is higher in the JS result than the MILP's, within HiGHS's default optimality gap). 40 of 64 were proven optimal; the 24 unproven runs were all on three hoarding-club stress leagues (hit the 250-node limit in ~3.5 s) and still matched the MILP optimum.
  - Best XI vs brute-force over all 8 formations on the same 8 leagues: identical. Edge cases: budget below the cheapest legal squad gives a clear message; fewer than 11 players returns nothing.
  - jsdom running the real page script (stubbed proxy, no `pal-shared.js`): 35 checks — versions in title / `#navVer` / `FF_VERSION`, cards present, collapsed and placed after Gameweek performance, no fetch until opened, squad load still works (regression), XI = 11 players with correct cost/points/formation and pills matching flagged players, squad = 15 within budget, budget change / invalid / too-low / infeasible handling and persistence, "Use my value + bank", skip-flagged removes at-risk players and syncs both checkboxes, refresh refetches once, fetch failure message, tab switching, no unexpected JS errors. `node --check` on both inline scripts. Phone-width (390 px) Chromium screenshot: no horizontal overflow, layout as intended. Diff against v1.52 is additive apart from the four version strings.
- Not tested: real FPL data / real proxy response (synthetic data shaped like `bootstrap-static`), real phone, live Supabase and second device, solver run time on a real phone (≈15 ms per search node on desktop; typical real cases should need 1–20 nodes), launcher.

### v1.52 — FF-024

- Reported: after the GW7 deadline (Sat 17 Oct 2026) the squad stayed on the old gameweek and games were slow to update, even after a manual refresh; and two transfers were not picked up by Sync from FPL.
- Full time: a game now counts as FT when FPL's `finished_provisional` is set or 90+ minutes are played (previously only `finished`, which FPL flips only after bonus is confirmed, often hours later). New helpers `isFixtureFullTime` / `isMatchFullTime`; `buildMatchStateByTeam` stores `isFull`; `thisWeekBoxHtml` and `matchOutcomeSentiment` (blank-at-FT = bad) use it. Older caches without `isFull` fall back to `finished`.
- Gameweek rollover: new `maybeRefreshAfterDeadline` reloads the squad on open (local and Supabase-synced cache) and when the app becomes visible again, if the cached `nextGwDeadline` has passed and the cache was fetched before it. No loop: after a reload `cachedAt` is later than the deadline. Guarded by `_squadLoading`, proxy config and entry id.
- Per-player GW points badge gets `*` (with tooltip) while the gameweek is not finished (cache now stores `gwFinished`, `fpGwReported`).
- Squad tab freshness line (`#squadFresh`): "FPL reports GWn (in progress/finished) · fetched live/from cache <time> · next deadline". Distinguishes a stale cache from FPL not yet having rolled over.
- Transfer sync: FPL's `/entry/{id}/transfers` does list transfers made before the deadline (tagged with the upcoming `event`). `reconcileTransferLog` now matches manual planned/locked/made entries that carry no player ids (free-text / pre-picker) by normalised player names (accent-insensitive, incl. Ø/æ/ß/ł), still one-to-one and inside the existing one-gameweek tolerance. Sync's message now also reports planned/locked-in entries from an earlier gameweek that FPL does not have. Data model unchanged (no migration); `ff_transfer_log` shape unchanged.
- Shared/launcher: `pal-shared.js` unchanged (only the `?v=1.52` cache-bust tag). Squad cache shape only gains optional fields, so no launcher change needed.
- Stage 1 testing (jsdom running the real page script, stubbed PalSync/proxy/FPL): provisional/90-min/live full-time rules; rollover refresh fires after a passed deadline on open and on returning to the app, not before the deadline and not when the cache is newer than the deadline; freshness line and `*` badge; both GW7 transfers (68↔95, 124↔368 shapes, one manual entry with ids, one id-less by name) fold into MADE/synced-from-FPL with no duplicates; repeat sync idempotent; unrelated planned entry preserved; stale-entry report. Negative control against v1.51 fails the full-time tests. `node --check` on both inline scripts.
- Not tested / known limits: real browser, live Supabase, phone, second device. `pal-fpl-proxy` caching beyond the force-fresh header could not be inspected (source not available); the freshness line is there to expose it. The exact cause of Pete's two unmatched transfers could not be confirmed (local log not visible) — the name fallback and unmatched report address the likely causes; if they still show as LOCKED IN after Sync, send the player names/screenshot.

### v1.51 — FF-023

- External-AI JSON import hardened (reported: errors on import). Importer now repairs the common AI/chat-UI slip-ups before parsing — curly quotes, trailing commas, `//` and `/* */` comments, citation markers (`【…】`, `[cite…]`, `contentReference`), raw line breaks and unescaped quotes inside strings, and replies cut off mid-way (closed and flagged with a warning toast). When a reply has several code blocks it prefers the one that looks like the reply schema (not an echoed copy of the situation JSON); an unterminated final fence is still tried. `players` is no longer mandatory (a reply with none of the schema fields is still rejected); `forGameweek` given as a string is coerced. Parse failures now show the text around the failing position, which is also included in "Copy a message to send back to the AI".
- Export prompt: new explicit JSON RULES paragraph (straight quotes, no trailing commas/comments/placeholders, single-line strings, no links or citation markers, null for unknown non-enum fields, summaries under ~250 chars so the reply isn't cut off, JSON block last). Removed `sources[].url` from the reply schema (unused by the app and the usual carrier of citation markup). Payload `schemaVersion` unchanged (6); older replies still import.
- Gameweek performance (new, bottom of Squad tab, collapsed card). Per gameweek the app saves: the locked-in team (starters, bench order, captains, transfers; saved on Lock in), the app's Advice team (XI + captain/vice; saved on each Advice run) and each imported AI's recommended XI/captain/transfer verdict (saved on import). All three freeze at the gameweek deadline so hindsight can't overwrite them. **Fetch results** (once the deadline has passed) pulls each involved player's points for that gameweek via `element-summary` plus FPL's own reported points for the entry, then shows a comparison table (captain, XI, total incl. captain double, difference vs your team), what differed per source, your XI player-by-player, and a running tally of your team vs the app across saved gameweeks. External AI names are matched to the saved squad; unmatched names are counted and shown. Totals exclude auto-subs, chips and hits (FPL's own figure is shown beside them).
- Data: stored under `record_key = 'gw_records'` in the existing `ff_score_history` table (generic key/data, same RLS) and local key `ff_gw_records` — **no database migration**. Merged per gameweek by `updatedAt`. Backup export gains optional `data.gwRecords`; import merges it if present and older backups import unchanged. Keeps the latest 40 gameweeks.
- Known limits: only gameweeks played after this version are recorded (no back-fill); a transfer that changes the 15 players drops the lock (v1.49) but the earlier saved snapshot for that gameweek stays until the user locks in again; the 'ff_score_history' pull for the 6-GW score history ignores the extra row.
- Tested (Stage 1): `node --check` both scripts; jsdom with stubbed shared code, proxy and `element-summary`: lock + advice saved and synced under `gw_records`; imports of a clean reply with prose, a mangled reply (curly quotes, comment, trailing commas, citation marker, raw newline, inner quotes, string gameweek), a truncated reply, two code blocks, garbage (rejected with position snippet) and unrelated JSON (rejected); results fetch and comparison table for locked / advice / three external AIs; freeze after deadline; prompt contains JSON RULES and no `url` field; no console errors.
- Not tested: real AI replies, real browser / phone layout, live Supabase and second-device merge (the `gw_records` row in `ff_score_history` has not been exercised against the real table/RLS), real FPL results, launcher (`index.html` not supplied; no launcher-facing change).

### v1.48 — FF-020

- Locked-in / planned transfers no longer linger once FPL confirms the same transfer.
- Root cause: in `syncTransfersFromFPL()` the "already in the log" check ran before the step that upgrades a matching planned/locked entry, so a confirmed FPL transfer could never absorb a later manual entry (double-counting in the running total and free-transfer slots). Separately, `pullRemoteTransferLog()` merges by id (union), so a manual entry removed on one device could be resurrected.
- Fix: new idempotent `reconcileTransferLog()` — pairs each manual planned/locked/made entry with a synced `'auto'` FPL entry for the same player out + player in (one-to-one; ignores FPL transfers from a clearly earlier gameweek), keeps the FPL entry, carries the manual note across, removes the manual one. Runs after every sync, after loading from cache, after the cross-device merge (re-persists so Supabase heals) and when a lock-in is added for a swap FPL already shows. Sync no longer upgrades in place: one code path.
- Export backup `appVersion` was hard-coded `'1.46'`; now reads `FF_VERSION`.
- No data-model or schema change; existing logs heal on first load.

### v4.4 — FTT-054 — Launcher summary holds eight favourites (was four) — 3 Nov 2026

- **Reported (Pete, deployment check of launcher v11.45, T5):** "Still single row of 4 on desktop card in launcher."
- **Cause:** the launcher's Film & TV card reads its favourites from the summary this app writes (`pal_ftt_stat.topFavourites`), and `writeStatCache()` has only ever put the first **four** in it. Launcher v11.45 (PET-152) shows up to eight on desktop, but the extra four were never there to show. The launcher's fallback (derive more from `ftt_v1`) could not help: since v3.x the library lives in IndexedDB (`ftt_db`) and `ftt_v1` is no longer in localStorage. The fault was in how v11.45 was built (assumed the old storage); the tracker was not supplied at that time.
- **Fix (`film-tv-tracker.html` only):** `writeStatCache()` takes `secFavourites().slice(0, 8)` instead of `.slice(0, 4)`. Same list, same order, same small entry shape (id, title, type, year, https poster or null); the first four are exactly what they were, so an older launcher is unaffected. `favouriteCount`, `watchlistCount`, `availableNow`, `bedtimeNow` and every other field unchanged. The summary is rewritten on every open and every save, so the card gets eight after the tracker has been opened once on that device.
- **Not changed:** the Favourites shelf, the data model, storage, sync, backup, the launcher contract (`pal_x_screen`) and the search list. `pal-shared.js` unchanged (`?v=4.4`, tag follows the app version as in v4.2). Launcher stays v11.45, Fantasy stays v1.65 (no change).
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, header badge, `pal-shared.js?v=4.4`, the new code comment.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, stub `pal-shared.js`, the **real tracker page with its library in IndexedDB and the real launcher page on the same origin**): 13 checks, all passing — tracker v4.3 writes four, v4.4 writes eight; the first four identical in id and order; saved favourite order kept with a Watched and a deleted favourite excluded; each entry keeps its small shape; other summary fields identical; no page errors on boot; **launcher end to end** (no `ftt_v1` in localStorage): desktop shows eight in two rows of four, phone four, tablet four; an older four-entry summary still shows four with no errors.
- **Not tested:** the real `pal-shared.js` / Supabase sync, posters loading, a real phone / Safari, the tracker's own UI beyond boot (unchanged code).
- **Known limitation:** the launcher card keeps showing four until the tracker has been opened once after deploying v4.4.

### v4.0 — FTT-050 — "Reel" look and feel: phone and desktop layouts, Up next hero, stat tiles, Unlock list — 1 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 1 Nov):** a look-and-feel refresh in the same family as Gigs & Trips v7.109 (GIG-122), with the app's own personality, **without changing functionality**. Built from the approved "Reel" design canvas. Pete's four decisions were all the recommended option: **a desktop tile click selects into a details pane**; **Up next hero + four stat tiles** at the top of the Library; **coral Film / violet TV**; **include the diary strip and the Unlock list**.
- ⚠ **ID note:** no Film & TV Tracker backlog was supplied, so **FTT-050 is the next number after FTT-049 in this changelog**, not one confirmed against the backlog. Version label v4.0 (not v3.9) because the whole look changes.
- **Responsive, not device-sniffing:** layout follows the window width. Under 700 px = **phone**, 700 – 1099 px = **tablet** (the phone layout in a centred column), 1100 px and over = **desktop**. `data-layout` on `<html>` records which; the layout itself is CSS media queries on one set of elements, and a `matchMedia` listener redraws what depends on it (details pane vs full-screen detail layer, selected tile) when a window is resized or a phone is turned.
- **Look:** new tokens in the existing CSS variables (warm paper `#F4F0E6` / night `#0E0D12`, one lime signal `#CBF55C` in dark and ink on paper in light, Bricolage Grotesque for titles and big numbers and DM Sans for the rest from Google Fonts with system-font fallback). `--film` is now the accent (lime / ink); the old teal tints and dark-on-teal text were remapped to the accent tokens. Film is coral and TV is violet, shown as a 4 px bar on the poster foot, never as the accent. The film-strip perforation is the motif (hero edges, under every section heading, empty states). The theme still follows the launcher (`PAL_THEME`).
- **Navigation:** phone/tablet = a **floating bar** (Library, a lime **Add** puck, Services; it replaces the tab row and the "+ Add" button in the search row). Desktop = a **left rail** (Add title, Library, Services with counts, sync chip at the foot). Dialogs are **bottom sheets** on phone/tablet and centred on desktop; on desktop the Add dialog is two columns (search and credits left, New releases / New seasons right).
- **Desktop:** the Library is a 6-column poster grid (shelves wrap instead of scrolling sideways) with a 420 px **details pane**. A tile click **selects** into the pane (the title's detail, with Edit title / Delete); with nothing selected the pane shows **Tonight** (Up next, the four tiles, the review banner, the diary strip); on Services it shows the **Unlock list**. ⚠ On desktop a tile click therefore no longer opens the full-screen layer; phone and tablet still do. Resizing keeps the same open title: shrinking a desktop window to phone width opens it full-screen, widening it puts it back in the pane.
- **New display elements (all derived on the fly from data the app already holds; nothing is stored):**
  - **Up next hero** (the first title of the Favourites shelf, else the first of Available to watch, i.e. the order the Library already uses): poster, meta, service chip, interest pips, Mark watched (existing `quickMarkWatched`) and Open. Shown only on the unfiltered All / Want to Watch Library (not with a filter, a service filter, a search, Select or Reorder).
  - **Stat tiles:** watched ring (watched of all), available now, bedtime-ready, new seasons. The figures use the same rules as the launcher cache (`pal_ftt_stat`); each tile opens the existing view (Watched, Available filter, Short / Bedtime filter, New seasons).
  - **Rank slates** 1..n on the Favourites shelf (the saved favourite order), **interest pips** on the Available to watch groups, a **season bar** (one segment per season; done / part-watched) above the season rows in the detail view, a blurred-poster header on the detail view, the Interest chooser as a segmented control.
  - **Diary strip:** titles watched per month for the last 12 months, from each Watched title's existing watched date (shown on the Watched view on phone/tablet and in the desktop Tonight pane).
  - **Services:** tiles with a logo (or initials), type, access tick and "n waiting" (Want to Watch titles on that subscription / free service); desktop adds three summary tiles. **Unlock list:** services you do not have, ranked by how many Want to Watch titles are blocked waiting for them (`isBlocked` + `resolveAvailability().required`), below the tiles on phone and in the pane on desktop. A service tap still opens the existing edit dialog.
- **Data / sync / launcher: not touched.** Same `ftt_v1` (IndexedDB with localStorage fallback), `ftt_svclogos`, `ftt_relfilters`, `pal_ftt_stat` (same keys), same Supabase table `pal_film_tracker` and PalSync paths, same JSON backup / restore / list import. No new stored data, no new dependency; still one HTML file. `pal-shared.js` unchanged (`?v=1.13`). The launcher card information is unchanged, so `index.html` was not edited (the card reads `pal_ftt_stat` only).
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, header badge, inline header comment. (No other displayed version string exists in the file.)
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium with a **stub** `pal-shared.js` and a 47-title fixture, Supabase absent): at phone (390), tablet (820) and desktop (1360), light and dark: layout tag, no sideways scroll, no console errors; floating bar vs rail, add puck, pane only on desktop; hero, tile figures equal the `pal_ftt_stat` cache, rank slates, interest pips, season bar states, diary total; search, status tabs, TV chip, More sheet and filters, service logo filter, Select mode (floating bar hides) and bulk bar, Reorder, Add (sheet on phone, two-column centred on desktop), detail layer on phone / tablet, Escape; **live resize** desktop → phone → tablet → desktop with an open title (layer and pane swap, selected tile, body scroll restored, floating bar and rail swap); desktop select into pane, Edit title saved to state and IndexedDB, Mark watched from the hero (persisted, hero advances, tiles and cache update), Favourite and Interest in the pane, Services grid, waiting counts, Unlock ranking and the edit dialog, Sync & Backup as a sheet, JSON export structure and import of the own backup, `PAL_THEME` switch; stored data compared before and after navigation, filters and modes (identical). Render time of `renderAll()` on a 1,504-title library: ~12 ms phone, ~33 ms desktop (v3.8: ~7 ms). Four first-run test failures were wrong test expectations (e.g. the Watched view shows 21 unique tiles in both v3.8 and v4.0 because the existing New seasons shelf repeats a title), re-checked against v3.8.
- **Not tested:** the real `pal-shared.js` and live Supabase / PalSync (two devices, Lex's account); the real launcher card and iframe; a real phone or Safari (touch, safe areas, on-screen keyboard, drag-to-reorder by touch); real TMDB posters and service logos; Google Fonts (only the system-font fallback was seen); your real library size (~2.5 MB).
- **Known limitations:** Sync & Backup dialog, title edit dialog, tag-imported-titles and new-releases review flow, More filters / Set interest / Tag filter sheets and the service edit dialog take the new colours and sheet/centred behaviour only; their inner layouts are unchanged. The viewport tag still has `user-scalable=no` (pinch-zoom blocked): recommend removing it, left alone as it is a behaviour change. The New seasons alert button is hidden on phone/tablet (the New seasons tile replaces it) and shown on desktop. The Up next hero is not shown when a filter or search is active.

### v3.8 — FTT-049 — Subscription logo filter

- **Request:** see which films/series on the lists are on each subscription, with logo buttons that work from whatever Library view is open.
- **Change:** a row of logo buttons sits under the Library pills (inside the sticky controls). It lists the subscription/free services you own (`hasAccess`, active) that have at least one title; tap one or several to narrow the current view to titles available on them (OR across services). It composes with every existing view: the sectioned All view, TV / Films / New release sections, Tag view, the flat filters (Available, Favourites, interest…), the Want to Watch / Watched / All status, and search. Section ordering is unchanged; Reorder is not offered in a filtered sub-view (same as TV/Films). The heading shows the selected service names and count; an empty result says "Nothing here is on the selected subscription." **✕ Clear** removes the filter. Buttons have a tooltip/aria-label "Name · N titles"; unselected buttons dim while a selection is active.
- **How it matches:** per title, stored `availability` entries of type subscription or free are mapped with the existing `findMatchingService`; rent/buy never counts. No new availability logic; refresh data with Update from TMDB if a title looks wrong.
- **Logos:** fetched once from TMDB `/watch/providers/movie|tv?watch_region=GB`, matched by normalised name, and cached as a tiny name→path map in localStorage `ftt_svclogos` (not the main library, so no FTT-041 quota impact). Without a logo (offline, no match) the button shows initials.
- **Data and sync:** none. Selection (`lib.svc`) is session-only UI state, never persisted or synced. No data-model, backup/JSON or Supabase change. `pal-shared.js` unchanged. Launcher: no change needed (`pal_ftt_stat` shape unchanged).
- Tested (Stage 1): `node --check`; jsdom on the real page with stubbed TMDB and a 5-title library: buttons shown only for owned services, logo fetched and cached, single and multi-select counts, combined with TV, Films + Want to Watch, flat-filter empty state, Tag view without error, search + filter empty state, Clear. Not tested: real browser/phone layout and horizontal scroll, live TMDB logo matching on the real service list, the real library at size, second-device behaviour.
- Known limitations: the filter resets on reload; matching depends on the fuzzy service-name match; logos need TMDB reachable once.

### v3.7 — FTT-048 — Show all of an actor's credits

- **Request:** the actor list in + Add search stopped at the 40 most popular; allow showing all.
- **Change:** when an actor has more than 40 credits, the note under the list now reads "Showing the 40 most popular of N" with a **Show all N** button. It lists every film and series credit (still most popular first, same talk/reality/"Self" filtering as v3.5) and the button becomes **Show top 40**. The choice (`_searchData.showAll`) is redrawn in place via `refreshSearch()` — scroll position kept, no new TMDB request — and is reset when an actor is opened again. Actors with 40 or fewer credits show no button.
- **Data and sync:** none; display only. `pal-shared.js` and the launcher unchanged.
- Tested (Stage 1, jsdom, real page, stubbed TMDB, 9 checks, all passing): 40 rows plus "Show all 95"; all 95 after the toggle with scroll kept and no request; back to 40; stays expanded after adding a title; reopening an actor starts at 40; 30 credits shows no button. The v3.6 search suite re-run: all pass except its own version check. Not tested: a real actor with several hundred credits in a browser (long list rendering speed), phone layout.

### v3.6 — FTT-047 — Adding from + Add search no longer jumps to the top of the results

- **Bug:** tapping + Watchlist or ✅ Add as Watched in the Add title search (title results and, from v3.5, an actor's credits) sent the list back to the top, so the next title had to be found again.
- **Cause:** `addFromSearch()` finished by calling `runSearch()` / `showActor()`, which replaced the list with a "Searching… / Loading…" placeholder, re-requested TMDB and redrew. The short placeholder collapsed the modal's height, so the scroll position was lost.
- **Fix:** the results on screen are kept (`_searchData`: title results + actor chips, or an actor's credits). After an add, `refreshSearch()` redraws the list from them synchronously — no placeholder, no new TMDB request — and restores the scroll position of the modal (`.modal`, the element that scrolls). The added row flips to "Already added — view" in place. Row/list HTML was factored into `searchHtml()` / `actorHtml()`. Typing a new search or tapping an actor / Back still re-fetches as before.
- **Data and sync:** none; display only. `pal-shared.js` and the launcher unchanged.
- Tested (Stage 1, jsdom, real page, stubbed PalSync/TMDB, 16 checks, all passing): scroll position kept after adding from the actor list and from the title results (the modal's scrollTop is stubbed because jsdom has no layout); no `search/multi` or credits request after an add; no placeholder shown; the added row (and earlier ones) flagged; v3.5 actor-search checks unchanged. v3.3 and v3.4 suites re-run: only their own version-number checks fail. Not tested: the real scroll behaviour on a phone/browser (layout is not simulated), which the deployment check covers.

### v3.5 — FTT-046 — + Add search finds actors as well as titles

- **Request:** search by actor or title from the Add title modal.
- **Change:** no mode switch — the one search box now does both. TMDB `/search/multi` already returned people (the app discarded them); up to three matching actors (acting department, with known-for titles) now appear as chips above the title results, showing a photo and two known-for titles. Tapping a chip lists that person's films and series from `/person/{id}/combined_credits`: most popular first, up to 40, with the character shown ("as …") and a **← Back** button to the title results. Rows use the same layout and buttons as title results (+ Watchlist / ✅ Add as Watched / Already added — view), so `searchRowHtml()` was factored out of `runSearch()`.
- **Filtering of credits:** talk / news / reality appearances (TMDB genres 10767, 10763, 10764) and "Self / Himself / Herself" credits are dropped so the list is the acting work; duplicate credits (one per title) are collapsed. A later release can loosen this if it hides something wanted.
- **Behaviour kept:** adding a title from an actor's list stays in that list and flags the row as added (`refreshSearch()` / `_searchView`); `mediaProviderSearch()` still returns films and series only (new `mediaProviderSearchAll()` returns everything). Placeholder and hint text mention actors.
- **Data and sync:** no data-model, sync, backup or storage change; nothing new is stored. `pal-shared.js` and the launcher are unchanged.

### v3.4 — FTT-045 — New releases filters (films/series, language, genre, hide)

- **Request:** trim the New releases scan down with more than the window and cinema/streaming choice — language, genres and similar — keeping it simple.
- **Change:** + Add → New releases has a collapsible **Filters** section (opens by itself when filters are active; its title summarises them, e.g. "Filters: Korean · Drama"). Choices: **Films + series / Films only / Series only**; **original language** (Any, English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Dutch, Danish, Swedish, Norwegian, Korean, Japanese, Hindi, Mandarin, Turkish); **genre** (one of 17); **Hide** tick-boxes (Animation, Documentary, Reality / talk, Family / kids); **Reset filters**.
- **How:** the filters are added to the existing TMDB `/discover` queries (`with_original_language`, `with_genres`, `without_genres`), so the 30-per-source cap is spent on matching titles rather than trimmed afterwards. TMDB's film and series genre ids differ, so each genre maps to both (`REL_GENRES`); a genre with no series equivalent (Horror, Romance, Thriller, History, Music) skips the series source, and Series only + Cinema only has nothing to look up (a message says so, no request is made). "Reality / talk" only applies to series. Review window, ignore list, dedupe against the library and the New releases button are unchanged.
- **Feedback:** the done / nothing-found toasts name the active filters.
- **Storage:** choices are remembered on this device only (`localStorage` key `ftt_relfilters`, read/written inside try/catch). Not in `state`, so no sync, backup, schema or data-model change. `pal-shared.js` and the launcher are unchanged.
- Tested (Stage 1, jsdom, real page, stubbed PalSync/TMDB recording the request URLs, 15 checks, all passing): no filters leaves the three queries unchanged; language + genre + hide reach all three queries; Horror skips series; Series only; Series + Cinema only makes no request and resets the button; per-media genre ids and the combined hide list; summary label; toast names the filters; save, restore and reset of the remembered choices. The v3.3 suite re-run on this build: 20/21 (the only failure is its own "title is v3.3" check). Not tested: real TMDB results (e.g. that `with_original_language` combines as expected with `with_release_type`), real browser/phone layout of the Filters block.
- ⚠ Language is TMDB's *original* language, so an English-language film from a non-UK studio still counts as English, and a dubbed foreign title is matched by its original language.

### v3.3 — FTT-044 — Season handling; New seasons / New releases buttons; new-season check moved to + Add

- **Mark watched on a TV show asks about its seasons.** On the detail card (no edit mode needed) a show with seasons asks "Have all N seasons been watched?". OK marks the show and every season watched; Cancel leaves everything unchanged and takes you to the Seasons list to tick them yourself. The bulk "Mark watched" action now also marks every season of a TV show (no prompt). Marking the show watched keeps any rating already set.
- **Seasons are tappable in the detail view** (✅ / ⬜). Ticking the last season marks the whole show Watched (`checkAutoCompleteSeries`, which now also preserves the rating).
- **New season on a Watched show:** TMDB sync (per-title refresh and the bulk check) uses the new `applyNewSeasonCount()`. A Watched show whose TMDB season count is higher moves back to Want to Watch, the season count is updated, every previously tracked season is marked watched, `newSeasonsDetected` is set as the review flag, and the rating/review are kept. New optional field `returningShow` marks this state so editing and saving the title does not wipe `watched`; it is cleared when the show is watched again. Watching the new season(s) marks the show Watched again with the original rating. A show already on Want to Watch just gets the `newSeasonsDetected` flag as before. A stale flag is cleared when TMDB no longer shows more seasons.
- **New seasons / New releases buttons** above the Library (`#libAlerts`, before the favourites). Each shows its count and appears only when there is something to review: New seasons = titles with `newSeasonsDetected` (opens the Library filtered to New season); New releases to review = pending titles from the releases import (opens the review window limited to `importSource:'releases'`; `pendingImportTitles()` / `openTagModal()` take an optional source). Hidden in select mode and while reordering favourites.
- **New-season analysis moved to + Add** (new "📺 New seasons" box with progress and Cancel); the button was removed from Data → Library Maintenance (the info text there points to + Add). The run now bumps `updatedAt`, saves, and pushes changed titles to Supabase in batches of 10, and reports how many were flagged / moved back / errored.
- **Data and sync:** no schema, backup format or storage change. `returningShow` is an optional field carried in the normal title record (sync, JSON export/import). `acknowledgeNewSeasons` now uses `max(seasons, newSeasonsDetected)`. `pal-shared.js` (`?v=1.13`) untouched. Launcher: no change needed (`pal_ftt_stat` shape unchanged).
- Tested (Stage 1, jsdom with `fake-indexeddb`, real page, stubbed PalSync/TMDB, 21 checks, all passing): alert counts and visibility; Mark watched OK / Cancel; season tick/untick and auto-complete; Watched show demoted with rating kept and old seasons watched; detail callout; re-watching restores Watched with the same rating; watchlist show flag-only; stale flag cleared; Add-modal check end to end incl. Supabase push of the changed title and the summary text; New releases filter; `returningShow` in the JSON export. Not tested: real browser/phone layout, the real `pal-shared.js`, live Supabase and a second device, real TMDB responses, the native confirm dialog, JSON file import in a browser.
