### v3.2 — FTT-043 — Launcher card follows the Favourites shelf; four favourites

- **Bug:** after a favourite was marked Watched it stayed in the launcher card's "Top favourites" (reported with World War II with Tom Hanks), although it had left the Favourites shelf in the app.
- **Cause:** `writeStatCache()` (v2.5) built `topFavourites` from `orderedFavourites()`, which is every live favourite including Watched and blocked ones. The shelf uses `secFavourites()` (Want to Watch, not blocked). Marking a title Watched does not clear its favourite flag or order, so the two lists disagreed.
- **Fix:** `topFavourites` is now `secFavourites().slice(0, 4)`, so the card shows exactly the first four titles of the shelf, in the saved order. Four rather than three (launcher v11.05, PET-109). `favouriteCount` is unchanged (all favourites). No data-model, sync, backup or storage change; the favourite flag and order of a watched title are untouched, so un-watching it puts it back where it was.
- Tested (Stage 1, jsdom, real page with a stubbed PalSync and seeded `ftt_v1`, 9 checks): four in saved order; marking the second Watched drops it and the fifth moves up; card equals the shelf; un-watching restores it; fewer than four; none; un-favouriting; non-https poster stored as null; counts still written. The same test run against v3.1 fails at the first Watched check. Not tested: real `pal-shared.js`, Supabase or IndexedDB, a real browser or phone, Lex's account, the launcher card updating live while the app is open in the iframe.

### v3.1 — FTT-042 — Site-wide localStorage total no longer depends on the shared file

- **Fixes v3.0-T3.** On the device the Storage panel showed "All apps' localStorage: not available".
- **Cause (inferred, the live file was not inspected):** the panel called `PalSync.storageUsage()`, which was added in pal-sync v1.13 (TI-089). The device's sync already works in shared mode (v1.12), so the `pal-shared.js` actually being served is most likely the older v1.12 copy (a cached copy under the same `?v=1.13` query string, or an older deployed file — the Shared Components section records that apps keep running the previous copy until the query string changes).
- **Change:** `storageReport()` now measures localStorage itself with a small read-only `localStorageUsage()` (same 2-bytes-per-character basis and ranking as `PalSync.storageUsage()`). "not available" now appears only if the browser refuses to list localStorage. No other change.
- **Not changed:** `pal-shared.js` and its `?v=1.13` reference are untouched; nothing in the app depends on v1.13. If the site is serving an older shared file, uploading the current `pal-shared.js` (v1.13, as supplied) is optional and separate from this release.
- **v3.0-T4 result recorded:** the breakdown panel works (availability 622 KB, overview 529 KB, everything else 716 KB, link data not stored 994 KB). The note on the ❌ read "Passed"; the note box only appeared on the Problem button, so it was used to attach the figures. Treated as passed.
- Tested (Stage 1, jsdom with `fake-indexeddb`, 102 checks across the three suites, all passing): the new test removes `PalSync.storageUsage` from the page (simulating the older shared file), then checks the line shows a figure that matches the real localStorage contents and lists the largest keys first; the v3.0 IndexedDB, fallback and pull suites re-run unchanged. Not tested: the live site's `pal-shared.js`, a real iPhone.

### v3.0 — FTT-041 — Library moves to IndexedDB; the FTT-039 trim is removed

- **Fixes the failed deployment check v2.9-T2.** On the real device the Storage panel showed this app's local copy at **0.0 KB** and "Last local save: Failed — storage full".
- **What the v2.9 panel revealed (device figures, UTF-16 KB):** availability 622, overview 529, posterUrl 172, watched 141, externalIds 106, everything else 1,024 = **about 2,594 KB (2.5 MB) even after dropping the links**, plus 994 KB of link data that v2.9 no longer stores (so the v2.8 cache was about 3.6 MB).
- ⚠ **Corrections to earlier entries.** The assumption recorded in v2.7 (FTT-039) and v2.9 that `ftt_v1` was "~1.2 MB, the real library" was wrong; the library is roughly twice that. Consequently the FTT-039 `trimIfLarge('ftt_v1', 2048)` was not inert: the local copy was over 2,048 KB, so after every cloud pull `saveState()` wrote it and the trim then **deleted it** (the likely reason for 0.0 KB; not directly confirmed on the device). v2.9's slimming alone could not make the copy fit alongside the other apps in the shared localStorage quota.
- **Change:** the library is stored in IndexedDB (database `ftt_db`, store `kv`, key `state`, the slimmed JSON text as one string), outside the quota shared by every app on the origin. localStorage is kept only as an automatic fallback and as the one-off source of an existing copy.
  - **Boot is asynchronous** (`initStorage()`, `loadState(raw)`); nothing is drawn until the copy has loaded. The sync pull (`onSession`) awaits a `_bootReady` promise so a session arriving during boot cannot run against an empty state.
  - **Move from localStorage:** if an `ftt_v1` copy exists it is written (slimmed) to IndexedDB, read back and length-checked, and only then removed from localStorage. If any step fails the localStorage copy is left in place and the app runs in fallback mode. If both copies exist the one with the later `lastUpdated` wins.
  - **Fallback:** used when `indexedDB` is missing, errors, is blocked or does not answer within 3 s. Behaviour is then exactly v2.9 (slim localStorage writes, one warning toast a minute on refusal).
  - **Writes** go through `writeLocalState()` → a coalescing pump (`pumpIdb()`): a burst of saves (the importer) becomes a few writes of the latest state. Failures (e.g. IndexedDB quota) use the same single warning toast and Data-panel status as v2.9. `localSaved()` resolves when queued writes finish.
  - **Removed:** the `trimIfLarge('ftt_v1', 2048)` call (FTT-039) and the `_slimRewritePending` flag (the fallback keeps the one-off slim rewrite at boot).
  - **Sync & Backup → Storage** now shows where the copy is stored, its size, this app's use of shared localStorage, the all-apps localStorage total (or "not available" if the shared file in use lacks `storageUsage()`), last local save status, and a longer "Where the space goes" (top 8 fields, tombstones, link data not stored, largest localStorage items).
- **Unchanged:** Supabase tables, sync and merge logic, cloud rows, JSON backup format (export still includes links), in-memory data model, `pal-shared.js` (still `?v=1.13`), launcher (`pal_ftt_stat` is still written on every open and every save).
- **Known limits / watch-points:** IndexedDB writes are asynchronous, so a change saved a split second before the page is killed (iOS) could miss the local copy; the cloud copy is unaffected, and this was equally true of the cache before. A device that has never synced has nothing locally until its first successful pull. Safari can clear all script-written storage (including IndexedDB) after about 7 days without use; the cloud copy repopulates it. Older cached copies of this page (v2.9 or earlier) would still write `ftt_v1` to localStorage; the newer-wins rule resolves this at the next open.
- **Version label:** v3.0 rather than v2.10 because v2.9 and v2.10 are already used by older builds (FTT-029 and FTT-030) and the storage change is architectural.
- Tested (Stage 1, jsdom with `fake-indexeddb`, running the real page and the real `pal-shared.js`; 97 checks across three suites): fresh install; reopen with no session; move of a fat 840-title localStorage copy (all fields identical apart from links, no `updatedAt` change, localStorage key removed); both-copies newer-wins in both directions; move failure (localStorage copy kept, fallback); later IndexedDB quota failure (one toast, panel status, recovery); localStorage completely refusing writes while IndexedDB works (saves succeed, no warning); a 1,500-title library of 2,622 KB (UTF-16 basis) pulled from a stubbed Supabase and **not deleted** after the pull, `trimIfLarge` not called, no title rows pushed; burst of 60 saves coalesced; session arriving during boot; export, restore from an old backup, panel contents; library render, detail view and `pal_ftt_stat`; no-IndexedDB fallback (the whole v2.9 suite re-run unchanged). jsdom page-load time with the large library not representative of a phone.
- Not tested: real Safari / iPhone (IndexedDB behaviour, the real quota, ITP eviction), the real library and Supabase, two devices, the launcher card on a device, a genuine quota failure in IndexedDB.

### v2.9 — FTT-040 — Leaner local cache, and storage you can see

- **Why:** `ftt_v1` (~1.2 MB on the Mac, the largest single key on the shared origin) was reported as a local-storage size problem. Findings from the code: (1) every `availability[]` entry stored a copy of the TMDB "where to watch" page link (`url`), repeated once per provider (often 10+ per title) and read by nothing; (2) a refused local write was swallowed (`console.error` / empty `catch`), so a full quota stopped the local copy updating with no sign; (3) the Data panel's "Size" counted characters while the other apps' storage reports count UTF-16 bytes (2 per character), so the figures could not be compared.
- **Leaner copy:** what is written to localStorage is now a slimmed copy of `state` (`serialiseForStorage()` / `slimTitleForStorage()`), without `availability[].url`. The in-memory state, the Supabase rows and JSON backups are untouched, so no data-model, schema or sync change; no `updatedAt` is bumped and nothing is pushed. Because `pal-sync` `pull()` replaces a local title with the cloud copy whenever the cloud's `updatedAt` is the same or newer, cloud rows keep re-introducing `url` into memory on every pull; slimming at write time (rather than once at load) is what keeps the stored copy lean.
- **One-off rewrite:** a cache written by an older build (contains `"url"`) is re-saved once at boot via a plain local write (same pattern as the favourite-order upgrade); no other file or data changes.
- **New TMDB mappings no longer create `url`:** `mapProvidersToAvailability()` emits `{ service, type }`. `sameAvailability()` already compared only type and service, so old and new entries count as unchanged and Update from TMDB does not rewrite titles because of this.
- **Local writes can no longer fail silently:** all four `ftt_v1` write sites (`saveState`, `persistOnly`, the export pre-write, the boot upgrade) go through `writeLocalState()`, which returns success/failure and never throws. On failure it shows one warning toast at most once a minute (storage full vs other refusal; with a cloud session it says cloud sync is not affected, without one it says to download a backup) and records the failure for the Data panel. The export pre-write is silent so the download still proceeds.
- **Sync & Backup → Storage panel** now shows: this app's local copy and the whole origin's total (both on the UTF-16 basis, via `PalSync.storageUsage()`), this app's share, last local save status, last saved / exported and data version (existing lines kept), and a collapsible "Where the space goes" (top fields by size, deleted titles awaiting sync, link data not stored on this device, largest items on the site). Read-only.
- **Not changed, on purpose:** the FTT-039 `trimIfLarge('ftt_v1', 2048)` call stays as it was (inert at current size). `pal-shared.js` is unchanged (still `?v=1.13`; uses the existing `storageUsage()`). No launcher change (`pal_ftt_stat` shape unchanged; the launcher's `ftt_v1` fallback reads titles, posters and order, not links).
- **Considered and not done:** moving the library to IndexedDB (removes the pressure from the shared quota but turns the synchronous boot async and needs a migration — kept as the next step only if the new panel shows the slimmed copy is still too big); cloud-first caching with `PalSync.cacheSet` (the TI-089 pattern — would end offline browsing, which this app promises); shortening `posterUrl` or dropping null/empty fields (small saving against a data-model change and `=== null` risks).
- Tested (Stage 1, jsdom running the real page against the real `pal-shared.js`, 53 checks): fat cache slimmed on boot with every other field, `updatedAt` and `lastUpdated` identical and all titles/tombstones kept; no rewrite for an already-slim cache; `saveState` stores slim while memory keeps `url`; full cloud pull with a stubbed Supabase (200 titles carrying `url`) stores slim and pushes no title rows, repeat pull the same, slim cache reloads with availability intact; mapping and `sameAvailability` old-vs-new; quota failure (no throw, one toast, rate limit, panel status, in-memory state intact, recovery, with and without a session); storage report arithmetic against `PalSync.storageUsage()`; JSON export, and import of an old backup; render and detail view on slim data; speed of a 2,200-title write. On a synthetic library (8 availability entries per title, ~70-character links) the stored copy fell 34.5%.
- Not tested: real browser (Safari / iPhone), the real library and Supabase, two devices, a genuine quota failure. The real saving is unknown until the new panel is read on the live app; the earlier estimate was ~300 KB of ~1,221 KB.

- Imports a Netflix viewing-history CSV (quoted-CSV parser; season markers resolve 166 shows / 277 show-season pairs / 1,060 ambiguous strings in Pete's file). Matching heuristic with exact-name TV check and full-string fallback; unmatched kept and flagged.

- Dashboard, Watchlist, Watched, Services, Search/Add, Reviews tabs. TMDB (GB) search, metadata and watch providers via `append_to_response=watch/providers`; Watchmode considered only if coverage proves thin.

# Fortnight Tracker

`fortnight-tracker.html`. The app's inline comment block keeps the 15 most recent releases; the full history was in `fortnight-tracker.md`, resequenced newest-to-oldest because the original inline order mixed ascending and descending runs. Supabase table `fortnight_bundles` (bundles keyed by `record_key`; `code_`, `leave_`, `bh_`, `la_` prefixed rows share the table). Local key `fn_tracker_v5`, also read directly by PeteGCal and Gigs & Trips for the working-day alert.

⚠ Several FT IDs are reused across versions in the source (for example FT-062 at v3.72 and v3.68; FT-039 at v3.44 and v3.42; FT-030 at v3.36 and v3.33; FT-026 at v3.34 and v3.32; FT-020 to FT-025 at multiple versions). They are preserved as recorded.

### v3.87 — Suite WP1.4 / WP1.2 — A refused save is reported; dates with a year are dd/mm/yy — 4 Nov 2026

- **Why:** `saveLocal()` swallowed a refused write (B3 / B9); dates showed as "01 Jul 2026" (D10).
- **Change:** `saveLocal()` writes through `PalShared.safeSet`; `fmtDate` (with year) and the print header date are dd/mm/yy; `shortDate` ("01 Jul") is unchanged.
- **Needs:** `pal-shared.js` 1.1.0 (tag `?v=3.87`).
- **Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, Europe/London, real data seeded from the 4 Nov backup files):** With the real 98 KB backup loaded, a refused write returns normally and shows the bar and `FT_DATA_UPDATED` is still sent; `fmtDate(new Date(2026,6,1))` = 01/07/26. Load of all 11 pages with no errors. **Not tested:** a real browser quota failure (simulated by making `localStorage.setItem` throw), Safari, the iPhone, cloud sync with the new build, nested copies inside other apps.
- **Files:** `fortnight-tracker.html`, `pal-shared.js`. No data format, storage key, sync or backup change.

### v3.86 — FT-078 — "Hours target at risk" now says when it ends — 3 Nov 2026

- **Problem:** the launcher showed "Hours target at risk" until the app was next opened, even after that fortnight had ended (the alert is computed when the app saves).
- **Change (`fortnight-tracker.html`, one line plus version text):** the alert published for the launcher now carries `until`, the bundle's `endDate` (the last working day of the fortnight; falls back to the last day in the bundle). The launcher (v11.60) hides it from the next day. Needs `pal-shared.js` pal-contract v1.1 (loaded as `?v=3.86`); with an older copy the field is dropped and the launcher falls back to the same rule from the alert id.
- **Not touched:** data, storage keys, sync, JSON export/import and backup, the Live, Timesheet, Archive and Leave tabs, the holiday upcoming items.
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, logo sub-line, rail footer, `pal-shared.js?v=3.86`, inline comment: v3.86.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, the real file with the real `pal-shared.js`, fake clock): a bundle created for w/c 26 Oct with one short day marked done publishes `ft-target-2026-10-26` with `until` 2026-11-05 (bundle endDate and last day agree); the same with the previous `pal-shared.js` publishes the alert without `until` and with no page errors; title and footer v3.86; no page errors. A diff against v3.85 shows only the intended lines (13). Not tested: the live app with your real bundles, a second device.

### v3.85 — FT-077 — Today's day card can be collapsed — 2 Nov 2026

- **Report (Pete, before deploying v3.84):** in the live fortnight, today's card does not collapse when the expand / collapse toggle is pressed.
- **Cause:** by design since FT-069, `toggleDay()` returned immediately for today's day ("today's day stays expanded") and `isOpen` was forced true for it, so the chevron did nothing.
- **Change (phone / narrow layout, where the chevron is used):** today's day card still opens by default, but its header chevron now collapses and re-expands it. The choice is kept in a session-only `focusCollapsed` map (same lifetime as `openDay`), so it survives live updates and re-renders but not a reload; nothing is saved. Other days behave as before (one open at a time). Desktop (row tap selects into the details pane) is unchanged.
- Version updated: `<title>`, header badge, rail footer, `pal-shared.js?v=3.85`.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, 390 px, a live bundle): today is expanded by default; the header tap collapses it and the chevron closes; a re-render keeps it collapsed; a second tap expands; another day expands and collapses without affecting today; after a reload today is expanded again; v3.84 behaviours re-run (17/17 and 38/38). Not tested: real iPhone touch, desktop pane.

### v3.83 — FT-075 — Holidays as an .ics calendar file — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 2 Nov; Stage C):** calendar export for **Fortnight holidays only** (Gigs already mirrors to Google Calendar; Gym and Claims were not chosen).
- **Change:** Leave tab › **Calendar** button downloads `fortnight-holidays.ics` (fixed, undated name): every upcoming holiday day (today onward, current and next tax year; bundle days marked Holiday plus manual leave records, one per date) as an all-day event "Holiday" with the booked hours in the description. Stable UID `ft-hol-YYYYMMDD@papps.local`, CRLF lines folded at 75 characters, exclusive `DTEND`. Nothing to export shows a message and downloads nothing.
- **Limitation (inherent to a plain .ics file):** re-importing updates the same events in most calendar apps, but a day you later remove here is **not** removed from a calendar that already imported it; delete it there by hand.

Not tested: importing into Apple Calendar / Google Calendar / Outlook, Safari download behaviour.

### v3.81 — FT-073 — "Timecard" look and feel: phone and desktop layouts, new summary elements — 1 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 1 Nov):** a look-and-feel refresh in the same family as Gigs & Trips v7.109 (GIG-122), with the app's own personality, **without changing functionality**. Built from the approved "Timecard" design canvas, together with Claim Tracker v2.21 ("Receipt"). Pete's decisions: Claims inside Fortnight folds its header and bar into one slim strip; desktop Live is rail + list + details pane (a row tap selects); the nine-column skyline hero; **no** quick "mark today done" button (kept out to stay display-only; prompt for the backlog given with this release).
- ⚠ **ID note:** the Fortnight Tracker backlog was not supplied, so **FT-073 is the next number after FT-072 in this changelog**, not one confirmed against the backlog.
- **Not changed (frozen):** every feature and workflow, all hours / pace / projection / capex / leave maths, data structures, local key `fn_tracker_v5`, Supabase table `fortnight_bundles` and its `code_` / `leave_` / `bh_` / `la_` rows, JSON backup / import, the launcher messages (`FT_ACTION` openTab, `FT_DATA_UPDATED`), the Claims standalone flag, PWA icon code and `pal-shared.js`. No new dependency; still one standalone HTML file. **No new stored data** — every new element reads what the app already holds.
- **Look (shared family DNA):** warm paper (#F4F0E6) and night (#0E0D12) themes following the launcher's setting (the app keeps its own default of dark when no preference is set); lime signal (#CBF55C in dark, ink on paper in light) for the New / Submit / Done actions and the active tab only; Bricolage Grotesque for titles and big numbers, DM Sans for the rest (Google Fonts, system fonts offline). The old token names (`--amber`, `--teal`, `--green`, `--red`, `--blue`, `--purple`, `--card`, `--surface` …) are kept because the JS-rendered markup uses them inline, and keep their meanings (projected / logged / on target / below / leave / above). New: `--acc`, `--lime`, `--s2`, `--hat1/2`. The whole look is one block appended after the existing CSS.
- **Fortnight's own signature ("Timecard"):** each bundle is a hero card: the big confirmed figure, a projected figure with an On target / short / over chip, a **70 h track** (solid = confirmed, hatched = projected) and the **nine-column skyline**: one column per working day (today outlined, in lime; projected days hatched), a gap between week 1 and week 2, a dashed 8 h line and a dashed ghost slot for the Friday off. The track is 1.25 × the day's standard so the 8 h line sits at 80% and "above" days can show (`segFill()`); TS-logged chips under each column keep their green / amber / red meaning.
- **Responsive, not device-sniffing:** under 700 px phone, 700–1099 px tablet (phone layout in a centred ≤540 px column), 1100 px and over desktop. CSS media queries on one DOM; `data-layout` on `<html>` / `<body>` records which; `data-tab` records the tab. A resize listener re-tags the page and redraws **once** when the window crosses the 1100 px line (so a desktop → phone → desktop resize restores the rail, pane and selection); nothing redraws at other widths.
- **Phone / tablet:** header (logo, version, sync chip) and a **floating bottom bar** (the same five tab buttons and `switchTab()`, now with line icons and the existing count badges); dialogs are **bottom sheets** with a grab handle; the toast sits above the bar; safe areas respected (`viewport-fit=cover` added; the rest of the viewport tag unchanged — see flagged item).
- **Desktop:** the header and tab buttons become a **left rail** ("New fortnight" button on top, sync chip and version at the bottom). **Live / Archive:** list in the middle, **details pane** on the right: a day row tap **selects** it into the pane (today by default; tapping the selected row keeps it) and the pane shows that day's existing editor (total, start / end / lunch, timer, extra, status, timesheet codes, notes, submitted). The "Details" button is hidden (the day list is always shown). **Timesheet / Leave:** the full width, matrix and cards unchanged. **Claims:** the nested Claim Tracker fills the area to the right of the rail. Dialogs are centred.
- **New elements (all display-only):** (1) skyline + ghost slot + today column; (2) 70 h track (updates live with `refreshBundleHeader()`); (3) "Day n of 9" chip; (4) ticket-style day rows: dashed date stub, status and TS chips, Done / Logged pair; (5) details pane on desktop (`.pane-hd`, `syncPaneSel()`); (6) Timesheet: capex **target tick** under each percentage and a **Timesheet hours logged** tile (logged vs projected for the bundle); (7) Leave: allowance **progress bar** (turns red when over) and a **hours-by-month strip** for the tax year (holiday blue, sickness red).
- **Restyled only (same markup and behaviour):** week headers, weekend cards, timer, extra, status buttons, timesheet codes in the day card, Timesheet matrix and week cards, Leave records, codes manager, every dialog (new bundle, leave record, bank holidays, add-timer-to-Extra, Sync & Backup), the toast and controls (buttons ≥ 44 px, status buttons wrap in 3 + 2).
- **Code touched outside CSS / the HTML shell (all display-only):** `segFill()` (scale, today / projected flags), `renderBundle()` (hero markup: day chip, 70 h track, today class), `refreshBundleHeader()` / `liveUpdate()` (track widths, hatch flag), `renderDay()` (stub, pane header), `toggleDay()` and `jumpToDay()` (desktop selects into the pane), `render()` (now `render()` = the old body + `syncPaneSel()`), `capexPctBodyHtml()`, `renderCapexTracker()` + new `loggedTileHtml()`, `renderAllowanceBlock()`, `renderLeave()` + new `leaveMonthsHtml()`, `loadClaimsFrame()` (see below), `switchTab()` (`data-tab`), `applyTheme()` (meta colours only) and the new layout block before BOOT (`isDesktop`, `syncPaneSel`, `syncLayout`). No element id was removed.
- **Claims tab / Claim Tracker v2.21:** the nested frame now loads `claim-tracker.html?embedded=ft`, which tells Claim Tracker to fold its own header and bottom bar into one slim strip (Pete's decision 1). The frame is full width under the header on phone / tablet and fills the area right of the rail on desktop (it was `100vh − 160px`). **Deploy both files together:** Fortnight v3.81 with an older Claim Tracker shows the old Claims layout (double header; nothing breaks); Claim Tracker v2.21 with an older Fortnight shows full Claims chrome inside the tab.
- **Launcher:** `index.html` was not supplied and is **not changed**. It reads `FT_DATA_UPDATED` and sends `FT_ACTION` (`openTab`) — message types, the local key and the table definitions were diffed against v3.80 and are identical. The launcher's 9-Day Fortnight card keeps its own look.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, header badge, the rail footer, `pal-shared.js?v=3.81` (the file itself is unchanged) and the inline history comment.
- Tested (Stage 1; headless Chromium, offline stub of `pal-shared.js` with an in-memory mock cloud, clock fixed to Wed 4 Nov 2026, Supabase not reachable): **differential run, original v3.80 vs v3.81, same scripted workflow — saved `localStorage`, all 28 values pushed to sync, toasts identical**: two bundles, statuses incl. holiday hours and training / conference, start / end / lunch / extra / note edits, Timesheet matrix cells, a day-card code, a leave record, allowance, capex target, week submitted toggle, export, wipe and import of that backup. **55 layout and element checks, all passing:** at 390 / 820 / 1360 — layout tag, floating bar vs rail, New button only on desktop, no sideways scroll on Live / Timesheet / Archive / Leave, nine columns + ghost slot + one today column, 70 h track equals `bundleStats`, ticket stubs, bottom-sheet vs centred dialog, phone rows still expand / collapse in place; desktop pane shows today by default, a row tap selects (Thursday), tapping again keeps it; **desktop → phone → desktop live resize** (bar floats and rail goes, pane stops being a side pane, no sideways scroll, rail / pane / selection restored); paper and night backgrounds and DM Sans; capex tick, logged tile, leave allowance bar and 12-month strip; nested Claims frame URL and geometry (flush under the header, no page scroll, 390 / 820 / 1360). ### v3.77 — FT-069 — 22 Oct 2026 — Holiday/sick hours recorded properly, clickable top bar, current day first

- **Holiday / sick recording.** Marking a day Holiday or Sick now adjusts the day's clock as well as setting `holidayMins`. Previously the clock and extra were left alone, so a manual holiday double-counted (e.g. 8h clock/extra + 8h holiday).
  - Full day (holiday hours ≥ the day's standard, 8h or Fri 6h): start = end, lunch 0, extra 0; the holiday covers the day.
  - Part day: the shift is shortened so clock + holiday = the standard day. Lunch is 0 for a shift of 4h or less, otherwise 30m; extra is zeroed. A half day (holiday ≈ half the standard) shows a "½ day" tag and `dayAbsenceLabel()` returns "Half day" (other part days stay "Partial h:mm").
  - Changing the holiday hours re-adjusts the clock (screen re-renders). Setting them to 0, toggling the status off, or changing to a non-absence status restores the previous end/lunch/extra, remembered in a new optional day field `_absPrev` (same idea as `_autoLeavePrev`). Holiday ↔ Sick keeps the original remembered values.
  - New functions `applyAbsenceClock`, `restoreAbsenceClock`, `isHalfAbsence`. `fillDayFromLeave` gained an optional `di` argument so part-day leave records (Leave tab / bundle creation) make up the rest of the day the same way; without `di` it behaves as before. Both callers updated.
- **Top bar.** Each of the 9 segments is now a link to its day: it opens the bundle's details, expands that week, opens that day and scrolls to it (`jumpToDay`). Holiday/sick share is blue (new legend item "Holiday / sick"); a half-day holiday shows the worked share in its normal colour and the holiday share in blue. Bar look factored into `segFill()`, used by both the initial render and `liveUpdate`.
- **Bundle layout.** The "current day" is today if it is a bundle day, otherwise the next bundle day (e.g. over a weekend); none if today is outside the bundle's span. That day is listed first in its week with the earlier days after it; the week holding it is listed first (week 2 first once in week 2); its week is never auto-collapsed. The current day is always expanded (tag "Today"/"Next", amber border) and cannot be collapsed; other days stay collapsed and open one at a time as before. New functions `focusDayIdx`, `orderDays`; `renderBundle`, `renderDay`, `toggleDay`, `isWeekCollapsed` updated.
- No change to storage keys, the Supabase schema or sync. New optional day field `_absPrev` is carried by existing JSON export/import and sync. `pal-shared.js` and `index.html` not changed (launcher needs no change). Version synced in `<title>`, logo-sub, the `pal-shared.js?v=` tag and the inline history comment.
- **Known limitations:** days already marked Holiday/Sick before v3.77 are not migrated (they keep their old clock until their holiday hours or status are changed). The Details panel is still opened with the Details button; the current day is expanded once it is open.
- Tested (headless jsdom, real `fortnight-tracker.html`, `PalSync` stubbed, mocked date, 42 checks, all passing): script syntax check; full-day holiday zeroes clock and totals 8h; toggle off restores; half day (4h) and 2h, plus short Friday, make up the full day; holiday hours to 0 restores; Holiday→Sick; part-day leave fill and revert, full-day leave fill, legacy call without `di`; bar links and legend; split bar fill; ordering with today on Thu in week 1, Tue in week 2 (week 2 first), a weekend ("Next" Monday), before start and after end; current day open and uncollapsible, other days one at a time; jump to a week-2 day; focus week not auto-collapsed when complete; saved localStorage contains the adjusted day. Not tested: a real browser or phone (layout, tap, scroll), live Supabase and a second device, the Leave tab and Done → Timesheet flows in a browser.

# Gigs & Trips

> ✅ **Back in the launcher from v11.24 (PET-128, 1 Nov 2026), for Pete and Lex.** It was on hold from P Apps Launcher v11.01 (PET-105, 2026-10-04) to v11.23; the file, data and backlog were unchanged throughout. See the v11.24 entry under P Apps Launcher.

`GigsAndTrips.html`. From v7.87, full entries go in the `.md`; the inline HTML comment keeps a short pointer (same convention as `index.md` and `PeteGCal.md`). Entries before GIG-072 (GIG-001 – GIG-071) were not migrated and remain as inline comments in the HTML (see "Pre-GIG-072 history" below).

Architecture notes recorded across the changelog and backlog:
- Gigs & Trips does **not** use PalSync: bespoke sign-in and direct Supabase REST calls. Supabase has one `events` table (`id`, `user_id`, `type` = `'gig' | 'trip' | 'venue_*'`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `data` jsonb, `updated_at`); gigs, trips and venues are whole-document rows; trip items are nested in `trip.days[].items[]`. RLS is an allow-list of the Pete and Lex UIDs (`user_id` for authorship only).
- Local storage: `gat_v1` (plus `gat_v1_clean` until v7.101), on an origin shared with the whole suite.
- Google Calendar via `pal-gcal.js` (see Shared Components), shared OAuth client and Cloud project quota with PeteGCal; calendar id `GCAL_CALENDAR_ID` hardcoded to Pete's account.
- Recurrence model (in force since v7.100): **Series → virtual occurrences → exceptions**. Extend it; never add a second recurrence implementation or return to creating hundreds of real records.
- Google projection of recurrence (since v7.105): a series is **one Google recurring event** (RRULE + time zone); a changed occurrence is an **override of that Google instance** (id = series id + original slot); a cancelled occurrence is an **EXDATE** on the series; a date that has a changed occurrence is never sent as an EXDATE.

### v7.114 — GIG-123 — A gig deleted in Google Calendar is removed here too (with Restore); Calendar is checked when you return to the app — 5 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 5 Nov):** a gig deleted in Google Calendar did not disappear from Gigs & Trips; should sync be two-way for creation, edits and deletion. Finding: it already was (v7.97, GIG-102/103/104), but a deletion in Google was only *listed for review* under Sync & Backup (never applied), and the check ran only when Google sign-in succeeded (page load) or on the manual Pull button, so a delete made in the Calendar app while this app was open or in the background never showed up. Pete's decision: **auto-remove gigs, with undo; trips and items stay on review.**
- **Auto-removal (gigs only).** When the deletion check finds that Google says a linked gig is gone (404/410, or `status: cancelled`, as before), a plain gig is removed from Gigs & Trips (local + Supabase tombstone only; **no Google call**, Google already lacks it). A snapshot of the whole record is stored first (`gat_gcal_removed`); if the snapshot cannot be stored, nothing is removed and the gig goes to review instead.
- **Still held for review, exactly as before:** repeating events (a series, and a changed occurrence of one — consistent with the v7.105 rule that a series deleted in Google is flagged but kept); trips and trip items; a gig with a Calendar change still waiting to send (pending or failed in the queue); **more than 5 gone gigs in one pull** (all of them go to review: a mass disappearance is more likely a wrong account or a bulk clean-up than intent); and any pull where Google returned **no events at all**.
- **Recently removed (Sync & Backup).** New section listing gigs removed this way (name, date, when), with **Restore** and **Forget**. Restore puts the full record back (reviews, ticket info, costs included) with a newer `updatedAt` so it wins over the cloud tombstone, drops the old Google link and sends it to Google as a **new** event (queued if not signed in). Entries are pruned after 30 days or beyond 30 entries. The list is **per device** (it is not in Supabase).
- **Toast:** names the gig removed ("was deleted in Google and removed here (Restore: Sync & Backup)"), joined with the existing "N Calendar changes need review" text when both apply. Sync log line: "N removed (deleted in Google)".
- **Pull on return to the app.** When the app becomes visible again it now also runs the Calendar pull, at most once every 2 minutes (the 10-minute throttle still applies to the automatic load-time pull). If the Google token has lapsed it makes the same silent token refresh the app already makes at startup; a successful sign-in then runs the pull itself.
- **Storage registry:** `gat_gcal_removed` classified (Temporary; pruned automatically) so the storage report does not show it as unknown.
- **Unchanged:** creation and edit sync in both directions; the review list and its three buttons for trips/items/series; deleting in the app still deletes the real Google event (and queues it if that fails); `pal-gcal.js` (v3), `pal-shared.js`, `pal-diag.js` and the launcher are not changed.
- Version updated: `<title>`, header badge, `pal-shared.js?v=7.114`. No data-model change; no Supabase migration.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chrome, the real `GigsAndTrips.html` with the real `pal-shared.js` / `pal-gcal.js`, **`PalGCal` network methods and the cloud push stubbed**; inline scripts pass `node --check`): **38 checks, all passing** — 404 and `cancelled` both remove a plain gig, snapshot stored with the full record, no Google delete call, tombstone pushed, nothing flagged; series master, changed occurrence, trip and trip item are flagged and never removed; a gig with an unsent local change goes to review; 6 gone at once → none removed, all flagged; exactly 5 → all removed; empty Google list → review not removal; snapshot write failure → gig kept and flagged; an event still in Google (moved) and a Google 500 → nothing removed or flagged; the full review path (one present, one gone) removes only the gone one and the toast names it; Restore brings back reviews/venue, re-creates in Google with a new link, drops the old link, refreshes `updatedAt`, empties the list; pruning by age and count; the section renders, escapes a hostile name, and is empty when nothing is removed; the return-pull gate (signed in → one pull, second within 2 minutes skipped, pull again after 2 minutes, no token → silent refresh and no pull, hidden → nothing) and that it is wired into the `visibilitychange` handler; `gat_gcal_removed` is classified; version in title, header and script tag; no page errors.
- **Not tested:** the real Google Calendar (what Google returns for an event deleted in the Calendar app is still assumed to be 404/410 or `status: cancelled`, as in v7.97), the real Supabase tombstone/restore round trip, a second device, the silent token refresh on return on a phone, the Sync & Backup panel layout, and Lex's account. The existing "Check repeating events" self-test was not re-run.
- **Known limitations:** the Recently removed list is per device (a gig removed on the phone cannot be restored from the laptop); a gig deleted in Google is removed on the *next* pull, not instantly; the per-pull cap of 10 deletion checks (v7.97) and the −14 / +180 day window still apply, so a gig outside that window is not checked.

### v7.112 — GIG-094 — More › Fortnight holidays: work holiday days as events, with duplicate checks — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 2 Nov):** Fortnight holidays should be added through Gigs & Trips so they sync to Google Calendar, checking for duplicates as part of that workflow.
- **Where:** **More › Fortnight holidays** (🌴), shown only for Pete and only when this device holds Fortnight Tracker data; the row shows "N to add · M to remove" or "up to date". Tapping it shows a summary and asks to continue; nothing changes before that.
- **What it reads:** Fortnight Tracker's own saved data on this device (same keys as the working-day alert; never written): holiday days from today onward = bundle days marked Holiday + manual leave records of type holiday (sickness, bank holidays and past days are ignored). The summary names how old that data is.
- **What it creates:** one all-day event per holiday day, name "Holiday", category Other, stable id `fnhol_YYYYMMDD`, flag `fnHoliday`, saved through `saveEvent()` and sent through the normal `gcalSyncGig()` path (so Google gets it exactly as a gig saved by hand does, queued if not signed in to Google).
- **Duplicate checks (before adding):** an event with that id already exists → left alone; the id was created or seen on this device before but the event is gone (you deleted it) → not re-created; another live gig that day whose name looks like a holiday (holiday / annual leave / leave / day off / time off), whether typed by hand or imported from Google → skipped and listed. Re-running is a no-op ("Nothing to change").
- **Removal:** a holiday event this feature created whose day is no longer a holiday in Fortnight Tracker is removed, including from Google Calendar (same delete-and-queue rule as deleting a gig by hand). Events you created yourself are never touched.
- **Known limitations:** (1) Gigs drops a local tombstone once the cloud confirms it, so "you deleted it" is remembered in a per-device list (`gat_fnhol_seen_v1`); a device that never saw the event live cannot know it was deleted and would offer it again. (2) It runs when you tap it, not automatically. (3) Two devices tapping at the same moment could both send to Google (the stable id keeps Gigs to one record; use Sync & Backup duplicate tools if that ever happens). (4) The Google side was exercised with a stub of the Calendar library only.
- Version updated: `<title>`, header badge, `pal-shared.js?v=7.112`. Nothing else in the app changed.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, mocked Supabase, **stubbed `PalGCal`** because `pal-gcal.js` was not available): plan (create / existing / duplicate / deleted-earlier / remove) for seeded data; More row and counts; confirmation text; events created with the right ids and fields and pushed through the normal save; 2 all-day Google creates with the app's own metadata and linked ids; user events untouched; a removal deletes its Google event; second run is a no-op; Lex sees no row and cannot run it; no Fortnight data on the device → no row. Not tested: the real Google Calendar, `pal-gcal.js`, Sync & Backup duplicate tools afterwards, the real Fortnight data on your phone.

### v7.109 — GIG-122 — "Stub" look and feel: phone and desktop layouts, per-category Important — 1 Nov 2026

- **Request:** build the "Stub" proposal in full (a ticket-style look, mocked up on a design canvas and approved by Pete), make the app **render differently on a phone and in a full browser**, and let **Categories** choose which types appear under **Important**.
- **Responsive, not device-sniffing:** the layout follows the width of the window, so it also reacts when a window is resized or a phone is turned. Under 700 px = **phone**, 700 – 1099 px = **tablet** (the phone layout in a centred column), 1100 px and over = **desktop**. `data-layout` on the page records which; the layout itself is plain CSS media queries on one set of elements (`#mainNav` and the add button move), and a width listener redraws the current screen when the class changes.
- **Look:** a new palette in the existing CSS variables (light "paper" and dark), one signal colour (lime) and four category colours (Gig pink, Appt blue, Trip amber, Standard grey) carried by the small tile / chip / dot; Bricolage Grotesque for dates and titles and DM Sans for the rest (loaded from Google Fonts; falls back to system fonts offline). `--acc` is now ink in light and lime in dark, so links and active states stay readable in both themes. The theme still follows the launcher's light / dark setting.
- **Phone / tablet:** the four tabs and the add button are one **floating bar** at the bottom (it replaces the tab row and the round add button). A trip under way shows as an **"On trip · name · Day n of m / Next: …"** strip above the bar. Dialogs open as **bottom sheets**.
- **Desktop:** a **left rail** (New, the four tabs, the on-trip strip), the list in the middle and a **details pane** on the right for Upcoming, Agenda and Past: tapping a row **selects** it (poster, clash notice, map link, ticket and notes rows, Open details / Edit) instead of opening a dialog; trips open full width; dialogs stay centred. ⚠ On desktop a row tap therefore selects rather than opens — "Open details" is one click further.
- **Upcoming:** the next event as a **hero ticket** (date, countdown, category, Work day, Clash, Open), a 7-day **week strip** with category dots (a tap opens that day in Agenda), then the Events / Trips / Conflicts figures, Needs attention, On now, **Coming up** (the next three) and **Later** (year › month › day, as before). Rows are tickets: dashed date stub, title, time · place, chips, category tile.
- **Agenda:** a **week strip** and a **day timeline** (hour axis, blocks in category colours side by side when they overlap, a red outline and "Overlap" tag for two or more commitments, a "now" line on today, untimed items above the axis, work day / day off tags), a date control and a Today button; below it the **Next 60 days** list as before. The class filter meanings are unchanged. Gigs have no stored length, so a gig is drawn as two hours (display only); an item uses its stored duration or one hour.
- **Past:** a **grid of stubs** per month (date, emoji, title, place, review stars, status) and a "n events waiting for your review" prompt that opens Reviews. Search still gives a flat list of rows.
- **Trip detail:** an amber **hero** (name, dates, nights, destination, days to go or "Day n of m", status, type, edit), a **cost bar** (paid / still to pay), and the days as a **journey** with a numbered line. The three tabs are a segmented control. Everything inside the tabs is unchanged.

An event follows its category's switch unless it has its own class; anything inside a trip stays in Important. Stored as an `imp` override in the category table (same synced record, merged item by item, so it follows Pete, Lex and every device) and removed again when it matches the default. Sections, the Gigs / Appts / Trips / Standard filters and the conflict rule are unchanged.
- **Data / sync / Google Calendar:** not touched — same `gat_v1`, same Supabase paths, `pal-gcal.js`, backups and import. The only data change is the optional `imp` field in the category table. Launcher v11.26 is unchanged and works with this version.

### v7.108 — GIG-121 — Categories: manage event types, their emoji and their section (under More) — 1 Nov 2026

- **Request:** a place in More to manage the event categories, their emoji and which section (Gigs / Appts / Trips / Standard) each belongs to. Decided with Pete: **shared via Supabase** (one table for Pete, Lex and every device) and **edit the built-in types and add your own**.
- **What a section is (unchanged rules, now written on the screen):** every gig has a class — chosen on the gig, otherwise derived from its type. Filters: **Gigs** = class Gig / Event; **Appts** = Appointment; **Trips** = Trip / Itinerary or anything linked to a trip; **Standard** = Standard or Other; **Important** = Gigs + Appts + Trips. An event with its own class keeps it. On a trip, Travel, Stay, Food, Key stop and Attraction are always Trips.
- **New screen — More › Categories:** the 16 built-in types grouped by section with their emoji, name and number of events. Tap the emoji to pick from a palette or type / paste any emoji; edit the name in place; choose the section from a menu (it moves to that group); **Hide** takes a type out of the add-event picker (existing events keep showing it); **Add a category** (name, emoji, section); **Remove** a category you added (refused while events use it); **Reset built-in categories to defaults** (keeps yours). Light / dark and phone layouts follow the rest of the redesign.
- **How it works:** `GIG_TYPES` is now the built-in defaults plus a per-type default section (`cls`); your changes are overrides, and `applyCategories()` rebuilds `GIG_TYPES` in place from the two, so every screen that reads types (rows, Agenda, forms, search, Google titles, reviews) follows. `defaultEventClassForGig()` reads the section from the table — with no changes it gives exactly the old result for all 16 types, with and without a trip (checked). A type whose section you chose is no longer flagged by "Review classes". Built-in keys never change, so stored events, Google Calendar colours and gym handling are untouched; a custom type has its own key (`c_…`) and uses the "other" Google colour.
- **Storage and sync (the one data addition):** local key `gat_categories_v1` and one shared record in the existing events table, row id `settings_categories` (`type:'gig'`, same shape and same upsert as venue rows; no schema change, no migration). Each item carries `u` (when it was last changed); two copies are **merged item by item, newer wins**, so one device's edit can never drop a category another device just added; a removed category stays as a marker. A change made offline is retried on the next pull. The record has no `id` in its data, so older app versions and every event / venue code path ignore it. It travels in JSON backups (`categories`) and is merged on import; older backups simply have none. `gat_v1` itself is unchanged.
- **Launcher:** the summary the launcher reads (`pal_gat_stat`) now carries each event's emoji (`ic`) and is rewritten when categories change; launcher v11.26 shows it.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, header badge, `pal-shared.js?v=7.108` (the file itself is unchanged).
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, stubbed `pal-gcal.js`, Supabase intercepted with a fake signed-in session): default class mapping identical to v7.107 for all 16 types (with and without a trip); More lists Reviews, Locations, Categories and stays highlighted with a back link; groups and counts; changing an emoji updates rows and the add form; renaming and moving Gym to Appts moves its events into the Appts and Important filters and out of Standard, an explicit class still wins, and it is no longer flagged for review; adding a custom category, refusing a duplicate name, using it through the real add form (stored, classified, shown with its emoji, found under the Gigs filter); remove refused while in use; hiding a type removes it from the picker but existing events still resolve; settings survive a reload; the push posts `settings_categories` with the venue-row shape; a pull adopts a newer remote item and keeps local-only changes; an older remote copy does not overwrite local and the local copy is pushed; the settings row is never treated as an event; export carries the table; reset restores built-ins and keeps yours; the launcher summary carries the emoji; the earlier dashboard, Agenda, Past, add / edit / delete, back-navigation and export / import checks all pass; no console errors; the screen fits a 390 px phone. Not tested: a second real device or Lex's account, the live Supabase table (the upsert reuses the venue path, which is proven in use, but this row was not sent to the real database), real Safari.
- **Known limitations:** categories apply to gig / event types; trip items (Travel, Stay… inside a trip's day) keep their own type list. Changing a section changes where events **without their own class** appear, immediately and for everyone. A custom category uses the neutral Google Calendar colour. The Trips section has no built-in standalone types (Travel, Stay, Food, Key stop and Attraction only count as Trips when on a trip); you can move any type there.

### v7.107 — GIG-120 — UI redesign: Apple-inspired look, four-tab navigation, Upcoming dashboard — 1 Nov 2026

- **Brief:** a visual redesign and navigation simplification, preserving all functionality, data and integrations. An evolution of v7.106, not a rewrite; still one standalone HTML file, no framework, same `gat_v1` key and data shape.
- **Visual system:** neutral grouped-list look (light and dark), a restrained violet accent, subtle separators instead of borders and shadows, compact type. The CSS variables stay the single place colours live; new tokens `--sep` and four muted category colours (`--cat-gig`, `--cat-appt`, `--cat-trip`, `--cat-std`) used as a small dot on rows and in the Agenda. The old card, list-header, Agenda and search rules were replaced in place (not overridden). Forms and buttons got matching, lighter controls; no field, validation or workflow changed.
- **Navigation:** **Upcoming · Agenda · Past · More**. Reviews and Locations are inside **More** (two rows with counts); they open exactly as before, More stays highlighted, and a "‹ More" link returns. Trip / day sub-navigation and back behaviour are unchanged. The add (＋) button is now on all four main screens (it was Upcoming and Past only). The sync chip is a quiet text control; its colour still shows the state and tapping it still opens Sync & Backup.
- **Upcoming is a dashboard:** heading "Upcoming — Your plans at a glance"; the class filter (unchanged meanings) as one compact control; summary figures **Events / Trips / Conflicts**, each shown only when above zero and calculated from the same filtered list the screen shows (an event is a gig or a repeat occurrence, a trip is a trip record — itinerary items are never counted); **Needs attention** (only when something needs a decision; up to three shown, "+ n more"); **On now** (trips under way, as before); **Next up** (the next three, chronological); then **Later** — the rest, still grouped year › month › day with the same expand / collapse. Tapping a figure goes to the relevant content (Events → the list, Trips → the Trips filter, Conflicts → Needs attention); tapping a warning opens the event or trip. Search still shows a flat result list.
- **What counts as a conflict (reusing the existing helpers `gigsConflictingTrips` and `tripsOverlapping`, plus the same-date rule `gigsOnSameDate` applies):** two or more commitments on one day, a commitment inside a trip it is not part of, two trips that overlap. A **commitment** is an event of class Gig / Event or Appointment; **Standard** events (gym, bins, payday…) and trip itinerary items can no longer produce a clash. A **work day or day off is context only** — a quiet "Work day" / "Day off" tag, never a warning (the old "you may need a day off" banner is now that tag). The same rule drives the row warnings, the dashboard and the Agenda. ⚠ This is a deliberate change from v7.106, where any two events on one date (including a bin day) raised a warning.
- **Rows instead of boxed cards (Upcoming, Past, search):** one grouped list per day; date block on the left, the title as the dominant text, time · place underneath, small category dot + type, quiet tags, a countdown on the right and a chevron. Done / Missed, review stars, the repeat mark, "in Calendar", gym plans and conflict lines are kept. Trip rows show the date range and nights, destination, type, status and "Day n of m" while under way; their **day-by-day breakdown, linked events and gym plans now sit behind a toggle** (open by default only while the trip is under way; your choice is remembered until the page reloads). ⚠ This supersedes GIG-056's "always show the breakdown" on the list; the breakdown is unchanged inside the toggle and in the trip detail. Notes, costs, bookings, itinerary, travel, reviews and every edit action are unchanged in the detail views.
- **Agenda:** same data, 60-day window and filters (meanings unchanged); compact date headers (Today, Tomorrow, weekday + date), grouped rows with the category dot, **Scheduling overlap** shown on the day header and on the rows concerned (commitments only), quiet **Work day / Day off** tags from Fortnight Tracker, a **Today** button and a **jump-to-date** control; the Now / Next card is lighter.
- **Past:** same grouping, collapse and status indicators in the new row style.
- **Launcher summary:** `gatWriteLauncherStat()` writes `pal_gat_stat` (next events with no class filter including repeat occurrences — at most two per series — trips under way, and clash kinds from the same rule as the dashboard) on every save and at start-up, before the launcher is notified. Read by launcher v11.25; if absent the launcher falls back to `gat_v1`. A local-only key; not synced, not part of backups.
- **Code notes:** the upcoming / past split and sort used by `render()` are now `gatUpcomingSplit()` / `evSortCmp()` (same logic, shared with the summary writer); `toggleTripCardExpand` now keeps an explicit open / closed choice (it was unused code). `renderGigCard`, `renderTripCard`, `renderAgenda`, `agendaRow`, `agendaDateHeader` and `dayHdrHtml` were rewritten; `renderReviews` / `renderVenues` only gained the back link.

### v7.106 — GIG-116 fix — A cancelled occurrence now reaches Google; a moved version number is not a conflict

- **Reported:** in the first real test of v7.105, "Cancel this event only" removed the date here but not in Google Calendar.
- **Cause (a real defect, reproduced):** a push of a repeating event is refused if Google's version number (etag) has changed. Any change was treated as "Google changed it too", so with an edit of the user's own waiting the app declared a conflict and sent nothing. The number can move without the series changing; the likely trigger was the preceding "Edit this event only" patching one Google instance (⚠ assumed to move the series' number, **not confirmed against Google**). Reproduced against a stand-in Google that behaves that way: old code listed a "changed in both places" item and sent nothing. The same weakness existed for single gigs since v7.97.
- **Fix:** before declaring a conflict the app compares Google's *content* (title, time, place, notes, the repeat rule including cancelled dates; not the version number) with what it last sent. Same content: adopt the number and send the change again **once**; if the number moves again immediately the change is left waiting (visible, retried), not turned into a conflict. Content really differs and the user also changed it: still a conflict, nothing overwritten. Applies to single gigs on both the push path and the Calendar pull.
- **Healing:** "Calendar changes to review" entries that were only a moved number are resolved automatically after sign-in and on **Retry now** (number adopted, change sent). Genuine conflicts are never touched.
- **Visibility:** "Cancel this event only" reports what happened ("Cancelled here and in Google Calendar ✓" / "…not updated yet — see Sync & Backup"). The repeating-event view shows its sync state and, for a series in Google, a **↻ Send to Google Calendar now** button.
- Files: GigsAndTrips.html, GigsAndTrips.md. `pal-gcal.js` unchanged (v3). Launcher unchanged.
- Tested in Node (17 suites pass) against a stand-in Google that moves the series' number when an occurrence is patched: the exact sequence from the report now sends the cancellation, with no conflict and nothing queued; a real conflict is still a conflict; one retry then waiting, never a loop; single gigs on both paths; healing; honest messages; badge and resend. Three older test expectations were updated for the intended change. Not tested: real Google or a browser; if the cancellation still fails the Sync Log line will say why.

### v7.105 — GIG-116 — Repeating events sent to Google Calendar, two-way

- **Model:** series = one Google recurring event (rule + time zone); changed occurrence = override of that Google instance (id = series id + original slot, the format verified on the real calendar in v7.103/v7.104); cancelled occurrence = EXDATE on the series. A date with a changed occurrence is not sent as an EXDATE (that would delete the override in Google).
- **What now reaches Google**
  - A **new series** is created when saved: rule, start in the series' time zone, 3-hour default end computed in real elapsed time (correct across both UK clock changes), the structured description, colour and metadata `{ app:'gigs-and-trips', type, gigId, kind:'series' }`.
  - **Edit all events** updates that Google event, with the version check (`expectEtag`).
  - **Edit this event only** on a series already in Google creates the changed occurrence pointing at Google's instance, so saving it changes that instance. If the series reaches Google later, its changed occurrences are adopted as overrides; a stand-alone copy sent earlier is queued for deletion so nothing is duplicated.
  - **Cancel this event only** adds the EXDATE and updates the series. **Delete all events** deletes the Google series and its changed occurrences (404/410 count as done).
  - Converting an ordinary gig that is already in Google into a series turns that event into the recurring one rather than creating a second.
  - The send queue handles repeats: retries, a rejected rule becomes a visible Failed item, and a drain sends the series before its changed occurrences.
- **Older series are not sent because they were edited.** Series made before this release (no Google event) are created in Google only through **Sync & Backup → "⬆ Send N repeating events to Google…"**, which lists them, asks first and sends one by one. Their changed occurrences wait without queueing; one already sent as a stand-alone event keeps syncing that way until its series is sent.
- **Google-managed (imported) series are editable again.** ⚠ Supersedes the read-only behaviour recorded under v7.104 (the guards were removed). The daily refresh now covers every series that has a Google series id, including ones sent from here; the button is now "↻ Refresh repeating events from Google now".
- **No silent overwrites**
  - A push is refused if the series changed in Google since the last sync. With nothing waiting to send here, Google's version wins (the title is stripped of the app's type icon, so it cannot grow on each round trip). If both changed, nothing is touched and it is listed under "Calendar changes to review" with a **Repeats** line and **Use Gigs & Trips / Use Google**: the first accepts Google's version number and sends ours over it; the second takes Google's rule and fields.
  - If Google changes the repeat to a form this app cannot represent, it is not applied: the series is flagged Failed with the reason and left as it was.
  - The daily refresh skips a series with edits waiting to be sent, a send queued, or (for a series made here) no sync baseline. A new Google version number with identical content is no longer counted as an update.
- **Review fixes made while finishing the release.** An unfinished earlier cut of this feature was found in the working copy and reviewed before release. Three defects were fixed: it sent every series on any save, including older never-sent ones; a changed occurrence of an unsent series was queued indefinitely and would have shown as "waiting to send" for ever; and a new Google version number alone counted as an update. Two earlier tests were updated because the behaviour intentionally changed (v7.94 metadata objects 3 → 4; v7.100 "series never sent").
- Not done: "this and following"; changing a single occurrence's time zone.
- Files: GigsAndTrips.html, GigsAndTrips.md. `pal-gcal.js` unchanged (v3). Launcher unchanged.
- Tested in Node against a stub Google (16 suites pass): event bodies (weekly timed, all-day yearly, a 31 Dec all-day end, ends across the autumn and spring clock changes, EXDATE excluding only cancelled dates, monthly last-Friday with UNTIL); create/update with the version precondition; converting a gig already in Google; what is and is not sent (older series, new series, changed occurrences of an unsent series, stand-alone copies); signed-out queueing and drain order; adoption of changed occurrences including queuing deletion of the stand-alone copy; edit-this and cancel-this with and without the series in Google; the three mismatch outcomes and both resolutions; refresh protection; a rule round trip for six varied series through the real event body; the explicit Send flow including failure and permanent rejection; series instances and overrides never imported as separate gigs; deleting a synced series; a series deleted in Google flagged but kept.
- Not tested: real Google or a browser. This is the first release that writes recurring events to the real calendar. Unproven assumptions: Google accepts the event body as built (time zone on both ends, `recurrence` in a PATCH to an existing single event, colour); a PATCH of an instance id creates an override; the version precondition behaves on recurring masters as on single events. A one-series first test was requested.

### v7.104 — GIG-117, GIG-116 (read direction) — Fold imported repeats into series; Google-managed series

- The second real-calendar scan verified the sync assumptions: instance-id format matched Google on all live instances checked (timed across BST/GMT and all-day), this app's engine produced Google's dates (56/56, 28/28, 14/14, 13/13 imported ids matched); remaining mismatches were occurrences changed in Google.

Predicted from the last scan: 89 series (46 replacing imports, 43 new running), 212 imported gigs folded in, 2 kept as changed occurrences, 14 Google-changed occurrences as exceptions, net −149 KB.

App-created series behave as in v7.100.
- Scan report folds single-clean-import series into one line ("ONE IMPORTED GIG EACH, ALL CLEAN (41)").
- After converting: 214 gigs become 89 series; occurrences are Standard class (hidden under Important); series appear in Needs Review; the rolling pull still skips recurring instances.

- Files: GigsAndTrips.html, GigsAndTrips.md. `pal-gcal.js` unchanged (v3).
- Tested in Node against a stub Google modelled on real rule strings (zero Google writes, exactly one save, idempotent second run, verdict failure cases, refresh behaviour, managed-series guards). A pure builder for an imported series record (deterministic id `gcal_<Google id>`, Standard class) exists but nothing calls it yet.

### v7.100 — GIG-106, GIG-107 — Repeating events, stage 1: in the app

- Deliberately not the GIG-048 design removed in GIG-060.
- A repeating event is **one gig record** (the series) with a recurrence rule; occurrences are computed when needed, never stored. Changing a single occurrence stores an ordinary gig (exception) pointing back via `recurrenceOf` and `recurrenceOriginalDate`; the series skips that date via `recurrence.exdates`. Cancelling one occurrence adds to `exdates`. Dates are plain calendar dates with wall-clock times (DST-safe). No Supabase schema change.
- Rules: daily; weekly on chosen days; monthly by date, 1st–4th weekday or last weekday; yearly; every N; ends never / on a date / after N. Weeks start Monday; a non-existent monthly date is skipped; 29 Feb only in leap years; COUNT counts before cancellations.
- UI: Repeats section on the gig form; occurrence view (🔁) with Edit this event only / Edit all events / Cancel this event only / Delete all events. A repeating event cannot be in a trip (a single changed occurrence can). Upcoming (next 120 days, capped at 400) and Agenda show occurrences; Past does not.
- Guards: the series record never appears as an extra entry, completion prompt, review candidate, clash or duplicate candidate. Series not synced to Google (changed occurrences sync as single events). Mirror deletion check recognises recurring events by occurrences.
- Known limits: no done/missed/review per occurrence; same-date/day-off warnings ignore occurrences (⚠ clash checks added in v7.101); no "this and following"; converting a Google-linked gig to a series leaves its single Google event.
- No `pal-gcal.js`, launcher or schema change. Tested in Node. Not tested in a browser or against real Google.

### v7.97 — GIG-100 part, GIG-102, GIG-103, GIG-104 part, GIG-105, GIG-115 — Two-way sync for gigs

- Supabase stays the source of truth. Google may change a gig's **title, date, time, location and notes** only. Each gig stores `gcalEtag` and `gcalSyncedHash` (hash of those five fields).
- On every pull: Google unchanged → nothing; Google changed only → applied; both changed → no overwrite, listed under "Calendar changes to review" (per-field, Use Gigs & Trips / Use Google). Gigs linked before this release are silently baselined (edits made in Google before v7.97 are not pulled in).

- Deletions in Google (GIG-103/104 part): linked gigs, trips and items missing from the pull window are checked individually (max 10 per pull; a 500 stops the check). Gone/cancelled → listed for a decision: gigs Remove here / Re-create in Google / Keep, unlink; trips and items re-create or unlink only.
- Not included: Google→app edits for trips/items, scheduled weekly reconciliation, richer hidden metadata (GIG-100 remainder), recurrence. Review entries stored in device-local `gat_gcal_conflicts`, pruned when stale.
- Tested in Node. Not tested against real Google: assumes etag in list/patch responses and 404/410 or `status: cancelled` for deleted events.

#### v7.104 (GIG-117, GIG-116 read direction) — Fold imported repeats into series; Google-managed series

**What your second scan proved.** The checks I could not make before now passed on your real calendar: **the instance-id format matches Google on all 32, 35 and 17 live instances** (timed series across BST/GMT and an all-day series), **this app's engine produces exactly Google's dates** for those series, 56/56, 28/28, 14/14 and 13/13 imported ids match, and the only mismatches are occurrences you changed in Google (a Gym session moved by an hour, two paydays moved earlier). The assumptions behind the sync are now evidence, not guesses.

**New: "🔁 Fold imported repeats into series…" (Sync & Backup → Checks).** Opt-in and safe by design:
- It re-checks Google, shows the verdict and what would change. **Conversion stays switched off unless the checks agree**: a live check must compare real Google instances and match on ids and dates, and any imported id or date that this app cannot reproduce must be explained by an occurrence you changed in Google.
- The buttons are in order: **1 · Download a backup first**, then **2 · Convert now** (disabled until the backup step, refused if the check is over 15 minutes old, and it asks you to confirm).
- It brings in every series this app can represent that either already has gigs imported here or is still running, so your yearly birthdays and anniversaries come in too. Your last scan predicts **89 series (46 replacing imported gigs, 43 running series not imported before), 212 imported gigs folded in, 2 kept as changed occurrences, 14 Google-changed occurrences recorded as exceptions, net −149 KB**.
- **Nothing is written to or deleted from Google Calendar by the conversion.** Everything is local plus Supabase, and it is **one local save for the whole job** (if saving fails, nothing is changed and nothing is pushed).
- A gig you edited, reviewed or reclassified is never discarded: it is kept as a changed occurrence of its series (and that date is excluded from the series). Occurrences changed in Google become exceptions linked to the Google instance, so the existing two-way gig sync keeps them current; cancelled dates and Google's own excluded dates are recorded. A series you deleted, or an exception you deleted, is not brought back, and a series you made inside the app is never overwritten. It is idempotent: running it again finds nothing left to do (the test for this found a real bug in my first version, now fixed: exceptions already created were being rewritten on a second run).

**Google-managed series.** A series made this way is edited in Google and refreshed from Google; the app does not write series to Google yet. So that nothing silently diverges, in the app such a series is read-only: its occurrence view says "managed in Google Calendar" with an Open in Google Calendar link instead of Edit/Cancel, the form shows no repeat controls for it, and Delete says it also deletes from Google Calendar. **Refresh:** automatically once a day after sign-in and from the new "↻ Refresh Google-managed series now" button, and only once a conversion has been done (until then nothing changes). A refresh applies title, time, place, notes, rule and end-date changes, adds newly created running series, and lists a series deleted in Google under "Calendar changes to review" (it never removes it by itself). Series you create inside the app behave exactly as in v7.100.

**Also:** the scan report now folds series with a single clean imported gig into one line ("ONE IMPORTED GIG EACH, ALL CLEAN (41)"), so your report is about 30 lines instead of 250.

**What changes for you after converting.** Those 214 gigs become 89 series; occurrences appear in Upcoming and the Agenda (and are Standard, so hidden under the default Important filter); the series appear in the Needs Review queue ("Keep all" handles them). The rolling Calendar pull continues to skip recurring instances, so nothing is duplicated.

**Not done:** writing series from the app to Google (so editing a Google-managed series in the app, or creating a series that appears in Google, is still to come), "this and following", and automatic refresh more often than daily.

Files changed: `GigsAndTrips.html`, `GigsAndTrips.md`. `pal-gcal.js` unchanged (v3).

**Tested — in Node, with a stub Google modelled on your data (and the real rule strings):** the conversion on a fixture with Gym (Tue/Thu with Google EXDATE, a moved occurrence, a cancelled date, a reviewed instance), Green Bin, a birthday with one import, a running birthday not imported before, and Payday with a moved occurrence: 5 series, 8 gigs folded in, 2 exceptions, 1 kept; the Gym series' excluded dates are exactly Google's EXDATE + the kept gig + the moved date + the cancelled date; the series expands to the right dates and the exceptions appear on theirs; **zero Google writes and exactly one local save**; every changed record pushed once; a second run changes nothing and does not even save; a Google rename / new weekday / new etag updates the series and keeps its exceptions; a deleted series and a deleted exception are not resurrected and an app-made series is not overwritten; a failed save changes and pushes nothing; the verdict passes on a clean fixture and fails for each of: no live check, an id or date difference, Google returning nothing for a running series, a failed check, unexplained mismatches, nothing to convert, while mismatches explained by changed occurrences are allowed; the screen (convert disabled until backup, refused when the backup is missing, the check is stale or you decline, hidden entirely when the verdict fails, sign-in check); daily refresh (silent with nothing Google-managed, once a day, picks up a new series and a Google edit, flags a series deleted in Google without removing it, ignores one Google still has, contains server errors and listing failures, never without a token); managed-series guards (occurrence view, blocked edit and cancel, the form note, delete also from Google); the report grouping. All earlier suites and the launcher test pass; scripts pass `node --check`.

**Not tested:** nothing ran against real Google or in a browser, and the conversion has not been run on your data. The confirm dialog, the screen's look on a phone and the first real conversion are unseen, which is why it is gated, requires the backup step, and is reversible only by restoring that backup.
