- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** a way to mark a planned session as missed (the app only had "Missed — ill" for a whole day) so the launcher alert clears for good.
- **Change (`gym-tracker.html`):** every planned-session row on today's and past days' cards has **✕ Mark missed**. A marked session shows as "✕ <plan> — Marked as missed" with **↩ Undo missed**; the day's chip says **Missed** once nothing else is left that day; Home no longer offers a missed session as today's plan (it says "✕ Missed today"); the Pulse ring counts a day whose only plans were missed as missed; the launcher summary (`publishContract`) leaves a missed session out of the planned sessions. A logged session still counts as done.
- **Storage / sync:** a schedule record `{id 'mis_…', kind:'missed', date, planId, _deleted, createdAt, updatedAt}` in `scheduleEntries`, written and synced exactly like the "Missed — ill" flag (`sbUpsert('schedule', …)`, no new table, no migration); un-marking soft-deletes it and marking again revives the same record. Every reader of schedule entries takes one-offs **without** a kind or `kind === 'repeat'`, so older copies ignore it; JSON export, import and backup carry it as part of `scheduleEntries`.
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, footer, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=2.136`, inline comment: v2.136.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, the real file with the real `pal-shared.js`, fake clock; diff against v2.135 reviewed, 61 changed lines): version strings; both sessions today get Mark missed and a future day does not; marking one shows the missed row with Undo and leaves the other planned; the stored record's shape; it is not mistaken for a one-off plan or a repeat rule; the launcher summary drops the missed session and keeps the others and future ones; Home offers the other plan; all missed → day chip Missed, state `missed`, Home "Missed today", Pulse state miss; Undo tombstones it and the session is planned again; marking again revives the same record; a past day can be marked; a logged session still counts as done; the records are in `scheduleEntries` (export / backup); no page errors. Not tested: the live app with your real plans, a second device syncing the record, a phone.

### v2.135 — GYM-121 — Saved items grouped into Food and Drink; launcher action to log a saved item; open the dialog with a name — 3 Nov 2026

- **Deployment check of v2.134:** all nine Gym tests passed. Pete's notes (against the launcher tests): Saved items should be grouped into food and drink, and the launcher input should only search existing items and open the app to add a new one.
- **Saved items (`renderSavedItemsList()`):** two headed groups, **🍽 Food** then **💧 Drink**, each sorted by name; an empty group is not shown. Each row keeps ⚡ Favourite, Edit and Delete (the per-row icon is dropped now the heading carries it).
- **Launcher action `quickAddSaved { kind, name }`:** logs **one** unit of an existing saved food or drink at its own saved numbers through `logIntake()` — a drink or ⚡ favourite folds into its "×N" card, any other food is a single Edit / Delete row, exactly as in the dialog. Refuses an unknown name ("Not a saved item — open the app to add it") and a saved item with no numbers ("…has no numbers yet — open the app to fix it"). Reply carries the combined day totals plus `addKcal` / `addProtein` / `addMl`; reqId replay protection as for the other quick-adds. `quickAddWater` / `quickAddMeal` are kept (an older launcher still works).
- **`PAL_OPEN { view:'intake', name }`:** opens today's Food & drink dialog and fills the name box (running the search), retrying while the app is still starting.
- **Version:** `<title>`, header badge, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=2.135`, inline comment: 2.135. No data, storage, sync or backup change. Pairs with launcher **v11.48**.
- Tested (Stage 1): `node --check`; the v2.134 suites re-run green (31 + 26 behaviour checks; the differential against original v2.133 still identical on legacy data); new checks: grouped headings and order; `quickAddSaved` for a drink (case-insensitive name, +150 kcal / 30 g / 500 ml, combined totals), a non-favourite food (single row), a favourite food (×2), an unknown name, a saved item with no numbers, and the same reqId twice saving once; `PAL_OPEN` with a name fills the box. Not tested: a real phone, live Supabase, a second device.
- **Known limitations:** unchanged from v2.134. **Flagged:** GYM-121 follows GYM-120; backlog not supplied.

### v2.134 — GYM-120 — One intake (food and drink are categories; any item can carry calories, protein and ml) and food & drink reminders — 3 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** (1) reminders to log food and drink, set somewhere in the Gym app and shown in the launcher's Needs attention at the time set; (2) simplify the input to one "intake": the category (Food / Drink) files it in the right section, every input can carry calories, protein and ml (not all needed) so a protein shake is both a drink and food, the launcher keeps its existing inputs, the larger input keeps quick favourites, and **the targets work off the total of everything logged**.
- **Design decisions (challenged and chosen):** (a) **no new table, no migration** — food entries and drink entries stay in their own lists (`nutritionEntries`, `waterEntries`; saved items in `savedMeals`, `savedWaterItems`) and every record in both now simply shares the same optional numeric fields; the category only decides which list a record is filed in and which day-card section shows it. A single merged list would have needed a Supabase migration and a rewrite of every reader for no visible gain. (b) **Reminders are stored on the existing water-target record** (`waterTargets[].reminders`), one synced record per user, again with no new table; the alternative (a `gym_intake_reminders` table) would have needed SQL run by hand. (c) **The launcher decides when a reminder is due** (see v11.47): a published summary only refreshes when this app runs, which is useless for "at 12:00".
- **Data model (additive; older records, backups and import unchanged):** entries (both lists): `calories`, `protein`, `volumeMl`, and for linked entries `savedItemId`, `count`, `perUnitCal`, `perUnitProtein`, `perUnitMl`; saved items (both lists): `name`, `calories`, `protein`, `volumeMl`, `quickAdd`; water-target record: optional `reminders: [{id, time:'HH:MM', label, kind:'any'|'food'|'drink', on}]`. A record without the new fields counts 0 for them.
- **One form (Food & drink dialog):** Name (search over saved foods **and** drinks), Calories, Protein (g), Volume (ml) — all optional, at least one needed — a **Food / Drink** category, a **⚡ Favourite** flag and one Add button. A blank box takes the saved item's own number; if only the volume differs from the saved item's, calories and protein **scale pro-rata** (250 ml of a 500 ml / 150 kcal shake = 75 kcal) and it is logged as its own entry; typing a number overrides. Typing a name that is exactly one saved item switches the category to it. A food pill still fills the form to tweak; a drink pill still logs one at once (GYM-074) — both as before.
- **One list for the day:** **cards** (− / + stepper, ✎ edit item, 🗑) for every ⚡ favourite and for drinks, now for **foods too**; then **rows** (Edit / Delete) for foods that are not favourites — exactly how foods behaved before. Entries whose saved item was deleted show as rows instead of vanishing from the list (they always counted in the totals). One totals block: calories and protein against the active / rest target, ml against the water target, each **adding food and drink**.
- **Everything that totals now adds both lists** (`getIntakeTotals()`): the dialog, the day Food and Drink cards (Food card counts foods but shows combined calories / protein; Drink card counts drinks but shows combined ml), the home Fuel rings, the active / rest averages (Insights), and the PDF Nutrition and Hydration sections (a drink joins the calorie picture only if it carries calories or protein, a food joins the water picture only if it carries a volume, so plain water never adds empty "0 calorie" days; PDF rows show "×N").
- **One saved-items list, one edit dialog:** "Saved items" replaces Saved Meals + Saved Drinks (⚡ toggle, Edit, Delete for both kinds); one Edit dialog (name, calories, protein, ml, category, favourite) for a saved item **or** a single entry. **Changing the category moves the record to the other list** (the old one becomes a tombstone so the move syncs). Removed: the two separate edit dialogs, the two saved-items dialogs, `renderMealsList()` / `renderWaterList()` and the water-only stepper functions (replaced by `renderIntake()` / `quickIntake*()`).
- **Launcher quick-add (unchanged inputs):** `quickAddMealEntry()` and `quickAddWaterEntry()` now go through the same `logIntake()` path, so a drink typed by name picks up a saved drink's calories / protein; replies carry the **combined** day totals plus `addKcal` / `addProtein` / `addMl` (extra fields only; existing ones keep their meaning). reqId replay protection untouched. A launcher food add now folds into a card if the saved food is a favourite.
- **Reminders (Notes tab, below Water Target):** "⏰ Food & Drink Reminders" — add / edit / remove rows of time, label, "Cleared by" (any food or drink / food / a drink) and On/Off; saved and synced as you change them (each change pushes the water-target record). `PAL_OPEN { view: 'intake' }` (from a launcher reminder) opens today's Food & drink dialog, retrying while the app is still starting.
- **`migrateWaterEntries()`** (runs on every load and pull) now keeps `calories` / `protein` when it builds a saved item for an unlinked drink and sets `perUnitCal` / `perUnitProtein`; without this, a drink moved from Food or edited by hand would have lost its calories on the next load.
- **Version:** `<title>`, header badge, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=2.134`, inline comment: 2.134. `pal-shared.js` itself unchanged. Launcher: **v11.47 needed** for the Gym card totals and the reminders (the app works without it, but the launcher card would then show food-only calories and drink-only water).
- Tested (Stage 1; `node --check`; headless Chromium with a stub `pal-shared.js` that records every push; fixed seeds): **differential run, original v2.133 vs v2.134, on legacy-shaped data (no new fields, linked and unlinked drinks, a fully-logged-day flag, a quick-add of each kind through the launcher message): home Fuel rings, day Food and Drink cards, Insights averages card, PDF Nutrition and Hydration blocks, and the quick-add replies' existing fields — all identical.** **57 behaviour checks, all passing**, through the real UI — food as a single row, repeat taking the saved numbers; a drink with 150 cal / 30 g / 500 ml saved as a favourite; combined totals in the dialog, the Fuel rings and both day cards; water-only adds ml only; a food with ml counts toward water; + / − on a favourite drink and a favourite food; 250 ml pro-rata and its own entry (saved item not overwritten); a new item with no numbers refused; pushes go only to the four existing entry / saved-item tables; Food→Drink move leaves totals unchanged and tombstones the old record; saved-item delete leaves totals and the entry (as a row); launcher quick-add by name picks up saved calories / protein, folds repeats, scales pro-rata, refuses empty food, same reqId saves once; reminders created on the water-target record (target 0), time / label / kind / On-Off stored, saving the water target keeps them and vice versa, every change pushed to `gym_water_targets`, empty time ignored; averages and PDF include a drink's calories ("Protein shake ×2 (300 cal, 60g)"), plain water adds no empty day; reload, backup export and re-import give identical totals and reminders; the migration keeps a drink's calories / protein; `PAL_OPEN { view: 'intake' }` opens the dialog. Screenshots at 390 px and 1280 px reviewed (dialog, saved items, edit, reminders).
- **Not tested:** a real iPhone / Android phone (touch, keyboard, safe areas, the bottom sheet), real Safari, the real `pal-shared.js` and live Supabase (writes verified at the stub, and the real `pull()` merge of the new fields is untested), a second device (a device still on v2.133 sums only its own lists and ignores the new fields until updated), your real data volumes, printing the PDF, the dialog inside the launcher's iframe.
- **Known limitations:** (1) foods that are not favourites are still single rows (no ×N) so each log can be edited; a drink entry is edited by − and re-adding, or by ✎ on the card (changes the saved item going forward). (2) Pro-rata scaling assumes calories and protein scale with volume (right for milk, wrong for a shake mixed with different scoops — type the numbers). (3) The inline comment block above now holds 16 releases (the older ones live in `gym-tracker.md`, not supplied, so it was not trimmed). (4) Targets themselves are unchanged (calories / protein by active or rest day, one water target).
- **Flagged, not changed:** the viewport tag still blocks pinch-zoom (first flagged in v2.131). The backlog was not supplied, so **GYM-120 follows GYM-119** in this changelog (not confirmed against the backlog).

### v2.131 — GYM-117 — "Pulse" look and feel: phone and desktop layouts, new summary elements — 1 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 1 Nov):** a look-and-feel refresh in the same family as Gigs & Trips v7.109 (GIG-122), with the app's own personality, **without changing functionality**.
- **Not changed (frozen):** every feature and workflow, data structure, localStorage key (`gym_tracker_v1`, `gym_pal_xapp` and the rest), Supabase table and sync path, JSON backup / import, program import, PDF report, the launcher messages (`GYM_ACTION` / `GYM_PONG`, `GYM_DATA_UPDATED`) and `pal-shared.js`. No new dependency; still one standalone HTML file. No new stored data: every new element reads data the app already holds.
- **Look (shared family DNA):** warm "paper" light theme (#F4F0E6) and deep dark theme (#0E0D12) — the theme still follows the launcher's light / dark setting, and the app keeps its own existing default of **dark when no preference is set**; one signal accent (lime in dark, ink on paper in light) used for the primary button and the active tab / chip; Bricolage Grotesque for titles, dates and big numbers and DM Sans for the rest (Google Fonts, system fonts offline); CSS-variable tokens for colour, radius, spacing and type. The old variable names (`--accent`, `--accent2`…`5`, `--ink`, `--surface`…) are kept as aliases because the JavaScript-rendered markup uses them inline.
- **Gym Tracker's own signature ("Pulse"):** a **seven-segment week ring** (Mon → Sun) as the hero, with ember (training), ion (water) and iris (protein) as the app's secondary colours; ticket-style **date stubs** on the day cards.
- **Responsive, not device-sniffing:** layout follows the window width on one DOM — under 700 px phone, 700–1099 px tablet (phone layout in a centred column), 1100 px and over desktop. `data-layout` records which; it is CSS media queries plus a `matchMedia` listener (and `orientationchange`) that re-tags the page and re-measures the header offset. Nothing is re-rendered on resize, so an open dialog or typed text survives it.
- **Phone / tablet:** header (logo, version, sync chip) and a **floating bottom bar** (Home, Insights, Plans, Exercises, Notes — same buttons and `switchTab()` as before, now with line icons); dialogs are **bottom sheets** with a grab handle; the toast sits above the bar; safe areas respected (`viewport-fit=cover`).
- **Desktop:** the same nav becomes a **left rail** with a "Start" button on top (it starts today's plan, or opens the plan picker); **Home** is two columns (a sticky left panel with the ring, fuel rings and weight, and the week with day cards in two columns, today's card full width); **Insights** is a two-column grid (Period Overview, Consistency, Progress, Weight, Body Areas, What To Train Next, then the exercise list in two columns); **Plans** (programs | other / archived), **Exercises** (tools | two-column library), **Notes** (notes | report and targets) are two columns; dialogs are centred; the **active session** gets a wider workbench with a **session outline** pane (jump to an exercise, sets done per exercise).
- **New elements (all display-only, from existing data):** (1) **week ring + today line + Start button** (segments = days with a session / PT / ill / missed / planned; centre = the existing "sessions this week" count; the button starts today's plan, or opens the plan picker); (2) **week strip** (follows ◀ ▶; each chip shows done / PT / ill / missed / planned; tap scrolls to and flashes that day's card); (3) **today's fuel rings** (calories, protein, water against today's own targets; amber when over; tap opens Food & drink); (4) **weight sparkline** on the weight tile; (5) **12-week consistency grid** in Insights (one cell per day, weeks trained and session count); (6) **sets-done bar** in the active session header (all sizes). Day cards also gain a date stub, a status chip (Done / Planned / Rest / Ill / PT) and a state colour bar.
- **Restyled only (same markup and behaviour):** Plans, Exercises, Notes, Insights cards, chips, badges, form controls, the session cards, Data & Backup drawer and every dialog inherit the new tokens and controls (bigger tap targets: buttons ≥ 38 px, chips ≥ 36 px, tab buttons 44 px+, set tick 38 px). Screen-only inline colours that were hard-coded (#f78166, #e3b341, #38bdf8, rgba blues / ambers) now use tokens; **the PDF report keeps its fixed print colours**.
- **Code touched outside CSS / HTML shell (all display-only):** `renderCalendar()` (day-card head markup + one `renderPulse()` call), `renderHomeWeight()` (sparkline call), `renderInsights()` (consistency call), `renderSessionItems()` (progress call), `switchTab()` (`aria-current`), `adjustBodyScrollTop()` (publishes `--chrome-h` for the rail), `applyTheme()` (meta colours only), and the new block before BOOT (`syncLayout`, `dayState`, `renderWeekRing`, `homeTodayInfo`, `homeCtaAction`, `renderHomeToday`, `fuelDial`, `renderHomeFuel`, `renderHomeWeightSpark`, `renderWeekStrip`, `jumpToCalDay`, `renderPulse`, `renderConsistency`, `updateSessionProgress`, `jumpToSessionCard`). No element ID was removed (checked), no CSS class used by the JS markup was dropped (checked).
- **Launcher:** no change. Launcher v11.27 reads `gym_tracker_v1` (`scheduleEntries` incl. `kind:'illness'`), `gym_pal_xapp` and the `GYM_PONG` version — all unchanged (the version shown is read from the app). `index.html` not supplied and not touched.
- Version: `<title>`, header `.ver`, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=`, inline comment set to 2.131 (`pal-shared.js` itself is unchanged).
- Tested (Stage 1; headless Chromium, offline stub of `pal-shared.js` with an in-memory mock cloud, fixture data relative to today, Supabase not reachable): **differential run, original v2.130 vs v2.131, same scripted workflows with a fixed random seed, local-only and with a mock sync session — saved `localStorage` (every key), exported JSON backup, every record pushed to sync, toasts and key screen values identical**: start a plan session, tick all sets, finish and decline the plan prompt, freestyle start / cancel, mark ill on / off / on, fully-logged day, log weight, add meal, quick water, PT session, add note, schedule a plan, week navigation, all tabs and Insights windows / filters, nutrition and water targets, edit plan, new exercise, add exercise to a session and reorder, archive plan, merge mode select, delete weight, tick and archive notes, generate report (report markup length equal), export, wipe + import the backup, and a pull of a change made "on another device". **UI suite (126 checks, all passing):** layout tag and navigation placement at 320, 360, 390, 820, 1360 and 1920 px; floating bar vs rail; two-column grids on desktop only; dialogs are bottom sheets on phone / tablet and centred on desktop; no sideways scroll or overflow on any tab at any width; tap targets; **live resize** 1360 → 390 → 820 → 1360 (700 / 699 / 1099 / 1100 boundaries, and a rotated phone) keeps the open dialog, the typed text and the active tab; each new element (ring segments vs data, today's plan in the hero and the button starting it, session bar following ticks and untick, week strip states / tap-to-scroll / follows the week arrows, fuel rings reading totals and updating after logging a meal and turning amber over target, sparkline, consistency grid cells and today marker); an empty app (no data) renders on every tab without errors; dark and light backgrounds, fonts, live theme switch and colour-contrast ratios for the ink and accent tokens on all three surfaces. No page errors. Performance with 2,000 extra sessions: `renderAll` 141 ms → 144 ms, `renderCalendar` 1.7 ms → 3 ms.
- **Not tested:** a real iPhone / Android phone (touch, safe areas, the on-screen keyboard, the floating bar over the home indicator), real Safari, the real `pal-shared.js` and live Supabase (the write path is verified at the stub), a second device, the app running inside the launcher's iframe (including how the desktop rail sits beside the launcher's own navigation), your real data volumes, print / "Save as PDF" output (the report markup is identical; only the page chrome around it changed), and the look of the plan editor, merge mode, saved-meals, program-schedule and Data & Backup dialogs beyond the shared colours and controls.
- **Known limitations / not restyled:** the PDF report keeps its blue print styling (deliberate). Plan editor, merge mode, saved meals / drinks, program schedule and import dialogs keep their old layouts in the new colours. Many small inline text sizes (9–11 px sub-labels) are unchanged. The active-session cards stay one column on desktop (the ▲ ▼ buttons reorder one place at a time, which would be confusing in a grid) — the outline pane is the desktop addition. The ring's centre number is the existing count of **sessions** this week, so two sessions on one day show 2 with one segment lit. Today's fuel rings use today's active / rest target, which flips as soon as a plan is scheduled or a session logged (existing rule). Google Fonts need a connection the first time. The app's own default (dark when no theme is set) differs from Gigs & Trips (light); kept as it was.
- **Flagged, not changed (needs your decision):** the viewport tag still has `maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no`, which blocks pinch-zoom — recommend removing it (an accessibility problem; iOS Safari already ignores it). The Gym Tracker backlog was not supplied for this task, so **GYM-117 is the next number after GYM-116 in this changelog**, not one confirmed against the backlog.

### v2.130 — GYM-116 — Mark a day as "missed — ill" (😷)

- **Why (Pete, 1 Nov):** be able to set a day as missed due to illness, shown with 😷 on the launcher card.
- **Design decision:** stored as a schedule record `{id, kind:'illness', date, _deleted, createdAt, updatedAt}` in `scheduleEntries`, not a new array. It syncs through the existing `gym_schedule` table, so **no new Supabase table and no migration**. Every existing reader treats schedule entries as one-offs (no `kind`) or `kind==='repeat'`, so it is ignored by plan resolution, "This day only", repeat rules and `isActiveDay()`; older app copies on other devices ignore it the same way. The cost is that the record shares an array with plans; the alternative (a dedicated `illnessDays` array and table, like `fullyLoggedDays`) would need a database migration for a one-bit flag.
- **Change (`gym-tracker.html`):** every calendar day card has a "😷 Mark day as missed — ill" button (any date; tap again to undo). A marked day shows "· 😷 Ill" in its header and the button becomes "😷 Missed — ill (tap to undo)". New `getIllDays()`, `isIllDay()`, `toggleIllDay()`, `renderDayIllnessToggle()`. Un-marking soft-deletes (tombstone) so it syncs; re-marking the same date revives the same record (one record per date). A session logged on the day still counts as done.
- **Not changed (deliberately):** the weekly streak (`currentStreakWeeks`) and the active/rest-day calorie and protein targets (`isActiveDay`) ignore the flag, so a planned workout on an ill day still counts as an active day for targets and a week lost entirely to illness still breaks the streak. Either could be made illness-aware on request.
- **Data model:** additive; existing data, backup / JSON import-export and sync unchanged.
- Version: title, `.ver`, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=`, inline comment set to 2.130.
- Tested (Stage 1): `node --check`; headless Chromium with a stubbed `pal-shared.js`: button on all 7 day cards; marking sets the header, flips the button and writes `{kind:'illness'}` to localStorage and pushes it to `gym_schedule`; the record is not seen by one-off / repeat / plan resolution and `isActiveDay` is unchanged; undo leaves one tombstoned record, re-mark revives it; flag survives a reload; no page errors. Launcher side: see v11.27. Not tested: real `pal-shared.js` and live Supabase (the write path is verified at the stub), a second device pulling the record, phone / Safari, importing an old backup (code path untouched).

### v2.129 — GYM-115 — Active session: ▲▼ follow the moved exercise; header buttons no longer toggle collapse on a phone

- **Why (Pete, 25 Oct, after v2.128):** (1) when moving an exercise with the arrows the view should stay with that exercise; (2) on the phone, tapping the arrows sometimes collapsed/expanded the card instead.
- **Cause (2), diagnosed from the code, not reproduced on a device:** the ▲ ▼ ✕ buttons were 24px, 2px apart, directly beside the full-width collapse tap area (`.tec-left`, `flex:1`). After a move the card jumped away and the next tap landed on a different card's title. Small targets, no `touch-action`, and the page not following the card combined to cause stray toggles.
- **Change (`gym-tracker.html`):** `moveSessionItem()` measures the card's screen position before the move and scrolls the session body afterwards so the moved card stays under the finger (falls back to scroll-into-view if clamped at the ends). Session-card header buttons (▲ ▼ ✕) are now 36px with 6px gaps in a non-shrinking `.tec-ctl` group, and `touch-action:manipulation`. Styles are scoped to `.tec-head`, so the plan editor's ▲▼ are unchanged.
- **Data model:** none; view only.
- **Unchanged:** collapse behaviour, GYM-114 reveal, auto-save, circuits (still no arrows), launcher, `pal-shared.js`.
- Version: title, `.ver`, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=`, inline comment set to 2.129.
- Tested (Stage 1): syntax check; headless Chromium in 390×700 touch emulation: three ▼ taps then one ▲ on the same exercise each moved it exactly one place and the card stayed at the same screen position (±1px) so each tap hit the same exercise; no card collapsed or expanded during the taps; buttons measure 36×36. Not tested: real iPhone touch behaviour (the stray-toggle fix is unproven until Pete tries it), live Supabase, second device.

### v2.128 — GYM-114 — Active session: after a card auto-collapses, the next exercise is expanded and scrolled into view

- **Why (Pete, 25 Oct, after v2.127):** when an exercise completes and its card collapses, the user should be shown the next exercise (the page was left wherever the shrinking card put it).
- **Change (`gym-tracker.html`):** `autoCollapseIfCompleted()` (GYM-112) now also picks the next card to work on: the first card **not yet completed after** the one just finished, otherwise the first not-completed card anywhere (e.g. one skipped earlier). That card is **expanded if it was collapsed** and scrolled to the top of the session body (smooth) after the next render. A circuit counts as one card and is "completed" only when all its exercises are. Nothing is scrolled when no unfinished card remains (the GYM-113 auto-save bar takes over). Works for both triggers (tick of the last set and set-timer completion). New view-only `_revealCardKey`; cards carry a `data-cidx` attribute; `.track-ex-card{scroll-margin-top:8px}`.
- **Data model:** none; view state only (not saved, synced, drafted or exported).

### v2.127 — GYM-113 — Auto-save when every exercise is complete (5-second countdown with Cancel)

- **Why (Pete, 24 Oct, after v2.126):** once all exercises are complete the session should save itself.

- **Change (`gym-tracker.html`):** when ticking a set (or a set timer) makes the last exercise of a **new** session Completed (every exercise completed, every set ticked), the bar appears; at 0 it calls `finishActiveSession()`, i.e. exactly the Finish Session path (save, sync, "save as plan" / "update plan targets" prompt). Cancel stops it for that session until a set is unticked and the last one re-ticked. Not applied when editing a saved session, on an empty session, or when restoring a draft that is already complete. The countdown is also cleared by Finish and Cancel session, and re-checked at 0 so adding a set during the countdown aborts the save. Helpers: `maybeStartAutoFinish()`, `cancelAutoFinish()`, `sessionAllComplete()`.
- **Data model:** none; countdown state is in memory only. Saved data is identical to a manual Finish.
- **Unchanged:** Finish button, cancel, GYM-076 "complete all?" prompt, plan prompts, everything from v2.126.

### v2.121 — GYM-107 — Plan editor and exercise library overhaul (1-set default, collapsible plan items, tick-box picker, merge, import matching)

- **Why (Pete, 22 Oct):** adding an exercise created three sets that then had to be edited; a long plan was hard to reorder; the library showed no link to plans and let duplicates build up; importing a trainer program created near-duplicate exercises and broke progression; and the plan editor had too many note fields.
- **Change (`gym-tracker.html`):**
  - **1 set by default.** A newly added plan item starts with one target set (reps/weight, time or distance). Type in the numbers and **+ Add Set** copies the last set. `defaultTargetSetsForType()` itself is unchanged, so a type switch or cascade still seeds its previous defaults.
  - **Collapsed plan items.** In the plan editor each item is one row: name, type, "N sets · 8×60kg x3", note count, ▲ ▼ ✕. Tap the name to expand/collapse; **Expand all / Collapse all** sits beside the time total. New items open expanded. Circuit members are collapsed the same way; the circuit header (rounds, move, remove) stays visible. Collapse state is editor-only (`_planExpanded`) and is not saved. Items missing an `id` get one when the editor opens.
  - **Notes review.** Each expanded item previously showed two always-open textareas (exercise note, this-plan note) in addition to the plan-level Notes field. They now sit behind one **📝 Notes (n)** toggle per item (closed by default; count shows how many are filled). The plan-level Notes field, the session screen's notes and the Notes tab are unchanged. Behaviour of the fields is unchanged: the exercise note still saves immediately, the plan note on Save Plan.
  - **Tick-box picker** (replaces "Choose Exercise"). Tick/untick, search by name or tag, **Done** applies the changes (Done shows +n/−n). Groups: *In this plan* (already assigned, ticked), *Used in other plans* (with "also in n other plans"), *Not used in any plan*. Removals are staged and confirmed on Done, so nothing is lost by an accidental untick. "+ Create New" still adds the new exercise to the plan.
  - **Library grouping.** *In plans* (shows count and the first three plan names) then *Not in any plan*. "Used" counts live, non-archived plans only; an exercise used only in archived plans appears under *Not in any plan*. Day-only copies (GYM-106) are not counted.
  - **Merge…** on each library card: choose the exercise to keep (same type only, likely matches ranked first). The merged exercise's sessions (`exerciseId` + stored `exerciseName`), plans including hidden day copies, and saved circuits are re-pointed at the kept exercise; tags are combined, differing notes appended; the merged exercise is soft-deleted (normal tombstone). History and progression therefore continue under one exercise. Plan targets are not touched. Blocked while a session is in progress.
  - **Import matching.** Program import now lists every exercise name not in the library, with a suggested existing match (name similarity, same type only; incline/decline/single/close etc. are treated as different exercises) and defaults to merging only on a strong match, otherwise "Add as new". Choosing a match maps the imported plan items to the existing exercise but the plan keeps the imported reps/weights. Cancel aborts the import with nothing created. The import body moved into `runProgramImport(bundle, overrides)`; with no unmatched names (or an empty library) it runs exactly as before.
- **Data model:** no new fields on any record and no schema or sync change. Merge writes through the existing session/plan/savedCircuit/exercise upserts.
- **Unchanged:** launcher (v11.23, not edited), `pal-shared.js`, JSON export/import, localStorage keys, deleteExercise, session screen.

### v2.120 — GYM-106 — Edit a scheduled plan for one day only

- **Why (Pete, 22 Oct):** editing a plan from a future day changed it everywhere (plans are shared by id across all days and repeats). He wanted the option to change just that day.
- **Change (`gym-tracker.html`):**
  - Each pending plan row in the calendar has **✏️ This day only**. The schedule edit screen (tap a plan row) has **Edit exercises for this day only** next to the existing "(all days)" button. The plan editor opens titled "Edit for <date> only"; saving there leaves the standard plan and every other day untouched, and skips the "update all" warning.
  - Mechanism: no new schedule fields beyond a link. Saving creates a hidden copy of the plan (`dayCopyOf`, `dayCopyDate`). One-off day: the entry's `planId` points to the copy. Repeat day: that date is added to the rule's `exceptions` and a one-off entry (`fromRuleId`) for the copy is created. Because the day resolves through the normal one-off path, starting the session, done detection and the launcher work unchanged.
  - `getPlans()` excludes copies, so they never show in Plans, pickers, programs, or archived lists. Plan cards' "done N times" also count sessions logged against their day copies.
  - A day with a copy shows "✏️ edited for this day" and **↩ Standard plan**, which discards the edit (repeat day: removes the exception and the one-off; one-off: points back at the standard plan; the copy is tombstoned). Editing an already-copied day updates that copy only.
  - The existing edit (all days) path is unchanged, including its confirmation.
- **Data additions (backwards compatible):** plan `dayCopyOf`, `dayCopyDate`; schedule one-off `fromRuleId`. Other devices must also be on v2.120, otherwise they would list the hidden copies in their plan lists.
- **Known limitations:** exercise-level history/insights group by exercise so are unaffected, but plan-level history for a session done on a copy is named like the standard plan and counted under it only in the "done N times" line; a copy cannot be reverted once a session is logged against it (the button only shows for undone plans); the day-only editor still shows the program dropdown but ignores it.
- **Unchanged:** launcher (v11.23, not edited), weekly schedule from v2.118/2.119, data model otherwise, JSON export/import.
- Version: title, `.ver`, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=`, inline comment set to 2.120.
- Tested (Stage 1): syntax check; scripted runs of the real functions: day-only on a repeat day and on a one-off day, standard plan untouched, other days unchanged, copy hidden from lists, no confirm in day-only mode, re-edit updates the same copy, revert for both origins, normal all-days edit still confirms and updates; earlier suites still pass.
- Not tested: real browser (button layout, editor title), live Supabase, second device.

### v2.116 — GYM-102 — One cloud pull per open, not two — 18 Oct 2026

- **Why (measured):** the v11.22 timeline from Pete's phone showed Gym starting all 16 table reads at 17631 ms and the same 16 again at 17727 ms. On open the launcher pushes `PAL_SESSION` and Gym also asks for one (`PAL_REQUEST_SESSION`), so `onSession` fired twice about 100 ms apart and each ran a full `pullFromCloud()` (32 requests; two concurrent merges into the same data).
- **Change (`gym-tracker.html`):** `pullFromCloud()` is single-flight. A call made while a pull is running joins it (its callback runs when that pull ends). If the running pull ended with errors and was joined, exactly one retry runs, so a fresher token from the second session event is still used. A callback that throws can no longer leave the guard stuck. `onSession` additionally skips its pull when one finished successfully within the last 3 s (session path only; **manual Pull and Push always pull**, preserving the GYM-010 pull-before-push rule). Pull/merge logic, tombstones, `_envGeneration` discard, retry queue: unchanged. Later pulls (manual, token refresh after 3 s, next open) behave as before.
- **Shared file:** loads the slimmed `pal-shared.js?v=2.116` (comments only, code identical).
- **Unchanged:** data model, localStorage, JSON export/import, Supabase schema and sync behaviour, quick-add, everything else.
- Version: title, `.ver`, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=`, inline comment set to 2.116.
- Tested (Stage 1, real Chromium, Supabase mocked in the browser): old gym fires 32 table reads for two session events, new fires 16 (overlapping, and 1.5 s apart); a session event >3 s later pulls again (32); manual Pull right after a pull still pulls; three overlapping calls = one pull and all three callbacks run once; later pulls normal; a throwing callback does not stick the guard; failed first pull plus joined second event = exactly one retry (16 failed + 16 retry); failed pull with no second event does not auto-retry; merged local data identical old vs new; opening Gym through the launcher with 300 ms request latency halves Gym's reads (old 36, new 18, the extra 2 per pull being trainer-notes reads an empty account triggers); no page errors.
- Not tested: live Supabase with real data, real timing on the phone, a second device, token expiry mid-pull.

### v2.115 — GYM-101 — Quick-add safe on first open / slow load

- **Change (`gym-tracker.html`):** (1) `GYM_ACTION` `ping` replies `GYM_PONG { ready, version }`; `ready` = `init()` has run and the first cloud pull has settled (or 12 s since boot). (2) `_gymQuickSeen` is now a Map of reqId → result: a repeated reqId re-sends the stored result and never saves twice. (3) Quick-added records are tracked in `_gymQuickPending`; `pullFromCloud` calls `gymQuickReapply()` after its merge, which restores and re-upserts any tracked record the merge dropped. (4) `pullFromCloud` marks the first pull as settled via a wrapped callback (all its exit paths already call `cb`).
- **Unchanged:** data model, other message handling, sync logic otherwise.
- Version: title, `.ver`, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=`, inline changelog set to 2.115.
- Tested (Stage 1): syntax check; simulated slow load against the real handler and launcher code: messages sent before the app's listener exists are lost (as in a real iframe) and nothing is saved until the app reports ready, then exactly one entry; replies lost twice still give one entry and the popup; never ready or an app that does not answer pings gives NOT_READY with nothing saved and inputs kept; ready logic (init only, init + pull); pull dropping a tracked record restores it once; duplicate reqId re-replies without a second entry; earlier drink, food, PT and card tests re-run (two expectations updated: duplicates now re-send the stored result).
- Not tested: real iframe load timing on a phone or slow network, real cloud pull merge behaviour (`pal-sync.js` not available to me, so the restore step is a safety net based on assumption), live Supabase.

### v2.114 — GYM-100 — PT session makes the day an active day

- **Change (`gym-tracker.html`):** `isActiveDay(date)` now also returns true when a non-deleted PT session exists on the date. Consequences: PT days use the active-day nutrition targets and show the 🏋️ Active tag (Food & drink modal, summaries); the calendar day card shows "✓ 🧑‍🏫 PT session logged — active day" instead of "No plan scheduled" when nothing is planned. The existing 🧑‍🏫 PT card/Edit/Delete is unchanged and remains the PT's own marker.
- **Unchanged:** data model, sync, export/import. A plan scheduled on a PT day is not auto-completed (that would create a false session record).
- Version: title, `.ver`, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=`, inline changelog set to 2.114.
- Tested (Stage 1): syntax check; scripted runs of the real `isActiveDay` and the launcher card code with PT-only, PT plus session, PT plus pending plan, deleted PT, and no-PT days.
- Not tested: real browser, live data, phone, second device. Past days already carrying a PT session change from rest to active in targets and tags (derived, not stored).

### v2.113 — GYM-099 — Launcher food quick-add receiver

- **Change (`gym-tracker.html`):** `GYM_ACTION` / `quickAddMeal` handled by `handleQuickAddMeal` → `quickAddMealEntry(calories, protein, label)`. Requires a name and at least calories or protein (limits 10000 kcal / 1000 g). Creates a `nutritionEntries` record for today and, if the name is new, a saved meal (same rule as `saveMealEntry`; existing saved meals are never altered). Saves via `save()` + `sbUpsert`, refreshes calendar and the open Food & drink list, replies `totalKcal`, `targetKcal`, `totalProtein`, `targetProtein` (base daily targets). Duplicate `reqId`s ignored. Drink handler unchanged.
- Version: title, `.ver`, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=`, inline changelog set to 2.113. No data-model change.
- Tested (Stage 1): syntax check; scripted runs of the real handler code (valid food, protein-only, missing name, no numbers, duplicate reqId, saved meal created once, drink path still works).
- Not tested: real browser, live Supabase, second device, phone.

### v2.112 — GYM-098 — Launcher drink quick-add receiver

- **Change (`gym-tracker.html`):** new `message` handling for `GYM_ACTION` / `quickAddWater` (same-origin guard unchanged). `handleQuickAddWater` → `quickAddWaterEntry(amount, label)`: validates 1–10000 ml; a name matching a saved drink with the same volume adds one to that drink's entry for today (as the +1 button); otherwise creates a plain water entry (default name "Water"). Saves via `save()` + `sbUpsert('waterEntry')`, refreshes calendar (and the open Food & drink modal), replies `GYM_QUICKADD_RESULT { reqId, ok, msg, totalMl, targetMl }`. Duplicate `reqId`s are ignored.
- **Unchanged:** data model, sync, export/import, existing water UI.
- Version: title, `.ver`, `VERSION`, `pal-shared.js?v=`, inline changelog set to 2.112.
- Tested (Stage 1): syntax check of inline scripts; scripted runs of the real files (launcher card render states, quick-add round trip incl. invalid amount, duplicate reqId, no-ack); version strings consistent.
- Not tested: real browser, live Supabase sync, second device, phone.
- Known limitation: a drink name matching a saved drink but with a different volume is stored as a plain entry (migration may later link it by name).

### v2.110 — GYM-096 — Local cache trim on sync (retrospective)

- ⚠ Added retrospectively from the inline comment block in the v2.110 `gym-tracker.html`; not originally logged here.

### v5.2 — Suite WP0.2c — Dates taken in the first hour after midnight in British Summer Time — 4 Nov 2026

- **Defect:** five places took "today" from `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, which is the UTC date. Between 00:00 and 01:00 local time during British Summer Time that is yesterday: the starting-balance transaction created with a new bucket, the default date of the add-transaction form and its fallback when the date is left empty, and the default and fallback name of a checkpoint. Entries could therefore be dated a day early. At any other time, and all winter, the results were identical.
- **Fix (`horizon.html`):** all five now use `todayISO()` from `pal-shared.js` (local date, already loaded by this app). Stored dates keep their `YYYY-MM-DD` shape; no existing record is changed.
- **Version sync:** `VERSION`, header badge, `pal-shared.js` tag and inline changelog: 5.2 (the tag was `?v=5.1`). `state.version` stored in the data follows `VERSION`, as in every earlier release.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, Europe/London, fixed clocks): at 00:30 BST the old v5.1 checkpoint date was the previous day and v5.2 is today; at BST midday and 00:30 in winter old and new agree; badge v5.2; no page errors. The other four sites are the same textual replacement and were checked by search (no UTC date conversion left in the file), not exercised one by one. **Not tested:** real iPhone/Safari, saving and syncing a transaction. Covered by the deployment check.

### v5.0 — HZN-016 — "Meridian" look and feel: light and dark themes, phone and desktop layouts — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 2 Nov):** a look-and-feel refresh in the same family as Gigs & Trips v7.109 (GIG-122) and the apps refreshed since, with its own personality, **without changing functionality**; light / dark "working as the others do". Built from the approved "Meridian" design canvas. Pete's four decisions were all the recommended option: **Age Line hero**; **load Bricolage Grotesque and DM Sans** (reverses the HZN-013 font drop); **slim top strip when nested inside On Budget**; **Today's £ / Future £ shortcut chip**. No backlog exists for this app (confirmed by Pete).
- **Theme (new):** Horizon was dark-only and ignored the launcher. It now follows the launcher like the other apps: `localStorage.pal_theme` is read before first paint (inline `<head>` script), `PAL_THEME` messages (same-origin only) and `storage` events on `pal_theme` switch it live, via `applyThemeCore()` from `pal-shared.js`; no toggle of its own. The storage-event path matters because On Budget does not relay `PAL_THEME` to the Horizon iframe. Light is the default (warm paper #F4F0E6); dark is night #0E0D12. Scenario and bucket colours that are used as hex in SVG / inline styles are refreshed on every theme change (`refreshPalette()`).
- **Tokens and type:** family palette with one signal accent (ink on paper, lime #CBF55C in dark) used for the primary button and the active tab only; Horizon's own Sun (buy), Teal (rent / growth), Ember, Coral and Violet (buckets). Legacy variable names (`--panel`, `--panel-alt`, `--muted`, `--accent`, `--teal`, `--danger` …) are kept so every inline style generated by the render functions works in both themes; five inline uses where `--accent` meant amber now use `--sun`. Bricolage Grotesque for titles and big numbers, DM Sans for everything else (Google Fonts; system fallback offline); `--mono` now resolves to DM Sans with tabular figures.
- **Layout by width, one DOM:** phone < 700 px, tablet 700–1099 px (phone layout in a centred column), desktop ≥ 1100 px. CSS media queries do the layout; a `matchMedia` listener keeps `data-layout` current and redraws the width-sensitive SVGs. Phone / tablet: floating bottom bar (Scenarios, Mortgage, Setup). Desktop: left rail with the brand, the three tabs, a Today's £ / Future £ control and the sync badge; Scenarios, one-pager and Setup use two columns. **Nested inside On Budget** (detected as "my parent is not the top window", or the referrer is `on-budget`): one slim strip on top, no bottom bar, no rail. Dialogs are bottom sheets on phone / tablet and centred on desktop.
- **New elements, all from data already held (no new stored data):** the **Age Line** (today → 90: buy age, retirement half-sun, guaranteed-pension span, the age each growth pot runs out); four **tiles** (monthly surplus, deposit-readiness ring from `computeHouseReadinessProgress`, buckets total, emergency pot); **surplus split bar** from `computeBucketFlows` (also on the Buckets readout; outlined red when over-committed); **rent-versus-buy chart** with £ axis, retire and buy markers (`buildChartSVG` now takes its size from the layout); **retirement meters** on each scenario card (`availableReal` of `neededReal`); **milestone chips** and a net-worth headline on the one-pager; **Life costs** (block 6): the one-off costs as a timeline, one row per category, replacing the diamonds drawn on the chart line and the plain-text list; one-pager in two columns on desktop; **Setup section chips** (one panel at a time on phone / tablet, jump links on desktop); **empty states** for "no mortgage selected" and "no buckets"; per-bucket colours shared between the bar and the cards; deposit ring on the growth bucket row.
- **Today's £ / Future £ shortcut:** hero chip on phone / tablet and a control in the desktop rail, both calling the existing `setDisplayMode()`; the Setup switch stays and follows.
- **Behaviour deliberately unchanged:** every calculation, record kind, `horizon_state_v1`, `horizon_records` paths, sync, soft delete, export / import, On Budget import, tab names, the three tabs, "tap a scenario card opens the one-pager" (also on desktop), all dialogs and their fields.
- **Small presentation changes to be aware of:** long explanatory paragraphs under each Setup panel title are folded into "About this section" (text unchanged); the eyebrow / tagline and the amber rule at the top of Scenarios are gone (the Age Line replaces them); the one-off diamonds no longer appear on the chart (see Life costs); chart y-axis starts at £0 when no value is negative.
- **Versions:** `VERSION`, the header badge, the rail caption and `pal-shared.js?v=` all read 5.0 (they disagreed before: badge and script v4.13, `VERSION` 4.12). `pal-shared.js` itself is unchanged.
- **Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium over a local server, real `pal-shared.js`, Supabase and Google Fonts blocked):** the identical scripted UI workflow (add / edit / delete income and outgoings, buckets, transactions, pension, one-off, mortgage + select, target preset, birth date, checkpoint, tracker year, display mode) on v4.13 and v5.0 leaves **identical stored state** (record kinds, data, settings; ids and timestamps normalised); JSON export has the same top-level shape, imports back to the same state, and an export made by the old build imports into the new one; 41 layout checks, all passing: layout tag and bar / rail at 390, 820 and 1360 px, no sideways scroll on Scenarios, one-pager, Mortgage and every Setup view, **live resize** 1360 → 390 → 820 → 1360 and the 700 / 1100 boundaries with the Age Line redrawn, dark at load from `pal_theme`, live switch by `PAL_THEME` and by a `storage` event from another tab, a foreign-origin message ignored, chart colours following the theme, both display-mode shortcuts, Setup chips on phone and desktop, bottom-sheet versus centred dialog, fresh-install empty states, nested-in-On-Budget strip and standalone-in-launcher rail (simulated with nested frames); no page errors.
- **Not tested:** a real iPhone / Android (touch, safe areas, keyboard), real Safari, the live launcher (whose `index.html` was not supplied; it is unchanged and Horizon has no launcher card to update, but the launcher actually writing `pal_theme` was assumed from Gigs & Trips reading it), the real On Budget file (only simulated nesting), live Supabase and a second device, Lex's account, and the look with the real Google Fonts loaded (blocked in the test; system-font fallback only).
- **Known limitations:** the Age Line labels can crowd when two milestones are within a year or two of each other; the eight dialogs, the Sync & Backup drawer, the On Budget import review, pension / checkpoint / tracker rows get the new colours, type and sheet but keep their old internal layouts; Google Fonts need a connection the first time; the one-pager "At retirement" block keeps its original sentence-style rows inside the new card.

### v1.9 — HTV-013 — "Cabinet" look and feel: phone and desktop layouts, drawer hero, section tabs — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 2 Nov):** a look-and-feel refresh in the same family as Gigs & Trips v7.109 (GIG-122) and the apps refreshed since, with its own personality, **without changing functionality**. Built from the approved "Cabinet" design canvas. Pete's four decisions were all the recommended option: **all per-tool buttons stay visible on phone cards**; **a desktop row click selects into a details pane**; **section chips plus a desktop-only search box** (display-only); **"Last backup" stays session-only and is labelled "this session"** (no new stored data).
- ⚠ **ID note:** the HTML Vault backlog was not supplied (the project holds no backlog doc) and the file's own header comment already mentions HTV-012, so **HTV-013 is the next number after the highest ID seen**, not one confirmed against a backlog. The header comment in the file also still said "v1.6" before this release; it now says v1.9.
- **Not changed (frozen):** every feature and workflow (upload with the Add tool step, edit name / section, archive as a soft delete with its confirm, reorder within a section, open full screen, open in new tab, refresh, JSON export and restore); the Supabase table `html_vault_items`, every `PalSync.sbFetch` call, the list query, the lazy fetch of `html_content` only on open, the row shape written on upload, the backup envelope (`version`, `lastUpdated`, `lastExported`, `data.items`) and restore (PATCH then POST); the launcher cache `pal_vault_stat` `{ count, updatedAt }`; theme handling (`pal_theme`, `PAL_THEME` message, `applyThemeCore`). No localStorage key added. No new dependency; still one standalone HTML file with `pal-shared.js?v=1.9` (file unchanged).
- **Look (shared family DNA):** warm paper light theme (#F4F0E6) and deep night dark theme (#0E0D12), following the launcher's light / dark setting as before; one lime signal (#CBF55C in dark, ink on paper in light) on the primary action and active states only; Bricolage Grotesque for titles, the big count and figures and DM Sans for the rest (Google Fonts; system fonts offline). CSS-variable tokens for colour, radius and type; the old variable names are kept. Vault's own colours: Work periwinkle, Personal clay, Untagged the launcher's existing Vault silver (#B9B5C6); amber only for "Heavy", green only for "Synced" and "New".
- **Responsive, not device-sniffing:** under 700 px phone, 700–1099 px tablet (phone layout in a centred ≤540 px column), 1100 px and over desktop. CSS media queries on **one DOM**, with `matchMedia` listeners that record `data-layout` on `<html>` and redraw only the list and pane when the desktop-only parts switch on or off. An open dialog and typed text survive a resize.
- **Phone / tablet:** the header (wordmark, version, sync chip) and a **floating bar** (Upload tool pill and a Sync & Backup button, replacing the Upload button at the top of the page); dialogs are **bottom sheets** with a grab handle; the toast sits above the bar; safe areas respected through `env()`. Each tool is a card (window glyph, name, filename, size / New / Heavy chips, Open, Edit, ↑ ↓, Archive — all visible).
- **Desktop:** a **left rail** (wordmark, Upload tool, Library with the count, Sync & Backup, the sync state), a page heading with a **search box**, a **hero strip** (drawer hero plus Total size, Last updated and Last backup tiles), section chips, a **table grouped by section** (size bar, added date, ↑ ↓) and a **details pane** on the right (Open, Edit, Archive, the metadata and the tool's position with ↑ ↓). A row click **selects**; Open is one click further than the old card button (⚠ deliberate, as in the other apps). Dialogs are centred.
- **Vault's own signature ("Cabinet"):** the **drawer hero** (tool count, total size, a Work / Personal / Untagged split bar, last added), **index-tab section headers**, a **window glyph** tile per tool (initials from the name, section colour), a **size weight bar** (relative to the largest tool) with a **Heavy** chip over the existing 2 MB warn limit and a **New** chip for tools added in the last 7 days, an empty state that explains the three sections, a storage split bar in Sync & Backup, and the chosen file shown in the Add tool dialog. All of it reads values the app already loads; initials, colours, chips and bars are derived at draw time and **nothing new is stored**.
- **Additive display behaviour (no data effect):** section chips (All / Work / Personal / Untagged) and, on desktop only, search over the loaded names and filenames. Filters hide rows only; ↑ ↓ still swap with the true neighbour in the full section, so order is never affected. Search is ignored below 1100 px, so a term typed on desktop cannot hide tools on a phone after a resize. Filter, search and selection are in memory only.
- **Restyled only (same markup and behaviour):** Sync & Backup, Edit tool and Add tool dialogs (emoji removed from the section menu labels; the stored values `work` / `personal` / empty are unchanged), the full-screen viewer bar (icon-only buttons on phone with accessible names, text labels from 700 px), the sync banner, toast.
- **Code touched outside CSS / the HTML shell:** `TAG_SECTIONS` gained a `name`; new layout and state block (`MQ_DESK`, `MQ_PHONE`, `applyLayout`, `viewFilter`, `searchTerm`, `selectedId`); `renderItemCard` and `renderList` replaced by `renderHero`, `renderControls`, `renderToolItem`, `renderList`, `renderPane`, `selectTool`, `handleToolAction` (the former delegated click handler, now shared by the list and the pane, same `data-action` names and the same `openTool` / `openRenameModal` / `archiveItem` / `moveItem` calls); `setSyncState` also updates the rail card; `renderStaged` shows the chosen file in the Add dialog; `populateDataModal` draws the storage bar; `exportBackup` refreshes the hero tile. `loadList`, `backfillSortOrder`, `moveItem`, `submitUpload`, `openTool`, `submitRename`, `archiveItem`, `exportBackup`'s export itself and `handleImportFile` are unchanged.
- **Launcher:** `index.html` was not supplied and is **not changed**; nothing it reads has changed (`pal_vault_stat` shape and write point verified identical; the launcher's Vault card keeps its own look). Test & Issues embeds this file as an iframe and is unchanged.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, both header badges (rail and header), the header comment, `pal-shared.js?v=1.9`. The app has no `version` field of its own.
- **Tested (Stage 1; headless Chromium, Playwright, a stubbed `pal-shared.js` with an in-memory table that mimics the list / PATCH / POST calls, 8 fixture tools):** 72 checks, all passing. At phone (390), tablet (820) and desktop (1360): layout tag, floating bar versus rail, details pane only on desktop, no sideways scroll, tablet column ≤540 px and centred, tap targets ≥ 40 px (viewer buttons ≥ 44), tablet and phone card tap does not select; hero count and total, section chips and counts, New and Heavy chips on the right tools only, reorder buttons disabled at the ends of each section; filters; desktop search by name and filename, no-match message, selection moving to a visible tool; **live resize 1360 → 390 → 820 → 1360** (bar / rail swap, pane hide / restore, search ignored on phone and applied again on desktop), **resize with an Edit dialog open and text typed** (sheet ↔ centred, text and open state kept); Edit (PATCH name, tag and `updated_at`, tool moves section), archive with confirm and with cancel (PATCH `deleted:true` only after confirm), reorder through the pane (two `sort_order` PATCHes within the section, selection kept), upload through the real Add tool step (POST row has every previous field, `sort_order` appended within the target section, tag stored), open and close in the viewer (html fetched only on open, frame cleared on close), JSON export (envelope, filename, `lastExported` shown), restore (known ids PATCHed, unknown id POSTed, list reloaded), Sync & Backup values, `pal_vault_stat` still `{ count, updatedAt }`; light theme background rgb(244, 240, 230) and dark rgb(14, 13, 18); empty vault, no-session banner with "Sync error", empty desktop; keyboard Enter on a desktop row selects; no console or page errors. Screenshots of phone, tablet and desktop in both themes, the Add and Sync & Backup sheets, the viewer and the empty state were reviewed; two defects found that way (Personal missing from the split bar; wrapped hero text on desktop) were fixed and the suite re-run.
- **Not tested:** a real iPhone or Android phone (touch, safe areas, the on-screen keyboard, the floating bar over the home indicator), real Safari, the real `pal-shared.js` and live Supabase (the stub reproduces the calls the app makes, not the server), a second device, large real data volumes, the app running inside Test & Issues' iframe and the launcher's own nesting, a real file larger than 2 MB through the upload path (the Heavy chip and the existing confirm are logic-checked, the native confirm was not exercised), the native `<select>` option list and file pickers, and the look of the Google Fonts (blocked in the test run, system fonts were reviewed).
- **Known limitations / not restyled:** the browser's own `confirm()` prompts (archive, large file, restore) keep their native look; the saved tools shown in the viewer bring their own style; the Test & Issues chrome and the launcher's Vault card are separate files; the native `<select>` menu is only partly styled. When the app is embedded inside Test & Issues it keeps its own full header (no slim strip, unlike Claims inside Fortnight). On a phone a toast can briefly cover part of an open sheet. The "Last backup" figure is still **session-only** (it reads "Never" after a reload); persisting it would need a new stored date and was not requested. Google Fonts need a connection the first time (system fonts until then). `viewport-fit=cover` was left off on purpose, as in the launcher refresh, so the safe-area padding only takes effect if a host adds it.
- **Flagged, not changed (needs your decision):** the viewport tag still has `maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no`, which blocks pinch-zoom — recommend removing it (an accessibility problem; iOS Safari already ignores it), as already flagged for Gym Tracker and On Budget.

### v1.8 — HTV-010 — Stat cache for the launcher

- For launcher PET-094: new `cacheStatForLauncher()` called from `loadList()` (the only place `items` is fetched, itself called after upload, delete, reorder and tag change) writes `{ count, updatedAt }` to localStorage key `pal_vault_stat`. Items themselves are still never stored locally. Silently skipped if localStorage is unavailable.
- Consumed by launcher `statVaultSub()` (v10.89).
- Verified manually (reload, upload, delete).

### v3.118 — Suite WP1.4 / WP1.2 — A refused save is reported instead of failing silently; export date dd/mm/yy — 4 Nov 2026

- **Why (baseline B3 / B9):** `save()` called `localStorage.setItem` with no protection, so a refused write (storage full or blocked) threw out of the click handler with no message, and the launcher notification and contract publish after it were skipped.
- **Change:** `save()` now builds the payload, then writes through `PalShared.safeSet` (fallback: a silent try/catch if the library is missing), so a refusal shows a red bar once (at most every 30 s) and the rest of `save()` still runs. The printed budget header's "Exported" date is dd/mm/yy. Month-name dates without a year ("Tue 4 Nov") are unchanged (D10).
- **Needs:** `pal-shared.js` 1.1.0 (tag `?v=3.118`).
- **Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, Europe/London, real data seeded from the 4 Nov backup files):** A refused write no longer throws; the bar appears once; the launcher message `OB_DATA_UPDATED` is still sent; a normal save still changes the stored data. Load of all 11 pages with no errors. **Not tested:** a real browser quota failure (simulated by making `localStorage.setItem` throw), Safari, the iPhone, cloud sync with the new build, nested copies inside other apps.
- **Files:** `on-budget.html`, `pal-shared.js`. No data format, storage key, sync or backup change.

- **Request (Pete, 3 Nov):** on desktop make Bills match the Spending view — the transactions that are ready for clearing in the right-hand column, with the cleared transactions in the main section under the graph.
- ⚠ **ID note:** the On Budget backlog was not supplied, so ON--111 is the next number after ON--110 in this changelog. Built on the supplied v3.116 (which includes ON--109 / ON--110).
- **Change (`on-budget.html` only, display only):** `renderBillsLedger()` now renders the list as **two blocks on one DOM** — `.bl-cleared` (cleared / skipped entries, same rows and same 30-item cap as before) and `.bl-uncleared` (the uncleared / forecast rows, unchanged markup with the ✓ and ✕ buttons) — and the `.bl-grid` carries `data-filter`. **Desktop (≥ 1100 px):** both blocks are visible; the page is a two-column grid (`.bl-main` and `#bills-tx-body` become `display: contents`): tiles, runway chart, **Cleared** list and the Recurring next-due list in the main column; a sticky **Ready to clear (n)** pane on the right (372 px, same as Spending's transactions pane), grouped **Due now / Coming up** with the same running balances, scrolling inside itself. The Uncleared | Cleared | All pills and the collapse button are hidden on desktop (the two lists replace them); the 90 days / Next income pills stay. **Phone and tablet are unchanged in behaviour:** the Uncleared | Cleared | All filter picks which block shows ("All" shows cleared then uncleared; it was one merged card, now two cards in the same order), the group headings and block headings are hidden, empty-state wording is as before ("No transactions yet" for All with nothing). `_billsFilter` is session-only and untouched, so resizing between layouts is safe.
- **Removed / changed from v3.113:** the desktop "column table" and its header row (item, amount, balance after, tick, delete) are gone — rows now use the same layout as phone in both lists. Rows in the pane use slightly smaller ✓ (40 px) and ✕ (32 px) targets to fit 372 px.
- **Also fixed while in the area:** at 1100–1299 px the three Bills tiles (Cleared balance, Lowest projected, Next pay-off) clipped their figures; below 1300 px the Cleared balance tile now spans the row and the other two sit beneath it.
- **Not changed:** the runway chart, all Bills maths and balances, clearing / deleting behaviour (same functions), data, storage, sync, backup, launcher messages and the v3.115 / v3.116 launcher contract. `index.html` not supplied and not changed.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, header badge, header comment, `pal-shared.js?v=3.117` (file unchanged), the `OB_PONG` version and both `version` fields.

Screenshots reviewed (desktop light / dark / 1100, phone light / dark, All filter).
- **Not tested:** a real phone or Safari, live Supabase and a second device, the launcher with the real `PalContract`, Horizon, and a very large cleared history on desktop.
- **Known limitations:** the Ready to clear pane lists the whole uncleared forecast (everything in the 90-day / next-income window, as the old Uncleared filter did), not only items due today — "Due now" and "Coming up" headings separate them; limiting the pane to due items only would be a small follow-up. The Cleared list shows the most recent 30 (unchanged cap). If "All" was the chosen filter before widening the window, the desktop Cleared list is oldest-first (the All ordering) until the filter is changed back on a phone.

### v3.114 — ON--108 — Bills runway chart: interactive, with readout and labels — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 2 Nov):** make the Bills graph dynamic so you can hover or click points and see what the balance will be there, and add contextual values and labels.
- ⚠ **ID note:** the On Budget backlog was not supplied, so ON--108 is the next number after ON--107 in this changelog.
- **Change (`on-budget.html` only, display only):** the runway chart on Bills › Ledger (added in v3.113) is now interactive. **One point per day that has a movement**, plus today. **Hover** (mouse) previews a point, **click / tap / drag** (touch) pins it, **← → Home End** step through the points when the chart is focused, and **‹ ›** buttons (44 px) do the same for touch. A **readout** above the chart shows the date and how far off it is, the **balance after that day**, how far it is above £0 (or "overdrawn", in red), the **change since today**, tags (**Lowest point**, **Income**) and **every item that day** with its signed amount (Tied and Overdue badges kept). With nothing pinned it shows the **lowest point**, so the page opens on the answer to "will I stay in credit". The pinned point survives a re-render (kept by date, per session only).
- **Labels and context on the chart:** y-axis values (£0 and the top), date ticks along the bottom, a labelled **Lowest £x** marker (lime), **Now £x** at the start, **+£ income** labels, the two **largest outgoings**, **Next income · date** (in Next-income view), a dashed red **£0 line** with an "Overdrawn" label and a red-tinted zone when the balance goes below £0, and a legend. Labels avoid overlapping each other. Works in the 90-day and Next-income views.
- **How it works:** `obRunway()` now builds a model from `billsForecastData()` (the same items and running balances the ledger shows) and emits a shell; `rwInit()` draws the SVG at the **real container width** (so text stays readable and it redraws on resize / rail changes via `ResizeObserver`); document-level delegated pointer, click and key handlers (the chart is re-created on every Bills render). Overdue items are grouped into today's point. No new stored data, no calculation changed.
- **Data / sync / launcher:** none — nothing written, no schema, no message change. `index.html` not supplied and not changed.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, header badge, header comment, `pal-shared.js?v=3.114` (file unchanged), the `OB_PONG` version and both `version` fields.
- **Tested (Stage 1; headless Chromium, Playwright, fixed clock 10 Nov 2026, stubbed `pal-shared.js`, fixture with Bills items dated in November):** at phone (390) and desktop (1360): chart drawn at 1:1 with its card; default readout = the lowest balance; **hovering every point shows that day's balance** (checked against `billsForecastData()` running balances); the guide follows the pointer and snaps to the nearest point; click pins and moving away keeps the pin; → Home End and ‹ keys step correctly; ‹ › are ≥ 44 px; the readout lists the day's items; the pin survives a re-render; the 90-day view draws more points; **resize 1360 ↔ 390 redraws at the new width**; an overdrawn case (readout red, "overdrawn", zero line and label); **touch tap** on a point (touch-enabled context). **Differential run, v3.113 vs v3.114, same scripted workflow** at 390, 1360 (and Decreasing mode): saved data, sync pushes, toasts and key values identical; launcher protocol (`ping`, tab and sheet actions, `quickAddFood` / `quickAddBills`) identical; v3.113 backup imports and v3.114 exports identical data; layout suite re-run and passing; no page errors. Screenshots reviewed in light and dark.
- **Not tested:** a real phone (drag-scrubbing versus page scroll — the chart uses `touch-action: pan-y`, so a vertical swipe scrolls the page and a sideways one scrubs), real Safari, screen-reader behaviour of the chart (it has a group label and arrow-key support but was not tried with VoiceOver / TalkBack), live Supabase and a second device, the launcher.
- **Known limitations:** points snap to days that have a movement (it does not interpolate between days, because the balance does not change between them); a day with several items shows the balance at the **end** of that day. With very many items in the 90-day view the labels show only the lowest point, now, incomes and the two largest outgoings; every other point is still reachable by hover, tap or the arrows.

### v3.113 — ON--107 — "Tally" look and feel: phone and desktop layouts, new summary elements — 1 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 1 Nov):** a look-and-feel refresh in the same family as Gigs & Trips v7.109 (GIG-122), with the app's own personality, **without changing functionality**. Built from the approved "Tally" design canvas; Pete's four decisions were all the recommended option (Tally hero; desktop row tap keeps the edit dialog; floating Add pill; five tabs kept on phone).
- ⚠ **ID note:** the On Budget backlog was not supplied, so **ON--107 is the next number after ON--106 in this changelog**, not one confirmed against the backlog.
- **Not changed (frozen):** every feature and workflow, all budget / pot / headroom / projection maths (including income and transfer handling in both Decreasing and Increasing modes), the localStorage keys (`on_budget_v1`, `ob_theme_pref`, `ob_hero_focus`), the Supabase table and record keys, JSON export / import / backup, the launcher messages (`OB_ACTION`, `OB_PONG`, `OB_QUICKADD_RESULT`, `OB_DATA_UPDATED`) and the shape of `dashboardSummary`. No new dependency; still one standalone HTML file. **No new stored data** — every new element reads values the app already computes.
- **Look (shared family DNA):** warm "paper" light theme (#F4F0E6) and deep "night" theme (#0E0D12), following the launcher's light / dark setting; one lime signal (#CBF55C) used for the Add button and active states only; Bricolage Grotesque for money figures and titles (tabular numerals) and DM Sans for the rest (Google Fonts, system fonts offline). CSS-variable tokens throughout; **the old token names (`--accent`, `--surface`, `--weekly` …) are kept** because the JavaScript-rendered markup uses them inline — `--accent` now means "good" (a readable green in both themes) and the new `--lime` / `--sel-bg` carry the signal and the selected state. Food, Travel and Other keep their green / blue / violet families; **Bills gets copper** to tell the two accounts apart.
- **On Budget's own signature ("Tally"):** the Spending hero draws the pay cycle as a **tally strip** (one tick per day, today in lime) above a **pot bar** that splits the pot into spent (Food / Travel / Other), reserved (Food and Travel still to come, hatched) and headroom. Pot = spent + reserved + headroom, so it is the existing figures drawn as one bar; if headroom is negative the bar is outlined red and the legend says "Short by".
- **Responsive, not device-sniffing:** under 700 px phone, 700–1099 px tablet (phone layout in a centred ≤540 px column), 1100 px and over desktop. CSS media queries on **one DOM**; `data-layout` on `<html>` records which, and a `matchMedia` listener (plus `orientationchange`) keeps it current and redraws the History chart (drawn 640 wide on desktop, 320 elsewhere). Nothing else re-renders on resize, so an open dialog and typed text survive it.
- **Phone / tablet:** header (logo, version, sync chip) and a **floating bottom bar** (the same five tab buttons and `switchTab()`, now with line icons); the Add transaction button is a **floating lime pill** above the bar; dialogs are **bottom sheets** with a grab handle; the toast sits above the bar; safe areas respected (`viewport-fit=cover` added; the rest of the viewport tag is unchanged).
- **Desktop:** the same tab buttons become a **left rail** with an "Add transaction" button on top and the pay-in date at the bottom; dialogs are centred. **Spending** is a wide hero (pot bar), headroom with "How calculated?" permanently open beside the Food-week card, Travel / Other / next pay-off tiles, and the transactions in a right-hand pane (a row tap still opens the same edit dialog). **Bills** is three tiles (cleared balance, lowest projected, next pay-off), the runway chart, a column table (item, amount, balance after, tick, delete) and a "Recurring — next due" side list. **History** is a six-column grid (cycle chart wide, comparison, top shops, left-over, month cards). The rail "Add transaction" button opens the Bills transaction sheet on the Bills ledger and the Spending sheet everywhere else (new `railAdd()`).
- **New elements (all display-only):** (1) cycle tally strip; (2) pot bar and legend; (3) week columns (each week's spend against its own budget, current week outlined, orange for moved-in spend) replacing the five thin bars; (4) date stubs and category / state chips on every Spending and Bills row; (5) Bills runway chart (running balance to the end of the forecast window, lowest point marked, incomes ticked) built from the existing forecast items; (6) History: delta chips on the cycle comparison, a dashed pot-limit line on the cycle chart (`settings.monthlyPot`), the left-over chart as bars (lime / red), shop bars; (7) empty and set-up states use the new tokens; (8) Bills "Next pay-off" tile and the desktop "Recurring — next due" list read `nextTiedOccurrence()` / `nextDueRaw()`.
- **Restyled only (same markup and behaviour):** Recurring, Scenario, Settings, every sheet (add / edit, Bills transaction, recurring, adjust budgets, clear, merge shops, scenario item), Sync & Backup drawer, controls (pills, segmented toggles, switches, inputs, buttons ≥ 44 px, filter pills 40 px) and the toast. The category buttons in the Add sheet use a colour square instead of an emoji; stat-card labels use a colour dot.
- **Code touched outside CSS / the HTML shell (all display-only):** new helper block before `renderDash()` (`OBI`, layout listener, `railAdd`, `obStub`, `obChip`, `obTally`, `obPotBar`, `obRunway`, `obBillsSide`); `renderDash()` (wrapper `div`s, hero / headroom / Food markup regrouped, week columns, strip icons, row stub + chip), `renderBillsLedger()` (tiles, runway, wrapper, side list), `billsRowHtml()` (stub, amount wrapper), `histTrendSvg()`, `histRemainderSvg()`, `renderHist()` (grid wrapper, classes, chips, shop bars), `applyTheme()` (meta colours only). No element ID was removed and no handler changed.
- **Launcher:** `index.html` was not supplied and is **not changed**. It reads `dashboardSummary` (shape unchanged, values verified identical), the `OB_PONG` version (now 3.113) and the `OB_ACTION` messages (verified, below). The launcher's On Budget card keeps its own look.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, header badge, header comment, `pal-shared.js?v=3.113` (the file itself is unchanged), the `OB_PONG` version and both `version` fields (autosave envelope and JSON export).
- **Tested (Stage 1; headless Chromium, Playwright, fixed clock 10 Nov 2026, seeded random, stubbed `pal-shared.js` with a recording mock cloud and an active session; fixture = 8 completed cycles, a live cycle with uncleared and income rows, 8 recurring Bills items):**
  - **Differential run, original v3.112 vs v3.113, same scripted workflow** (add Travel, Food and Income spend; tick a transaction cleared; edit; delete; Balance / Left toggle; "How calculated?"; adjust-budgets sheet; Bills add, tick cleared, filters, Recurring, Scenario, forecast mode; Settings food budget and week start; History): saved localStorage envelope (incl. `dashboardSummary`), all 15 records pushed to sync, every toast and key screen value **identical**, at phone (390), tablet (820) and desktop (1360, using the rail Add button), in Increasing and Decreasing modes.
