### v3.112 — ON--106 — Per-month pay-day exceptions; Balance / Left toggle on the Spending card

- **Why:** the Food/Travel budgets reset each pay cycle on the Pay-in day (28th, moved back to the nearest working day on a weekend). December pay always arrives early (Christmas), and there was no way to change one month without changing the rule for all. Pete also wants the main Spending card to lead with either the card balance or the budget left.
- **Change 1 — pay-day exceptions (`on-budget.html` only):** new optional `settings.payinOverrides` = `{ 'YYYY-MM': 'YYYY-MM-DD' }`, keyed by the month the cycle **starts** in (so `'2026-12': '2026-12-22'` = the December cycle starts 22 Dec and November ends 21 Dec). `payinDate()` is the one place that reads it (only when called with the base `payinDay`, normalising a month index of 12), so `getBoundaries()`, `cycleKeyForDate()`, `getWeeks()` / `projectNextMonthHeadroom()`, `cycleRange()` / `cycleLabel()` (History), `computeDashboardSummary()` (launcher card) and the next-month preview all follow it with no other logic changed. An exception date is used exactly as entered (no weekend shift). The pay-in strip shows "(adjusted)" for an exception ("(moved)" is still the weekend shift). Settings → new "Pay-day exceptions" list (date picker + Add, Remove per row); saved straight away (own `save(true)` + `syncUpsertSettings()`), no need to press Save settings. Only a cycle later than the current one can be added; a date equal to the normal date is refused. `saveSettings()` now carries `payinOverrides` explicitly (it rebuilds the settings object).
- **Effect to know about:** budgets are pro-rated by day, so a shortened cycle (Nov: 27 Nov–21 Dec) gets fewer Food weeks and the lengthened one (Dec: 22 Dec–27 Jan) more; Travel stays one monthly figure. Test scenario: Food £428.57 for the short cycle vs £535.71 normally.
- **Change 2 — Spending card toggle:** Increasing (credit-card) mode only. A small Balance | Left pill beside the hero label switches the headline between "Card balance" (as before; sub-line "£x left of £y budget") and "Budget left" (headline = budget left or "-£x" when over; sub-line "card balance £x of £y budget"). Choice is remembered per device in localStorage `ob_hero_focus` (not synced, so phone and desktop can differ). Falls back to Balance when no spending limit is set. Decreasing mode is unchanged (its headline already is the amount left, so no toggle). Headroom, projections, bar, launcher card and all budget maths unchanged.
- **Data / sync:** `payinOverrides` is an additive field inside the existing synced `__settings__` record and in JSON backups; absent/empty = old behaviour, so existing data and older backups load unchanged (`DEFAULT_SETTINGS.payinOverrides = {}`). No migration, no schema change. Launcher (`index.html`) not edited (not supplied); its card reads `dashboardSummary`, whose shape is unchanged.
- **Not changed:** Bills recurring dates (the Monthly CC Pay Off and wage incomes stay on their own 28th dates in Bills), Food/Travel budget values, past cycles.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, badge, header comment, `pal-shared.js?v=`, the OB_PONG version and both `version` fields.
- Tested (Stage 1): `node --check`; headless Chromium (Playwright, stubbed `pal-shared.js`, clock fixed). With no exceptions the cycle dates, week budgets and hero figure are identical to v3.111. With Dec = 22 Dec: Nov cycle 27 Nov–21 Dec, Dec cycle 22 Dec–27 Jan, `cycleKeyForDate` correct either side, getBoundaries correct on 30 Nov, 10/21/22 Dec, 5 Jan, 28 Jan, History label correct; UI add/remove, rejection of current-cycle / default-date / empty, `saveSettings()` keeps the field, survives reload, present in the saved envelope (version 3.112). Toggle: both views correct (£300.00 balance / £650.00 left of £750.00), persists across reload, absent in Decreasing mode; mobile-width screenshots checked; no page errors. **Not tested:** real data, Supabase sync / second device (settings merge is whole-object last-write-wins on `updated_at`, as before), real phone, launcher card.

### v3.102 — ON--096 — Spend transfers (Bills → Spending) and the tied Monthly CC Pay Off

- **Why:** Spending is now a credit card paid off from Bills on the 28th. Request: transfer funds Bills → Spending (one direction only); flag a Bills transaction (and, if recurring, all future ones) as a spend transfer; show it in both places with each side cleared separately; tie a recurring Bills item to Spending as the "Monthly CC Pay Off", sized by the monthly budget in Settings and raised to the projected figure when spend goes above it.
- **Change (`on-budget.html` only, additive):**
  - New Spending transaction type `'transfer'`, never spend or income. `isSpendTx()` replaces `type!=='income'` in the pot, headroom, % used, `computeDashboardSummary`, `ftClearedPot`, `monthAgg` (History) and Spending-screen filters, so pot / headroom / reserve / projections / History / launcher figures ignore it. `cardBalanceInfo()` subtracts transfers (they pay the card off), so the card balance and cleared card balance move; decreasing-mode pot is unaffected.
  - Bills: new optional `xfer` flag on Bills transactions (Add/Edit transaction switch "⇄ Transfer to Spending", outgoing only) and on recurring items ("⇄ Transfer to Spending"; every future occurrence cleared copies the flag; already-cleared ones unchanged). New optional `tiedToSpend` on a recurring item ("🔗 Tied to Spending"): its amount is locked to `settings.monthlyPot` (`syncTiedAmounts()` on save of Settings, boot and every pull). Badges "⇄ Spending" / "🔗 Tied" in the ledger and the Recurring tab.
  - `reconcileXferLegs()` (idempotent; runs on Bills render, boot and after every pull) keeps one Spending leg per recorded flagged Bills transaction: deterministic id `xf_<billsTxId>`, starts UNCLEARED, never has its cleared state touched afterwards. Created only once the Bills transaction is dated today or earlier (so no future/phantom months); amount, date and name follow later edits; moved (old row tombstoned) if the date falls in another pay cycle; tombstoned when the Bills transaction is deleted, skipped or un-flagged; revived if re-flagged. Each side clears independently (Bills ✓ / Spending ✓). A leg cannot be edited or deleted from Spending (a toast points to Bills).
  - Spending (Increasing mode): a "Next pay-off £x · date" strip for the next future tied occurrence. When the projected card balance at pay-in is above it, the strip shows "Update next bill": it writes a per-occurrence override of the projected figure (e.g. £820, not £750 + £70); the standing amount is untouched.
  - Month setup in Increasing mode now prefills the spending limit with the Settings monthly pot.
- **Unchanged:** the existing Bills "⇄ Transfer" (Savings / Food & Travel, ON--051), budget maths, JSON export/import shape, sync tables (new fields ride on existing records), `pal-shared.js`, the launcher.
- **Data / sync:** no schema change; older records need no migration. ⚠ Update every device together: an older version would show the transfer legs as ordinary spend.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, badge, header comment, `pal-shared.js?v=`, the OB_PONG version and both `version` fields.

### v3.100 — ON--094 — Launcher quick-add reliable on first open / slow load

- **Why:** launcher card Spend / Bills quick-add could post before On Budget was listening, give up while it was still booting, duplicate on a retry, or have the entry dropped locally by the app's first cloud pull. See launcher v11.18 (PET-122) for the full investigation.
- **Change (`on-budget.html` only, additive):**
  - `OB_ACTION` `ping` → `OB_PONG {reqId, ready, version}`. `ready` = boot sequence finished AND the first `syncPull()` has settled (success or error, `_obFirstPullSettled`), or `onNoSession` fired, or 12 s since boot.
  - The result of every quick-add `reqId` is stored (`_obQuickResults`) and replayed for a repeated `reqId` (same `ok`, `msg` and `category`), replacing the old "mark seen before saving, answer 'Already added'" guard. Still one `saveSpend()` / `saveBtx()` per `reqId`.
  - Each quick-added spend / bill is tracked for 5 minutes; `obQuickReapply()` runs inside `syncPull()` after the rebuilds and before `checkClearedBalanceDrift()`. If the entry is no longer in `months[mk].transactions` / `bills.tx` (and is not in the deleted logs) it is put back and re-upserted (`syncUpsertTx` / `syncUpsertBillsTx`) once; if the pull kept it, nothing happens. The bill's cleared-balance change is not touched (it was applied by `saveBtx()` and the settings merge keeps the newer local value).
- **Not changed:** `saveSpend()`, `saveBtx()`, categories, budget maths, data structures, JSON export/import shape, sync schema, `pal-shared.js`. Version set in title, logo badge, header comment, `pal-shared.js` cache-bust query and both backup-version fields.
- **Data / sync:** no schema change; older launchers still work (they simply do not ping).
- Tested (Stage 1): `node --check` of both files; jsdom run of the REAL `index.html` and `on-budget.html` (served over HTTP with an artificial load delay) with a stub `pal-shared.js` (the real one was not supplied) and an in-memory cloud: (A) cold load with a 2.5 s app delay saves exactly once after the app is ready; (B) `switchTo()` mid-load plus a slow first pull — nothing saved and the typed amount kept until ready, then exactly one local entry and one cloud row; (C) first two replies lost on the Bills row — one entry, popup shown, balance moved once; (D) new launcher with the OLD v3.99 app — not-ready message, nothing saved, entry kept; (E) repeated `reqId` ×3 — one entry, identical replayed result and category, a new `reqId` still saves; (F) spend and bill added during `syncPull()` — each present exactly once afterwards, restored once, one cloud row each, next pull restores nothing; (F0) baseline v3.99 drops the same mid-pull spend (bug reproduced); (G) baseline v11.17 + v3.99 mid-load add loses the message (bug reproduced); (H) old v11.17 launcher + v3.100 app still saves; (I) warm add ~40 ms, second deliberate add makes a second entry. The jsdom harness emulates the browser's `postMessage` origin/source.
- ⚠ Not tested: a real cold load on a phone or slow network, live Supabase / the real `pal-shared.js` pull implementation (the bills-pull race window was simulated by adding during the pull call), a second device, the Gym card in a browser.

### v3.91 — ON--085 — Deleted Food & Travel transactions no longer reappear on other devices

- **Symptom:** a transaction deleted from the cleared list on one device was still there on another.
- **Root cause:** the app writes transactions as `tx_<monthKey>_<id>` (`syncUpsertTx` / `syncTombstoneTx`), but `PalSync.table().pull()` keys on the record's own `id` field and, when it pushes a local-only record or retries an unconfirmed tombstone, writes `tx_<id>` (no month). That left two cloud rows per transaction: the real month-keyed row (tombstoned on delete) and a stale live bare row. `pull()` processes rows in `record_key` order, so the month-keyed tombstone was applied and then the stale live row re-adopted the transaction. The deleting device was protected by its local `deletedTxLog`; other devices have no such log. Confirmed on live data: 11 transactions had duplicate rows, 3 of them tombstoned-with-stale-live (`mrrolkket3ya`, `muua0uvn419b4y`, `muwylf17dc1lcw`). The three were tombstoned by hand in Supabase first; this release stops it recurring. Two transactions also had three live rows (old ON--046 refile left the previous month row live); the heal handles those.
- **Fix (all in `on-budget.html`; `pal-shared.js` unchanged, no other app affected):**
  1. Transactions merge on a composite sync id `_sk = <monthKey>_<id>` (`txSyncKey`), so `pull()` writes the same `tx_<monthKey>_<id>` key the app always has. `_sk` is stripped from local records after the merge; it can appear in cloud `data` only on rows `pull()` itself pushes (harmless).
  2. `txPlanSync()` collapses cloud rows to one per transaction id before the merge. The newest `data.updated_at` decides; on a tie a month-keyed row beats a bare row, then a tombstone beats a live row. Other live rows are tombstoned (keeping their own `updated_at` so they can never outrank the winner); a live winner on a non-canonical key is re-created under the canonical key and the old key retired. `txApplyHeal()` applies the writes (best-effort, retried next pull); `txDedupeById()` guards against the same id appearing twice locally.
  3. Pull when the app returns to the foreground (`visibilitychange`), throttled to once per 60 s and skipped while a sync is running or an edit sheet is open. Previously the app only pulled when a session arrived, so a long-open copy never saw another device's delete.
- **Data / sync:** no data-model change, no schema change; local storage, JSON export/import and `deletedTxLog` untouched. Existing duplicate rows are repaired on the first pull after deploying. Each device should be reloaded once after deploy.
- **Known limitation (not changed):** a transaction added on this device while a pull is awaiting the network can be dropped from local state when the pull rebuilds the month arrays; it is already on the cloud and returns on the next pull. Non-401 push failures still rely on the re-confirmation sweep.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, badge, header comment, `pal-shared.js?v=` and the `version` fields in save and JSON export. Launcher: no change needed.
- Tested (real `pal-shared.js` v1.13 `PalSync.table().pull()` and the real `on-budget.html` helper code, against an in-memory mock of the Supabase REST API): live bug (tombstone + stale live bare row) not adopted by a fresh device and bare row retired; second pull is a no-op; refile triple keeps only the newest; lone stale bare row migrated to the canonical key without being deleted; local-only push and tombstone retry land on `tx_<month>_<id>`; newer cloud edit adopted; moved-month transaction deduped; cloud tombstone removes a local live copy; a dataset shaped like the live query output leaves only the two genuinely live ids. Headless jsdom load of the full app: no errors, title and badge v3.91, visibility handler a no-op without a session. Not tested: real browser, live Supabase, second device, phone.

### v3.87 — ON--081 — Bills Ledger: confirm before removing

- **Why:** the new ✓ (v3.86) sits beside the ✕, and the ✕ removed an entry instantly with no confirmation and no undo. A mis-tap on ✕ is much harder to recover from than one on ✓ (a recurring row records a skipped occurrence; a cleared row reverses the balance and is soft-deleted).
- **Change:** the ✕ on uncleared rows (`confirmRemoveUncleared()`), the ✕ on cleared rows and the Delete button in the edit sheet (`confirmDeleteBillsTx()`) now ask first, via the browser's native `confirm()` (same style as the app's existing `prompt()` use). The message names the entry and amount, says a recurring row is a skip and that the schedule isn't changed, and says a cleared delete reverses the cleared balance. Cancel changes nothing. The ✓ stays one tap (recoverable from the edit sheet). ✓ also gets a little more space from ✕.
- **Not changed:** the delete logic itself (`deleteBillsTx()`, `quickDeleteUncleared()`), Spending's ✕ (no prompt there — left alone as that screen is signed off; possible follow-up), the clear sheet's own "Skip" / "Cancel" buttons, data model, sync, backups, `pal-shared.js`.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, badge, header comment, `pal-shared.js?v=` and the `version` fields in save and JSON export.
- Tested (headless jsdom, real `on-budget.html` v3.87; `pal-shared.js` not available, `PalSync` / `esc` / `toast` / `uid` stubbed, `confirm` stubbed): cancel on each of the four delete paths changes nothing (no tx removed, no skip recorded, balance unchanged); accept performs the same result as v3.86 (ad-hoc removed, recurring skipped, cleared removed with balance reversed, skipped row removed with no balance change); message text; rendered rows call the confirm wrappers and no direct delete handlers remain; ✓ still one-tap with the right delta; version labels. Not tested: a real browser or phone — in particular that `confirm()` appears inside the launcher's iframe on iOS and desktop, and the ✓/✕ spacing.

### v3.86 — ON--080 — Bills Ledger: tick to clear, matching Spending

- **Why:** the v3.85 Spending pattern (one-tap ✓ on uncleared rows, switch in the edit sheet to change cleared state) was preferred; Bills now behaves the same way.
- **Tick to clear:** every uncleared row in the Bills ledger (recurring occurrences and ad-hoc / planned entries) gets a ✓ button, reusing the v3.85 `.tx-clear` style, next to the existing ✕. New `quickClearUncleared(kind, a, b)` clears the row at its **current** values — for a recurring occurrence that includes any per-occurrence override (name, amount, date). It mirrors `saveClear()`: recurring → a new cleared `bills.tx` entry (`source:'recurring'`, `recurringId`, `schedDate`, item note) and the override is consumed and tombstoned; ad-hoc → the existing entry gets `cleared:true`. In both cases the stored `clearedBalance` takes the same delta, `bills.settings.updated_at` is stamped, and tx / settings / override-tombstone syncs are issued. A second tap on an already-resolved row is a no-op (guarded), so a double-tap cannot double-apply the balance. The existing tap-the-row clear sheet (edit / clear / skip) is unchanged.
- **Cleared → uncleared:** done from the cleared row's edit sheet via the existing **Cleared now / Uncleared (planned)** switch (added v3.61, ON--060). No code change was needed; confirmed it works for entries generated from recurring occurrences as well as ad-hoc ones. Setting one to uncleared reverses its balance contribution and it reappears in the uncleared section as a "Planned" row (the recurring occurrence is not regenerated, so no duplicate). Skipped occurrences remain display-only and excluded from the balance.
- **Not changed:** data model, JSON backup shape, Supabase schema, Spending, `pal-shared.js`, launcher (`dashboardSummary.clearedBalance` has the same meaning) — `index.html` stays at v11.07.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, badge, header comment, `pal-shared.js?v=` and the display-only `version` field in the save and the JSON backup.
- Tested (headless jsdom, real `on-budget.html` v3.86; ⚠ the real `pal-shared.js` was **not available** in this session, so `PalSync` and a few helpers (`esc`, `toast`, `uid`) were stubbed — sync calls were verified as issued, not as accepted by Supabase): ✓ shown on recurring and ad-hoc uncleared rows and not on cleared rows; ad-hoc outgoing and income clear with correct balance deltas; recurring clear uses the override values and note, adds exactly one tx, consumes the override and issues tx upsert, override tombstone and settings upsert; double-tap is a no-op; cleared → uncleared via the edit sheet for a recurring-sourced entry reverses the balance, appears once as uncleared with no duplicate occurrence, and re-ticking restores it; same for an ad-hoc entry; skipped rows not editable; drift check unchanged; localStorage carries v3.86 and the right balance. Not tested: a real browser or phone (tick / ✕ spacing on narrow rows), live Supabase, a second device, the Spending tick after this change beyond confirming the function is unchanged (that code was not touched).

### v3.85 — ON--079 — Cleared and uncleared transactions in Food & Travel

- **Why:** Food & Travel had no concept of cleared transactions, so the Spending tab could not be matched against the card or bank, where recent spends have not yet posted. Bills already had cleared / uncleared; Food & Travel now has its own version, deliberately as a **display split only**.
- **Rule:** cleared status changes only what is shown as the total and the cleared balance, and how the list is grouped. Every budget, "left" figure, week bar, Travel figure, Other breakdown, reserve, headroom, pot and History figure still works on cleared **plus** uncleared, exactly as before.
- **Data model (additive, no migration):** each Food & Travel transaction can carry `cleared`; `cleared !== false` means cleared (the same convention Bills uses), so every existing transaction and backup is cleared. New setting `settings.clearMode`: `'auto'` (default — what everyone already had; new transactions are cleared) or `'manual'` (new transactions start uncleared). `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` carries `clearMode:'auto'`, so older backups and cloud settings without it load as Auto.
- **Settings:** new **Transaction clearing** toggle (Auto / Manual) under Pot tracking direction, staged until Save settings like the other toggles. `saveSettings()` rebuilds the settings object, so `clearMode` is carried through explicitly (as `potDirection` was). Switching back to Auto leaves existing uncleared transactions as they are.
- **Hero card:** the big figure stays the **total** (cleared + uncleared). A `Cleared £X · +£Y uncleared` line sits under it and the label gains "(total)". It shows in Manual mode or whenever anything is uncleared; with Auto and nothing uncleared the card is unchanged. Increasing mode (card balance): cleared = `cardBalanceInfo(..., clearedOnly)`. Decreasing mode (pot): cleared = start balance + cleared income − cleared spend (`ftClearedPot()`). The uncleared amount is total − cleared, signed.
- ⚠ **Decision to confirm:** the brief named the *Card* balance; the cleared line is also shown in Decreasing (debit pot) mode so the two modes behave the same. It is a single line and easy to restrict to Increasing mode if not wanted.
- **Set balance (Increasing):** now typed against the **cleared** balance (the figure the card statement shows); the prompt says so when Manual or anything is uncleared. The stored `cardAdjust` is the same single offset as before, so the total follows automatically. With nothing uncleared the behaviour and stored value are identical to v3.84.
- **Transaction list:** uncleared transactions are grouped above cleared ones under `Uncleared` and `Cleared` headings with counts. The headings only appear when something is uncleared, so the list is unchanged otherwise. Uncleared rows get a one-tap ✓ button (`clearFtTx()`) that marks the transaction cleared, refreshes `updated_at` and upserts it. Delete is unchanged.
- **Add / edit sheet:** a Cleared switch is shown in Manual mode, and when editing a transaction that is currently uncleared (so it can always be cleared). New transactions default to the mode (Auto cleared, Manual uncleared); the switch overrides either way. The toast says "(uncleared)" when relevant.
- **Launcher quick-add** (`quickAddFood`) follows the setting: it sets the sheet's cleared state from the mode before calling `saveSpend()`, so a stale value left by an earlier sheet cannot leak in.
- **Launcher summary:** `computeDashboardSummary()` exports `ftClearMode`, `ftUnclearedCount`, `potCleared` (Decreasing) and `cardBalanceCleared` (Increasing) for launcher v11.07 (PET-111). Every existing field, including the Bills `clearedBalance`, is unchanged — the new fields are named to avoid that clash.
- **Sync:** no schema change. `cleared` rides on the existing whole-record transaction upsert; `clearMode` on the settings record, which already merges as `{...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, ...remote}`. ⚠ **Multi-device caveat:** a device still on v3.84 shows uncleared transactions as ordinary rows, and if it saves Settings it writes a settings record without `clearMode`, which can switch other devices back to Auto. Update every device to v3.85 before relying on Manual.
- **Not changed:** History, month aggregates, Other breakdown, budgets and reserve maths, Bills, the JSON export / import shape (they simply carry the new fields), `pal-shared.js`.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, badge, header comment, `pal-shared.js?v=` and the display-only `version` field in the save and the JSON backup.
- Tested (headless jsdom, real `on-budget.html` and `index.html`; `pal-shared.js` was a copy already present in the working directory, not supplied with this request, version not established): Spending-tab HTML for legacy data is byte-identical to v3.84 in both Decreasing and Increasing modes; every pre-existing summary field is unchanged; with two uncleared transactions every summary figure and every on-screen budget / left / week / reserve / Other figure is identical to the same data all-cleared; hero total and cleared figures and signs in both modes; Set balance against cleared (typed 100.00 → cleared 100.00, total 80.00) and identical stored value to v3.84 when nothing is uncleared; add sheet in Auto and Manual including the override; list grouping, headings, counts and tick buttons; tick-to-clear (one sync upsert, `cleared:true`); edit sheet visibility rules; delete of an uncleared transaction; settings staging and save; localStorage, reload and JSON backup carrying `clearMode` and `cleared`; importing a v3.84 backup defaults to Auto; History renders; launcher quick-add in both modes; launcher card cases (see v11.07). Not tested: a real browser or phone (layout of the hero line and the tick button), live Supabase sync of `cleared` / `clearMode`, a second device, a v3.84 device alongside a v3.85 device, the real `prompt()` UX of Set balance.

### v3.83 — ON--077 — Launcher quick-add (`quickAddFood` / `quickAddBills`)

- Two new `OB_ACTION` actions for launcher v11.02 (PET-106). The message carries `{ amount, label, reqId }`. The handler switches to the Dashboard (Food) or Bills Ledger (Bills) tab, sets the same sheet state `saveSpend()` / `saveBtx()` read (`_cat='weekly'`, `_ftType='outgoing'`, `_dateShown=false`, `_editCtx=null`; `_btxEditId=null`, `_btxType='outgoing'`, `_btxDateShown=false`, `_btxCleared=true`), fills the amount (`setPennyValue`) and label, and calls the real save function. Entry shape, Bills balance update, label history (`touchFtLabel`), Supabase upsert, `OB_DATA_UPDATED` and toast are therefore exactly what the sheets produce. The sheets are not opened and the inputs are reset afterwards.
- Replies `{ type:'OB_QUICKADD_RESULT', reqId, ok, msg }` to `e.source` (falls back to `window.parent`) so the launcher only clears its inputs on a confirmed save. A repeated `reqId` returns ok without adding again. An amount that is zero, not a number or under one penny, or over £1,000,000, is rejected with `ok:false` and nothing is written. Label is trimmed and capped at 60 characters. Bills with a blank label saves as "Spend" (existing `saveBtx` behaviour); Food with a blank label saves with no label (existing `saveSpend` behaviour). Origin guard unchanged.
- Additive: `openFoodSheet`, `openBillsSheet`, `openSpendingTab`, `openBillsTab`, `openBillsTxSheet` untouched. No data-model, calculation or sync change.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, badge, header comment, `pal-shared.js?v=`, and the display-only `version` field in the save and the JSON backup. ⚠ Those last two still said `3.81` at v3.82 (v3.82 did not update them); corrected here.
- Tested (headless jsdom, real `on-budget.html` and `pal-shared.js`): Food and Bills adds (amount, label, category, type, cleared, date, source), Bills cleared balance 1000 → 974.01, persistence to `on_budget_v1`, label history, duplicate `reqId`, zero / NaN / sub-penny rejection, foreign origin ignored, sheets not left open, `openSpendingTab`, `openBillsTab` and `openFoodSheet` unchanged. Not tested: real browser, live Supabase sync of a quick-added entry, second device, phone.

### v3.100 — Suite WP0.2c — Dates in British Summer Time: projected finish dates and period starts were a day early — 4 Nov 2026

- **Found by:** the suite review (3 Nov), confirmed by running the v3.99 code under the Europe/London time zone.
- **Defect:** three places turned a local date into text with `toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, which is the UTC date. For local-midnight dates during British Summer Time (late March to late October) that is the previous day. Effects in v3.99: `projectedFinishDate()` was one day early; `getDateRange("month")` returned the last day of the previous month (for example `2026-06-30` in July), so the Stats "this month" totals started a day early; the "week" start and the "Last 7 days" label were one day early; "year" was correct only by coincidence of how it is built. In winter the old and new code give identical results.
- **Fix (`reading-tracker.html`):** new `localISODate(d)` (uses `PalShared.localISO` from `pal-shared.js` 1.0.0, with an identical inline fallback) replaces the three conversions in `projectedFinishDate`, `getDateRange` and `getPeriodLabel`; the "all time" start is now `new Date(2000, 0, 1)` (local) instead of a UTC-parsed string. `todayISO()` (already local) is untouched. No stored data, key, sync, contract or backup shape changed; existing records are not rewritten.
- **Library tag:** `pal-shared.js?v=3.89` → `?v=3.100`, so Reading now loads the bundle that contains `PalShared` (it had been lagging since v3.89).
- **Version sync:** `<title>`, header logo, inline comment: v3.100.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, Europe/London, fixed clocks): old v3.99 and new v3.100 run side by side at BST midday, 00:30 BST, winter, and the spring-forward day. New: month, year and all-time starts correct; projected finish dates exact; week start is today minus 6; no page errors. Old: defect reproduced in every BST case; winter output identical to new apart from the fixed-date control. **Not tested:** real iPhone/Safari, a signed-in session with real data, the Stats screen visually, cloud sync. Covered by the deployment check.

### v3.98 — MR-083 — Fix: book details did not open from the Bookcase for books in the other section — 4 Nov 2026

- **Bug report (Pete, deployment check):** v3.97-T7 failed. Selecting a book or audiobook on the Bookcase did not open the details (modal on phone, side pane on desktop), with Arrange off as well as on.

Header counts still describe the To read list. List layout unchanged (To read | Read switch behaves as before). No data, storage, sync, launcher or schema change.

- Version: `<title>`, badge, inline comment v3.98.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, stub `pal-shared.js`, real mouse clicks with the book scrolled into view): at 430 px the modal and at 1280 px the pane open for the right book for To read and Read, standalone and series, book and audiobook (v3.97 showed the wrong book for Read items on desktop); modal stays open after a re-render and after the owned switch, with all four sections inside; List layout shows only To read books in To read and only Read books in Read; JS syntax check; no page errors. Not tested: phone touch on a real device, live sync on a second device. (Earlier v3.97 test scripts opened details via `spineOpenBook` and never clicked a book, which is why this escaped.)

### v3.97 — MR-082 — One Bookcase: To read and Read sections, mixed books and audiobooks, series bands, series number on every spine — 4 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 4 Nov):** keep Arrange and plants / trinkets for books and audiobooks; always show the series book number on the spine; one bookshelf for all books with clear To read and Read sections, where dragging a book or audiobook between them sets its status in Arrange mode; a coloured background for a series with its books together and in order (a series may be split across Read and To read); options for telling audiobooks apart. **Decisions (Pete):** layout A (mixed shelf with an All / Books / Audiobooks filter at the top) and keep the current audiobook look (aqua cap and headphones).
- **Bookcase layout (List layout unchanged):** the To read | Read switch is hidden in the Bookcase. Two sections, **TO READ** and **✓ READ**, each with its own count and its own tinted frame (accent / green), books and audiobooks together. A filter under the toolbar shows **All / Books / Audiobooks** with counts; the choice is remembered on the device (`rt_bk_filter`). Search and the tag filter apply to both sections.
- **Series:** books with the same series name (case and spacing ignored) sit together on a **tinted band** with the series name on top, in book-number order (books and audiobooks of one series mix; no number sorts last). Seven-colour palette chosen from the series name, so a series keeps its colour. If a series is split across the sections, each section has its own band. A band that wraps onto a second shelf row continues with its own band piece.
- **Number on the spine:** every series book with a number shows it in a small round chip at the foot of the spine (cover tiles: top-left), so a long title can never hide it. Decimals show as typed (3.5). It shows on the Bookcase, the Home shelf and the active cards. The spine text is now the plain title (v3.92–v3.96 appended " #n" there). The full "Title (Series #n)" is unchanged everywhere else.
- **Arrange:** drag a book into the other section (onto a book or the empty shelf) to change its status: into **Read** sets it finished **today**; into **To read** clears finished (reading log kept, same as "Not read after all"). Dragging within a section reorders; **a series moves as one block** (order inside it follows the book numbers); dragging a series book into the other section moves **only that book**, and it joins that section's band for the series if there is one. Decor can be dragged between sections too. Arrange also works while a Books / Audiobooks filter is on.
- **Plants and trinkets:** the Add tray appears in **each section** (they were per Books / Audiobooks shelf). Existing decor keeps its section and position. Decor added with All showing is shown only under All; decor added while a Books or Audiobooks filter is on shows under that filter and under All; decor made before this version (tied to the Books or Audiobooks shelf) shows under All and its own filter.
- **Data (additive):** one new optional field on a Book List item, `shelfOrder` (display order within a section, because books and audiobooks now interleave). Dropping a book also rewrites the per-type `manualOrder` in step with what you see, so List-view Manual sort and the monthly queue (when its reading order is Manual) follow the shelf. Items without `shelfOrder` show after those with it: books first, then audiobooks, by their manual order, so nothing moves until you arrange. No schema, storage-key, backup-format or launcher change; older versions ignore `shelfOrder` and keep working (they would show decor per Books / Audiobooks shelf and the old two-view bookcase).
- ⚠ **Known limits / to confirm:** (1) a book dragged into Read gets today's date, and there is no way yet in the details panel to change the finished date afterwards (the Mark as read form on a To read book does take a date); (2) the Bookshelf header counts (Total / Books / Audiobooks) still describe the To read list only, as before; (3) a series band shows even for a series with one book in a section; (4) the Home "this month" shelf is unchanged apart from the number chip.
- **Audiobook look options shown to Pete (not built):** sound-wave stripes, slimmer rounded top, dashed edge with headphones; he kept the aqua cap and headphones.
- Version: `<title>`, badge, inline comment v3.97.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, 430 px and 1280 px, stub `pal-shared.js`, the real file; JS syntax check; real mouse drags): two sections in the right order with counts; series in number order and together (including a decimal and a book + audiobook mix); band membership; number chip on each numbered series spine and none on standalone or number-less ones; switch hidden; All / Books / Audiobooks filters including decor visibility by group; legacy decor shown in All; arrange tray in both sections; dragging a standalone book To read → Read (finished today) and a series book To read → Read (only that book moved, joined the Read band in number order) and Read → To read (finished cleared); dragging one series book moved the whole series as a block and kept it together; decor dragged between sections (scope changed); order stable after re-render; per-type `manualOrder` follows the display order; search across both sections; details panel opens; unowned fade and cart still work; Home shelf chip; no page errors. Not tested: live sync (shelfOrder, status and decor changes) on a second device, touch dragging on a real phone, many books on a real shelf, the light theme, a series whose members have no page counts, the monthly queue after a drop (reasoned from `manualOrder`).

### v3.85 — MR-070 — Covers found for ISBN look-ups; looser title/author search; per-book Spine/Cover — 2 Nov 2026

- **Reported (Pete, v3.84):** two books updated from their ISBN still had no cover anywhere; wanted the cover in the details panel and a per-book choice of spine or cover on the shelf (cover facing out); wanted search to work without an exact match.
- **Cause (no cover):** an ISBN look-up asked Open Library only, and Open Library often knows a book but holds no cover for it; because it returned a result, Google Books was never consulted, so nothing was saved.
- **Fix:** after any look-up, a result without a cover gets one from Google Books (by ISBN, or by title and author, title-checked), then from Open Library's by-ISBN cover (`?default=false`, only kept if the image really loads). Applies to Find details, the add form, the edit panel and the bulk Covers tool. Books already saved without a cover: run **Book List > Covers** (it uses the book's ISBN first).
- **Looser search:** title/author search tries strict title+author, then a free-text query on the significant words, then the first three words of the title; Google Books gets a plain-words query after the `intitle:` form. Bulk matching also accepts a title that shares at least 60% of its words (offered as "check this", unticked). Retries are spaced 1 s apart.
- **Per-book shelf style:** the details panel (Book List > Bookcase) has Spine | Cover for a book with a cover, stored on the book as `shelfStyle` and synced with it; the bookcase button sets the default for books with no choice. Books without a cover always show as spines.
- **Data/sync:** one new optional field on Book List items (`shelfStyle`); no migration.
- Tested (headless Chromium, mocked services and Supabase): ISBN result without an Open Library cover gets a Google Books cover; misspelt title found by the loose query; bulk matches an ISBN book and saves its cover; details panel shows the cover; per-book Cover/Spine; plus suites bulk 21, v3.84 22, reading 23, search 28, backup 30, launcher 21, page-error regression 0 diffs. Not tested: the real services from Pete's browser, a phone, a second device.

### v3.84 — MR-069 — Bulk look-up reliability; show books as covers instead of spines — 2 Nov 2026

- **Reported (Pete):** the Covers and details tool stopped with "Open Library and Google Books could not be reached (3 times in a row)" and counted the 2 failed books as "no match"; a book looked up on its own showed no cover; wanted the option to show a book by its cover rather than its spine.
- **Look-up reliability:** `bkGet` timeout raised from 8 s to 20 s and now retries once (after 1.5 s) on a timeout, network error, HTTP 429 or 5xx. Errors now say what happened (`HTTP 403`, `timed out`, `blocked or offline`) and are shown in the dialog, so the real cause on Pete's device can be seen. `bkLookup` returns `failed:true` only when both services failed to answer.
- **No false "no match":** failed look-ups are no longer added to the no-match list and are not cached; they are reported as "could not be looked up … tried again next time". No-match memory key changed `rt_bk_nomatch_v1` → `rt_bk_nomatch_v2` so the books wrongly remembered by v3.83 are offered again. After 3 failures in a row the run stops with the cause and a 3 s pause between failed books.
- **Covers option:** Bookcase bar has **Show covers / Show spines** (per device, `rt_bk_covers`). Books with a cover show as a cover tile (title fallback if the image fails, ✓ finished, progress bar, active marker); books without a cover remain spines. Select, drag/arrange and the detail pane work unchanged (same `.bk-item` button). The detail pane shows the cover when the book has one. Default stays Spines. The single-book lookup does save the cover; the Bookcase previously only drew spines (list rows already showed covers), which is why it did not appear.
- **Data/sync:** no data-model or sync change.
- Tested (headless Chromium, mocked Open Library/Google Books, mocked Supabase): HTTP 403 shows the cause and records nothing as no-match; one 429 is retried and succeeds; covers toggle, persistence across reload, mixed cover/spine rows, detail pane cover; existing bulk suite (21), reading suite, search, backup, launcher regression diffs 0. Not tested: the real services from Pete's browser (CORS, rate limits, real latency), a phone, a second device.

### v3.83 — MR-068 — Add covers and details to existing books (bulk, with review); author-only search — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 2 Nov):** a bulk tool to back-populate covers and details for books already in the app; plus, asked in the same exchange, finding by author alone.
- **Where:** Book List › **Covers** (next to Tidy up). It lists how many books have no cover (Book List items **and every tracker's books**), then **Look them up**: one title + author search each (Open Library, Google Books if needed), about one a second to respect Open Library's limit, the same title+author looked up once even if it appears twice, with progress and a "Stop and review what was found so far" button. After 3 failed lookups in a row (neither service reachable) it stops with a message.
- **Review before anything changes:** a list of suggestions, each showing your book, what was found (title, author, year, publisher, cover) and a verdict. **"Looks right"** (exact or leading-title match, author agrees, a cover exists) is pre-ticked; **"check this one"** (partial title, author mismatch or no cover) is unticked. Apply writes only the ticked ones.
- **What Apply changes — additions only:** cover (`coverId` / `coverUrl`), publisher and year if empty, ISBN if empty, **pages only if the book has none**, and `metaSource`. Title, author, genre, notes, reviews, progress, ownership and tags are never touched. Each changed record is pushed to the cloud on its own; a tracker book is pushed with **its own** tracker's id (not the active tracker's).
- **No-match memory:** books with no match are remembered on this device (`rt_bk_nomatch_v1`) and skipped next time; "Also retry the books with no match" clears that. Unticked "check this one" suggestions are simply offered again.
- **Bug found and fixed during testing:** the first version held references to the book objects seen when the lookups started; a background sync can replace those objects during a longer run, so the update could be written to stale copies. Apply now re-finds every book by id at the moment it applies (a book deleted meanwhile is skipped).
- **Author-only search:** Find details now works with just an author (Open Library `author=` with no title; Google Books `inauthor:`); the empty-form message says "an ISBN, a title or an author".
- Version updated: `<title>`, on-screen badge, `pal-shared.js?v=3.83`. No change to data structures beyond the v3.82 optional fields.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, both services mocked): count excludes books that already have a cover; 4 distinct lookups for 5 books, spaced at least a second apart; verdicts and default ticks (exact "Dune" beats "Dune Messiah"; a no-cover partial match is unticked); no-match counted; Apply 3 selected adds cover/publisher/year/ISBN and fills pages only where empty (an existing 500 stays), leaves genre, notes, title, author, ownership alone; unticked and no-match books unchanged; a tracker book updated with its own tracker id and each record pushed; a simulated sync replacing every object mid-run did not lose the update; no-match memory and the retry button; stopping midway; both services down stops after 3 failures and changes nothing; author-only search; earlier suites re-run (Reading lookup 23/23, search 28/28, backups and the original-vs-new regression comparison below). Not tested: the real Open Library / Google Books services, large libraries (hundreds of books: about 1.2 s each), covers loading on your devices.

### v3.82 — MR-067 — Book details lookup (ISBN or title) with covers — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 2 Nov; Stage D):** ISBN entry, book metadata lookup and covers, with manual entry kept as the fallback. A visual library / bookcase view was also on the list: **the Book List already has a Bookcase layout (and spines), so nothing was added there**; covers appear on the list rows instead.
- **Sources assessed before building (their own documentation, 2 Nov 2026):** Open Library: no key; non-identified requests limited to about 1 per second; covers fetched by **cover id are not rate-limited** (by ISBN: 100 per IP per 5 minutes); guidelines ask for human-initiated, cached, low-volume use and a courtesy credit. Google Books: no key needed for light use with a lower quota (default about 1,000 requests a day per project). Chosen: **Open Library first, Google Books only when Open Library finds nothing or cannot be reached.** Single-user, one request per button press, so well inside both. Browser-side (CORS) access to Open Library was not stated in its documentation and was **not verified against the live service** (see Not tested); failure is handled by a clear message and manual entry.
- **Change:** Book List **Add to Book List** form and each item's **edit panel** get an ISBN field and a **Find details** button. With an ISBN it makes one lookup; with no ISBN it searches by title (and author if filled) and offers up to 5 matches with cover, author, year, publisher and pages. Tapping one fills title, author, pages and genre (mapped to the app's own genre list) and keeps the ISBN, cover, publisher and year; nothing is saved until you press Add / Save. ISBNs are validated (10 or 13 digits with check digit). The edit panel shows the current cover and a "Remove cover and details" button; blanking the ISBN field clears it.
- **Data (additive, optional):** `isbn`, `coverId` (Open Library cover id), `coverUrl` (https only, Google fallback), `publisher`, `publishYear`, `metaSource`. Covers are linked by id / URL and **not stored as images**, so storage use is a few bytes per book. The fields are carried when a Book List item becomes a tracker book and back (`buildBookFromWishlist`, `moveBookToWishlist`), are included in JSON export, and older backups and items without them load unchanged. The tracker-side **Add a book** form is unchanged (no lookup there yet).
- **Display:** Book List list rows show a small cover and a "publisher · year · ISBN" line; the Universal Search row for a book now also carries year and ISBN. Open Library is credited in the panel text only through the "via Open Library / Google Books" note.
- Version updated: `<title>`, on-screen badge, `pal-shared.js?v=3.82`.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, **both services mocked**): ISBN validation; one request to Open Library for an ISBN and none to Google; title search with 3 candidates; picking fills fields and genre; item stores all fields; form resets; list row shows cover and meta line; Open Library down falls back to Google Books and says so, with an https cover URL stored; both down shows a clear message and a manual add still works with no metadata fields; bad ISBN and empty input messages; edit panel prefill, remove-and-clear, re-find-and-save; carry to a tracker book; export contains the fields; search index row carries ISBN and year; phone screenshot reviewed; earlier suites re-run (search 28/28, launcher 21/21, apps 17/17, backups 30/30, regression comparison with the original files: no differences). Not tested: the **real** Open Library and Google Books services (CORS, response shapes, quotas), covers loading from `covers.openlibrary.org` on your devices, barcode scanning (not built: browser support, notably Safari, unverified), the tracker-side add form.

### v3.79 — MR-064 — Every book drawn as a solid book; the marks explained in a Key; size follows page count — 2 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 2 Nov):** why do some books on the shelves appear dashed; make the rest look like the first (solid) book; explain and label the logic of the dashes, tabs and other marks; apply it to the Home books view too; and is a book's size linked to its page count (if not, make it so).
- ⚠ **ID note:** the backlog was not supplied, so **MR-064 is the next number after MR-063 in this changelog**, not one confirmed against the backlog.
- **Why they were dashed (v3.75 – v3.78 logic):** the spine had three looks by progress. **Not started** was a faint, dashed-outline "ghost" of the book; **in progress** was solid in the part read and faded above it with a bookmark line; **finished** was solid with a tick. So only the one book with reading progress looked solid. A lime tab meant "Reading" (set on the book or its List chip), independent of the dashes.
- **Change:** all books are now **solid, cloth-coloured spines** with a lit left edge, a shaded right edge and two ridge bands, whether or not they are started. Progress no longer uses dashes: a started book keeps its **bookmark line** and a **darker top** (still to go) over a **bright bottom** (read), with the % on wide spines. Applied to the bookcase, the Home shelf, the Book List row thumbnails and the key samples. Dashed outlines are no longer used anywhere.
- **Marks, now labelled:** lime tab = Reading; bookmark line and darker top = how far you've read; plain spine = not started; tick = finished; **aqua cap and a headphones icon = audiobook** (the icon is new); a **?** = no page count set. A collapsible **"Key: what the marks mean"** with drawn examples sits under the shelf on Home and above the shelves in the bookcase.
- **Size:** it was already linked to length, but only weakly: height was `pages × 0.28` limited to 100 – 184 and width `24 + pages/18` limited to 30 – 56, so every book under about 360 pages came out the same height and every long one the same size, and a book with no page count got the minimum. Now **thickness follows pages** (`20 + pages × 0.048`, 28 – 66 px; chapters for audiobooks) and **height rises a little with length** (`112 + pages × 0.085`, 112 – 198 px). A book with **no page count uses a standard 320-page (24-chapter) size and shows a "?"** so it is clear the size is a placeholder; setting the pages (Edit, or the first Log) resizes it. On your 2 Nov backup 23 of 87 books had no page count.
- **Not changed:** data model, storage, sync, backups, every feature; arrangement, decor, Reading switch, Mark as read and Tidy up.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, header logo span, `pal-shared.js?v=3.79`, inline changelog comment.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, stub `pal-shared.js`): the full v3.78 suite re-run, **176 passed**; plus screenshots of the bookcase and Home shelf against your real 2 Nov backup at 390 and 1360 px (solid spines, aqua cap and headphones on audiobooks, bookmark and darker top on a started book, "?" key sample, sizes varying with pages, key opens, no overlap).
- **Not tested:** a real phone and Safari; the real launcher and cloud.
- **Known limitations:** the spine colour is still picked from the title (no stored colour), so two books may share a colour; very long titles are cut off with "…" on narrow spines (the full title is the tooltip and the screen-reader label). Size is a guide, not to scale.

### v3.78 — MR-063 — Mark as read without logging pages; Tidy up; past reads no longer land on To read — 1 Nov 2026

- **Reported (Pete, 1 Nov, with a backup `my-reading.json` exported 20:57):** books repeated in To read, books that have already been read showing as To read, and no way to mark a book read without logging every page.
- ⚠ **ID note:** the backlog was not supplied, so **MR-063 is the next number after MR-062 in this changelog**, not one confirmed against the backlog.
- **What the backup showed:** 87 Book List items, 77 unread. **11 titles were repeated** (the same book added on 13 Jul and again on 12 Sep, i.e. a book import run twice; Dracula three times), plus near-repeats (a trailing full stop, a "bk8" suffix, a subtitle). **25 unread items were books and audiobooks already finished in the "Read in Past" and "Audio Listened in past" history trackers.**
- **Cause of the "already read" books (a defect in the v3.67 / MR-052 tracker migration):** `mergeAllTrackersIntoBookList()` decided a tracker book was finished only when `pages > 0` and the log reached it (or `manualComplete`). History books have **no page count**, so they were imported as **unread**, while the Home Book List card (v3.64 / MR-049) deliberately counts the very same books as read. Every restore re-runs that migration, so they came back each time. It also stamped finished books with **today's date** when none was recorded.
- **Fix to the migration:** a tracker book is finished when `logged >= pages` (so no page count counts as finished, the same rule as the Home card) or `manualComplete`; the finish date is the book's own date, else its last log date, else **"date unknown"**; and when a Book List copy of a tracker book already exists (the case in your data) and is still unread, it is now **marked read** (date unknown) rather than left alone. Running the migration over your backup turns the 25 into Read automatically.
- **Mark as read:** a book's details (modal on phone, panel on desktop) now have **✓ Mark as read (no pages needed)**: pick the date finished, or tick **I don't remember when**. Nothing is logged and the page count is untouched. A finished book offers **Not read after all** (puts it back on To read; its log is kept). The List rows have a **✓ Mark read** chip that opens the details.
- **"Date unknown":** stored as the finish date `1900-01-01` (no new field). It is shown as "date unknown", it counts as read everywhere (Read shelf, Past, Reviews, Home card), it sorts last, and it is **not counted in any month** in Stats or "finished this month".
- **Tidy up (Book List › Tidy up):** a review before anything changes. It lists (a) **repeated titles**, keeping the copy with the most history (logs, notes, review, active, tags) and ticking the others for removal, and (b) **To read items that are finished in the old history trackers** (matched by id, then by title), ticked to be marked read. "Similar" titles (same text before a colon, e.g. a subtitle) are listed **unticked** for you to decide. The button shows how many sure changes are waiting. Removals use the existing delete (with its cloud tombstone). On your backup it finds 17 repeats and, once the history trackers are back in place, 25 past reads.
- **No double counting:** the Home Book List card no longer counts a finished tracker book again when a finished Book List copy of it exists (before tidying, the card showed 95 for a list of 70).
- **Also:** dialogs now sit above the floating bar and the Add pill.
- **Not changed:** the data model apart from the "date unknown" convention, sync, backups, Stats figures, everything frozen at v3.74.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, header logo span, `pal-shared.js?v=3.78`, inline changelog comment.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, stub `pal-shared.js`): the v3.77 suite re-run plus new checks, **176 passed, repeated twice**; and a run against **your actual backup**: before 87 items; the migration heals the 25; Tidy finds 17 repeats (1 similar left unticked) and removes them (70 left); no repeated titles remain; the Read shelf holds 24 books and 12 audiobooks, none counted in a month; the card total goes from 95 to 70 with no double count; a book marked read without pages keeps its 68 pages and 0 logs; no page errors.
- **Not tested:** the real `pal-shared.js` and cloud (so how the cloud treats the removals and the healed copies on your other devices); the real launcher; a real phone and Safari.
- **Known limitations:** matching is by title (and tracker book id), so two different books with the same title would be listed together (review before pressing Apply). "Similar" titles are only suggestions. Marked-read books have no finish date to show in the monthly history until you edit them. Take a backup before pressing Apply if you want a way back.

### v3.77 — MR-062 — Plants and shelf settings now sync; an easier way to the bookcase on phone — 1 Nov 2026

- **Reported (Pete, 1 Nov):** (1) the bookcase is hard to reach on the phone; (2) plants and trinkets were not syncing across devices.
- ⚠ **ID note:** the backlog was not supplied, so **MR-062 is the next number after MR-061 in this changelog**, not one confirmed against the backlog.
- **Cause of the sync fault (real defect, introduced in v3.75):** decor is stored in `monthlyConfig`, which travels in the synced `__monthlyConfig__` row. The shared `pal-sync` `table().pull()` only pushes a record that is **new** to the cloud or an unconfirmed tombstone, never an **edit to a record that already exists** (the same structural limit recorded at v3.29 / v3.30 for books and wishlist items). So a change to the settings row was saved locally but never reached the cloud, and another device could not pick it up. ⚠ This limit also applied to the old monthly targets and collections (they were never pushed after the first time), which is no longer relevant now they are removed.
- **Fix:** every decor change (add, move, remove), and the one-time clearing of old collections, now calls a new `rtPushConfigNow()`, a direct `_rtWishlist.upsert()` of the settings row, the same proven route `pushWishlistItemNow()` uses. If it cannot be sent (offline or signed out) a local retry flag `rt_cfg_dirty` is kept and the settings are pushed again after the next successful sync pull. The receiving side needed no change: `reassembleFromSync()` already applies the newest settings row, and the bookcase redraws after a pull. The flag is a local helper key (not synced, not in backups).
- **Bookcase access on phone:** Home's hero now has a full-width **Open bookcase** button (always opens the bookcase, even if you last chose List), and the **Book List card moves up**, directly under your active books and above Reading days. Nothing was removed; the bottom bar is still four tabs.
- **Not changed:** the data model, backups, the List view, logging, active books and everything listed as frozen at v3.74 / v3.76.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, header logo span, `pal-shared.js?v=3.77`, inline changelog comment.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, stub `pal-shared.js` with the session and the cloud upsert faked): the v3.76 suite re-run plus 11 new checks, **152 passed, repeated three times**. New: the Open bookcase button, its landing in the bookcase (also over a saved List choice) and the card order on phone; offline changes push nothing and keep the retry flag; once signed in the settings row is upserted with id `__monthlyConfig__` and contains every plant, and the flag clears; a later offline change is pushed by the retry; the pull wrapper is installed; settings arriving from another device through the real merge function show their plants in the bookcase.
- **Not tested:** the real `pal-sync` and Supabase (so a true two-device round trip, and whether the cloud accepts this upsert exactly as it does for books, has not been seen); the real launcher; a real phone and Safari. If plants still do not appear on the second device, the Sync & Backup log will show "Direct push of settings" or "Settings push FAILED" with the reason.
- **Known limitations:** the newest settings win as a whole (as for the old targets), so two devices changing the bookcase decor at the same moment while offline will keep only one side's changes. The retry runs after the next successful sync pull, not on a timer.

### v3.76 — MR-061 — Targets and collections removed; books you mark as "Reading" are the front screen — 1 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 1 Nov):** remove the target idea; track active books and audiobooks that show on the front screen (several at once, set by you in the book details); the app and Stats should always aim at **one full book each month**, while Stats keeps tracking books, pages, chapters and days read. Decisions: a **status line plus a gentle pace reminder** for the **most recently read** active book (with its own stats and progress; if only one is active, that one); dated collections **removed entirely**; every **started, unfinished book starts as active**; the launcher logs to the **active book read most recently**.
- ⚠ **ID note:** the backlog was not supplied, so **MR-061 is the next number after MR-060 in this changelog**, not one confirmed against the backlog.
- **Active books:** a new optional per-book flag `active` (true / false) on Book List items. It is set from the **Reading switch in a book's details** (modal on phone, pane on desktop) or the **● Reading / ○ Not reading chip on a List row**. Older data has no flag: a **started, unfinished** book counts as active until you choose (so nothing is written to your data on upgrade); finishing a book takes it off the shelf. The flag travels with the existing synced Book List record and in JSON backups; older app versions ignore it.
- **Home:** the hero shows **this month's finished books and every active book** as spines. Beside the shelf: the **most recently read active book** (title, progress bar, pages read and left, last read, pages a day this week) and this month's figures (**finished, pages, chapters, days read**). The chip says **"Aim: one full book this month"**, or **"✓ n finished this month"** once a book (or audiobook) is done. While nothing is finished it adds a **pace reminder** ("About 18 pages a day finishes it by 30 Nov — you're on pace / a little behind"); once one is finished it says the month's book is done. Under it, **one card per active book** with its own Log box (page or chapter reached, same validation as before, Enter works). "Month by month" replaces the old Monthly progress card: books finished each month (a tick for one or more), pages, chapters and days read. "Reading days" and the Book List card stay.
- **Removed:** monthly targets and reading order (books, pages, audiobooks, chapters; cycle start date), the "reach today" page / chapter and the daily pace boxes, the two Monthly cards, "Up next", and the **dated collections** feature (cards, creation dialogs and the stored collections, which are cleared from the settings on first load; take a backup before updating if you want to keep them). The Book List's "Monthly targets & reading order" panel is hidden. The old code and the stored target fields are left in place, unused, so older versions and old backups still open. The month is the calendar month.
- **Launcher (`RT_ACTION` quick-log):** `bookListQueue(type)` now returns the **active** books of that type, most recently read first, so a quick-log from the launcher goes to the active book you read most recently; with none active it replies that there is no current book. Message names and replay safety are unchanged. ⚠ The launcher's own Reading card was not supplied; if it shows target figures it may need a matching update.
- **Bookcase:** the lime "reading" tab now follows the Reading flag (previously the queue head plus started books).
- **Not changed:** storage keys, sync, export / import, the Stats screen's figures (it never used the targets), logging in the details pane, the pace maths on the old Tracker screen.
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, header logo span, `pal-shared.js?v=3.76`, inline changelog comment.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, stub `pal-shared.js`, local data only): the v3.75 suite re-run with its target-based checks replaced; **141 checks passed, repeated three times**. New: old Monthly cards and collections gone; one card per active book; logging from a card adds an entry, updates the card and refuses a lower page; switching a book off removes its card and is saved (and appears in the JSON backup); the most recently read book is the focus; the pace reminder shows only while nothing is finished and is replaced by "done" afterwards; single-active shows "Reading now"; collections in an old config are cleared; the Monthly targets panel is hidden; the Reading chip on List rows and the switch in the details modal both toggle the flag; the launcher quick-log goes to the most recently read active book once.
- **Not tested:** the real `pal-shared.js` and any real sync of the `active` flag between devices; the real launcher and its Reading card; a real phone and Safari; a very large Book List.
- **Known limitations:** the month for the pace reminder is the calendar month, and the reminder is a prompt, not a stored goal. Audiobooks count toward "one full book" (any finished item does). Pages a day this week is measured over the last seven days including today.

### v3.75 — MR-060 — Bookcase view of the Book List; Home shelf shows every started book — 1 Nov 2026

- **Request (Pete, 1 Nov):** (1) Home's shelf should show **all the books you are reading**, not just one, with the stats underneath as in v3.74. (2) A **bookcase view** that toggles **read and want to read**, shows every book with its progress, marks the active ones, lets you **move and order** books, opens a **modal** (desktop: the details panel) with the book's info, edits and **reading log**, and lets you add **plants and trinkets**. Decisions (Pete): decor is **synced with your data**; dragging changes the **Book List manual order**; books and audiobooks on **separate shelves**; Home shows **every book with progress that is not finished**.
- ⚠ **ID note:** the backlog was not supplied, so **MR-060 is the next number after MR-059 in this changelog**, not one confirmed against the backlog.
- **Home:** the hero shelf now shows this month's finished books plus **every started, unfinished book** (books first, then audiobooks, each in manual order; up to eight, with a "+n more" chip). The shelf previously showed only the head of each reading queue. If nothing has been started yet it falls back to each queue's next book. **A spine is now a button**: it opens that book in the Bookcase. Meters, the "reach today" line, the Monthly cards and everything underneath are unchanged. ⚠ The Monthly cards and "Log" still work on the **queue head** only; other started books are logged from the Bookcase details.
- **Bookcase (Book List › Bookcase | List):** the Book List now has a **List / Bookcase** switch. **Bookcase is the default**; the choice is remembered (new local UI-preference key `rt_wl_layout`, not synced, not in backups). The Active / Past buttons are relabelled **To read / Read**; the existing search and tag filter apply to the bookcase too.
  - Books and audiobooks are on **separate shelves** that wrap to new planks to fit the width. Spine height and width follow page / chapter count; a solid spine is the part read, faded is still to go, a bookmark and a percentage show the current page, finished books carry a tick, audiobooks an aqua cap. **Active books** (started and unfinished, plus each queue's next book) get a **lime tab** and sit slightly forward.
  - **Arrange** mode: drag a book or a decor item (mouse, touch or pen) to move it; a lime marker shows where it will land. Dragging a book calls the existing `setManualPosition()`, so it writes the **Book List manual order** (same sync pushes as before). The screen says the monthly queue follows it when the reading order is set to Manual.
  - **Tap a book:** phone / tablet open a **bottom-sheet modal**; desktop selects it into the **details pane**. Both show the book's progress, a quick **Log** box (page or chapter reached, dated today, through the existing `addReadingEntry()`), and the existing Reading history, Notes, Review (finished books) and Edit sections (the same DOM nodes, moved, so every handler works; they go back to the row on close).
  - **Plants and trinkets:** ten drawings (fern, succulent, cactus, monstera, globe, candle, mug, photo frame, hourglass, lamp). In Arrange mode each shelf group has a tray to add them; drag to move, × to remove. They are placed **after a book** (or at the start / end), so they stay with their neighbour when you reorder, and are kept separately for To read and Read and for books and audiobooks.
- **The one data addition:** `appState.monthlyConfig.decor` — an array of `{id, kind, scope:'want'|'read', group:'book'|'audiobook', after:<book id or null>}`. It lives **inside the existing settings object**, so it travels in the existing synced `__monthlyConfig__` row, in JSON backups (`monthlyConfig`) and in restore, with **no schema change and no migration**; `updatedAt` is bumped on every change so the newest copy wins a merge (the same whole-object, newest-wins rule the monthly targets already use). Older app versions ignore the extra field. Existing config code only writes the fields it knows, so decor is preserved.
- **Not changed:** every v3.74 behaviour listed as frozen (storage keys, sync, export / import, launcher messages, pace maths); the List view and its rows, desktop details pane, sort and tag tools; `pal-shared.js` (only the `?v=` query).
- Version updated everywhere: `<title>`, header logo span, `pal-shared.js?v=3.75`, inline changelog comment.
- Tested (Stage 1, headless Chromium, a **stub** `pal-shared.js`, local data only): the full v3.74 suite re-run (80 checks) and 47 new checks, **127 passed, repeated four times**. New: Home shelf shows every started book; Bookcase is the default and the List is still available; shelves, planks and groups; To read shows the 6 unfinished books and Read the 2 finished; active tabs; no sideways scroll; tap opens the modal (phone, bottom sheet) or pane (desktop); logging from the details adds an entry and the modal refreshes; closing the modal puts the sections back; decor tray, add, render, remove; decor stored in `monthlyConfig`, present in the JSON backup and in the synced row builder, `updatedAt` bumped; **drag reorder** (mouse pointer events) changes the manual order and the bookcase follows; decor and order survive a reload; import restores decor; the earlier launcher quick-log, resize and persistence checks. A scripted diff confirms the original JavaScript is unchanged apart from the earlier colour / font strings.
- **Not tested:** real touch dragging on a phone (pointer events were simulated with a mouse; touch uses `touch-action:none` in Arrange mode), real Supabase merge of the decor between two devices, the real `pal-shared.js`, real Safari, very large collections (hundreds of spines), the launcher.
- **Known limitations:** decor is anchored to a book, so if you move or finish that book the decor moves with the shelf position it now follows; a book finished or un-finished moves between the To read and Read cases (decor stays on the case it was placed on). The Monthly widgets still log only the queue-head book. Dragging between the Books and Audiobooks shelves, and between To read and Read, is not supported. Arranging while a filter or search is active only orders the books you can see.

### v3.73 — MR-058 — Launcher quick-log receiver — 18 Oct 2026

- **Why (feature):** lets the launcher's Reading card log the page (book) or chapter (audiobook) reached for the current active Book List item. See launcher v11.19 (PET-123).
- **Change:** the existing `message` listener now also handles `RT_ACTION`. `ping` replies `RT_PONG {reqId, ready}`; ready only after `selectUser`'s first cloud pull has settled (`_rtFirstPullSettled`) and a user is selected. `quickLogProgress {kind, value, reqId}` runs `quickLogBookListProgress()`: takes `bookListQueue(type)[0]`, validates (a number above the current position, not above the total), adds an ordinary `readingEntries` record `{id, date: today, pageTo}`, sets `completedDate` when it reaches the total, then `save()` and `pushWishlistItemNow()` as the in-app logger does, and replies `RT_QUICKLOG_RESULT {ok, kind, title, value, added, total, finished}` or `{ok:false, error}`. The result is stored per `reqId` and replayed on a re-send, so the launcher's re-sends cannot log twice. `rtQuickReapply()` runs right after `reassembleFromSync()` in `pullAllFromCloud()` and puts back a quick-logged entry if a later pull dropped it (then pushes it again).
- **Deliberate difference from the in-app logger:** an item with no page/chapter count is rejected with a message ("set it in the app first") rather than treated as "set the total", because a bare number from the launcher is ambiguous.
- No data-model, localStorage key, export/import or sync-schema change. The launcher origin guard is unchanged (same-origin only).
- Version: title, logo span, `pal-shared.js?v=` query and inline changelog comment set to v3.73.
- Tested (Stage 1): `node --check`; scripted run of the real receiver, queue and entry functions (18 checks): ping not-ready then ready, no reply before ready, book log, same-`reqId` replay does not double-log, rejects not-higher / over-total / non-numeric / no item left / no page count, audiobook uses chapters and does not touch the book, finishing sets `completedDate`, re-apply after a pull drops the entry and is idempotent. Not tested: the real app boot and first pull (needs the real `pal-shared.js` and Supabase), the real browser, a second device.

# Test & Issues

> ⏸ **On hold since 2026-10-04** — removed from the launcher at P Apps Launcher v11.01 (PET-105) while Pete explores other ways of working with it. File and data unchanged; it hosts the embedded HTML Vault tab, so see the Vault note in the launcher v11.01 entry. See "Applications on hold".
